# dctx

> dctx turns any folder into the smallest correct context for a task, offline, with byte-stable output that prompt caches can reuse. dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts irrelevant text from selected tool answers. It does not save tokens by default; savings depend on a system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context. Extra calls can add tokens. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything.

Read the pack at https://www.dctx.internet.technology/llms-full.txt.

## Facts

### What dctx is

dctx is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Rust context engine for AI-assisted coding: one local binary that packs a project into one structured block, or answers bounded, byte-stable symbol queries (find, read, neighbors, skeleton) as CLI output or MCP tools.

What it is not:

- No RAG: no embeddings, no vector search, and the engine never calls a model.
- No network: pack, map, cache and mcp make no network calls; the release check counts socket calls under strace and fails on any.
- No telemetry, not even opt-out.
- No agent loop: dctx answers one command at a time; the agent or the human decides what to ask next.

### Version and download

- Current version: 1.3.1, released 2026-11-09 (tag `v1.3.1`): https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/releases/tag/v1.3.1
- Each release on GitHub ships prebuilt archives for Linux x64/ARM64, macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64 with a SHA256SUMS file.
- Verify a download: `sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS`
- Releases from 1.3.0 also ship keyless cosign signatures, CycloneDX SBOMs, build provenance and offline bundles; see [verification](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/VERIFYING.md).

### Modalities

- CLI (available): `dctx pack PATH` for one structured block (clipboard, file or stdout); `dctx map find|read|neighbors|skeleton|...` for bounded symbol answers. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/cli/
- MCP server (available): `dctx mcp PATH` over stdio for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex; `--profile lean` exposes only find and read. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/modalities/#mcp-server-convenient-tools-with-startup-context
- Task context (available): `dctx pack --for TEXT --budget N`: find, neighbors and read of the names in TEXT, cut to an estimated-token budget. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/map-mode/
- CI and prompt cache (available): Deterministic pack and map output; tree lines carry no timestamps by default, so the prefix stays stable across a touch. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/modalities/#ci--prompt-cache-prefix-stability
- Rust library (available from Git): The `dctx` facade crate as a tagged Git dependency; crates.io publication pending. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/modalities/#rust-library-embed-the-facade
- Desktop app (preview): A Tauri preview you build from source; a GPUI rebuild is planned. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/modalities/#desktop-app-tauri-preview-today
- Python, Node and Go wrappers (Node on npm; Python and Go from CI): Thin `dctx rpc` wrappers, built and tested in CI. Install Node with `npm install @tejl/dctx`, which includes pinned `@tejl/dctx-<platform>` optional dependencies; use CI artifacts for Python and Go. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/modalities/#python-node-and-go-wrappers

Two scopes, one binary:

- System binary: the `dctx` on PATH belongs to you and your agents, and you upgrade it. Interactive agents and MCP call this one.
- Project binary (Node from npm; Python and Go from CI): a binary installed by a project library lives inside that project (virtualenv, node_modules), pinned and managed by that package manager. Application code and CI call this one; a library never silently falls back to PATH.
- Same engine, different owner. `dctx doctor` lists every binary in reach; verify each against SHA256SUMS and its cosign signature.

### Before you start

> dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts irrelevant text from selected tool answers. It does not save tokens by default; savings depend on a system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context. Extra calls can add tokens. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything.

### Benchmarks

Baseline: grep plus reading files.

- Measured: 11 November 2026: 20 questions, a private 13-crate Rust workspace, claude-sonnet-5-5, dctx 1.3.0, three repeats per arm. Median total tokens [min, max]: grep plus reads (A) 14,904,014 [14,604,149, 15,622,381]; warm dctx CLI (B) 14,157,974 [11,221,908, 15,613,375]; fresh-cache dctx MCP (C), startup/indexing measured, 15,922,125 [15,513,198, 16,700,029]. B versus A: -5.01 %. On this corpus and model dctx did not save 25 % tokens; the pre-registered rule was not met. Official strict citation recall medians [min, max], A/B/C: 10.10 % [10.10, 20.73] / 14.46 % [8.36, 22.65] / 13.41 % [12.02, 66.72]. Diagnostic file-level recall medians: 53.77 % / 71.70 % / 76.42 %; diagnostic, not a replacement metric. The claim is accuracy and bounded context, not token savings: B and C named more required files at about equal (B) or higher (C) token cost. C cost +6.8 % tokens and +30 % wall time. dctx on its own does not save tokens by default. Savings come from a harness or agent system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context across long sessions over a large body of work, with complete control over every byte. There is no measured, citable savings figure for such a system yet. One corpus, one model, no significance claim; corpus and raw answers private and cannot be published; dctx 1.3.0 is not current HEAD. Under ~200 files, use grep. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/benchmarks/#grep-read
- Measured: Byte stability: the same query on unchanged code returns the same bytes; 33 of 33 text and JSON answers were byte-identical after unrelated edits (Linux only). https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/stability/
- Historical: The October and November in-house numbers (run 7: 140 of 140 task questions, cold index and warm latency) measure tool output only, as estimated stdout tokens and raw fact coverage without a model; they are not agent completion rates or session costs. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/benchmarks/
- Hypothesis: That a pack template changes model answer quality or cost is a hypothesis pending an A/B test; nothing on this site measures it. https://www.dctx.internet.technology/templates/

### Removed in 1.2.0

These existed before 1.2.0 and no longer work. A transcript that uses them describes an old version.

- `dctx PATH` (the implicit snapshot command, for example `dctx .`): use `dctx pack PATH`.
- the top-level snapshot flags `-d`/`--diff`, `-t`/`--tree` and `-r`/`--reset`: use `dctx pack PATH` with its filters.
- the project rule files `.legacyignore` and `.dctxomitcontent`: use `.gitignore` and `.dctxignore`.
- `dctx cache gc --legacy` and its export-selection flags: use `dctx cache gc`.

### How to verify a claim

- Test suite: `cargo test --workspace --locked --exclude dctx-desktop --exclude dctx-desktop-api` https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/TESTING.md
- CI: Every push and pull request runs the suite on Linux, macOS (ARM64 and x64) and Windows, on stable Rust and the minimum supported version 1.91. https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/actions
- No network calls: `scripts/release-check.sh --quick target/release/dctx-cli` https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/scripts/release-check.sh
- Byte stability: `python3 docs/research/stability-20261105/verify.py` https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/stability/
- Historical benchmark: `docs/research/bench-3way-20261030/run-3way.sh target/release/dctx-cli` https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/tree/main/docs/research/bench-3way-20261030
- Every output on this site: Recorded from the real binary by tools/website/capture.py; tools/website/check.py re-records and fails on drift. https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/tree/main/tools/website

### Docs

- [Documentation](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/): Specification, guides, benchmark reports and project policies for dctx, rendered from the repository.
- [Choose your path](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/start/): dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Pick the path that matches your work: one giant folder, many small projects, a library in your own tool, or a team rollout.
- [One giant folder](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/start/giant-folder/): You work inside one very large tree, for example a 200 GB monorepo, data or document folder. Setup, first command, what to expect and the pitfall to avoid.
- [Many smaller projects](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/start/many-projects/): You move between many small and medium repositories during the day. Setup, first command, what to expect and the pitfall to avoid.
- [Agent builder embedding a library](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/start/library/): You build an agent, editor or tool and want dctx inside it. Setup, first command, what to expect and the pitfall to avoid.
- [Team or organisation admin](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/start/team/): You roll dctx out to a team or a fleet of machines. Setup, first command, what to expect and the pitfall to avoid.
- [For AI evaluators](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/for-ai-evaluators/): What dctx is and is not, its version, modalities, benchmark status, removed commands and how to verify every claim.
- [Why dctx](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/why/): Why dctx exists, its philosophy, and why byte-identical output keeps the prompt cache hitting.
- [README](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/readme/): Installation, quick start, map mode, language tiers and the CLI reference.
- [What dctx is](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/start/): The claim and its limits, the advanced-user notice, choose your path, the safe path in ten minutes, responsibilities and the two scopes.
- [Choosing how to use dctx](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/modalities/): Clipboard, grep plus reads, long sessions, huge trees, MCP startup cost and CI.
- [Map mode guide](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/map-mode/): Every map verb with examples, budgets, ids and precision labels.
- [Agent snippet](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/agents/): The AGENTS.md section that tells coding agents to ask dctx first.
- [Plugins guide](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/plugins/): The plugin boundary, capabilities, consent and current limits.
- [Specification](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/spec/): The core belief, the five constraints, the ten RAG defect classes, policy and roadmap.
- [Privacy guarantees](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/privacy/): Ignore semantics and the full sensitive-file deny list.
- [Language coverage (ADR-018)](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/language-coverage/): The three tiers and how a language enters one.
- [Template contract (DTS v2)](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/templates-contract/): DTS source v2 and the compiled plan IR v1.
- [Templating engine (ADR-003)](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/templating/): Markers, ahead-of-time compilation, the two rendering passes and the data variables.
- [CLI exit codes](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/exit-codes/): The exit-code contract for map, pack, mcp and languages.
- [How dctx works](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/how-it-works/): Five short animations: two scopes of one binary, calls times context, prefix stability, the giant folder and the safe path for new users.

# Changelog

All notable changes to dctx are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). Dates are ISO 8601.

For current functionality and limitations, see the [README](README.md).
Historical entries describe the behavior and support scope of that release.
Current licensing: all first-party code and documentation, including the desktop app
and planned GPUI rebuild, are Apache-2.0, copyright Eris Margeta. Historical license
and distribution plans below do not describe the current release.

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- Repository-scale map-find latency fixtures (`--scale-files`) with settled mtimes, recorded shape, and informational Windows/Linux CI samples for 1,551 files.
- Opt-in `DCTX_TIMINGS=1` emits map-find phase microseconds as stderr JSON, with phase medians in the Windows CI latency report.
- Publish the first whole-session grep-versus-dctx benchmark: CLI median tokens -5.01 %, below the 25 % savings rule; both recall metrics and spread reported in [the study](docs/BENCHMARK-20261111.md).
- `dctx trace A B` returns bounded shortest directed call/reference paths, and
  `dctx impact SYMBOL` returns direct sites plus transitive callers grouped by
  file. Both support JSON, explicit depth/record/byte bounds, `--place`, `--also`,
  outside-index notices, MCP tools and engine RPC.

- `dctx agent-setup [--format claude|agents|plain]`: short, deterministic rules for
  choosing dctx or grep and using dctx from coding agents.
- Windows CI reports warm per-call `dctx map find` p50/p95 latency over 50 separate
  process invocations on a fixed fixture, with raw samples uploaded as an artifact.
  The measurement is informational and does not fail CI. First result (release
  build, GitHub-hosted windows-2022, stable): p50 10.2 ms, p95 11.3 ms.
- Map and context pages report eligible definitions outside the index with a
  relative path and an `--also` hint. A bounded local-import fallback respects
  ignore, omit and sensitive-file rules and refuses symlinks.
- Repeatable `--also DIR` on map verbs, pack and context joins read-only roots
  with root-labeled IDs and a cache identity covering the complete root set.

### Fixed

- Windows generation opening reuses guarded traversal directories and enumeration metadata, avoiding repeated ancestor opens per file while retaining identity, permission and racy-window checks.
- Python, Go and npm bindings expose `trace` and `impact` with CLI byte parity, including bounded/no-path and empty-impact results.
- Windows outside-index notices and `trace`/`impact` now normalize native separators and verbatim drive prefixes, keeping relative paths and `--also` hints slash-separated.
- Map query bounds errors name the offending option, its value, the user-facing
  verb (including `grep`) and its allowed range; usage errors still exit 2.
- Windows: a file briefly locked by another process (antivirus, indexer, editor) no longer fails the whole pack; dctx retries for up to ~0.3 s.

### Changed

- Measure shell versus MCP-default stdout sizes on 1,551 files; the [study](docs/research/bash-path-20261112.md) reports 260 calls, a negative default-size result, and exact shell bounds.
- MCP discovery uses compact descriptions and advertises text/limit defaults.
  Map, hubs, trace and impact have smaller default answer bounds; explicit
  limits still override them. A bounded `pack` tool returns task definitions,
  callers/imports and source in one call. Tool names and opt-in JSON remain
  compatible; byte budgets guard catalog and response size in tests. See the
  [payload study](docs/research/mcp-cost-20261112.md).

- Node wrapper is published as `@tejl/dctx` on npm; the unscoped name `dctx` was refused by the registry.

- Clarify npm stability and binary verification, and guard every npm package manifest against install hooks.
- Release version checks now cover the bundled git plugin, its fixtures and their digests.

## [1.3.1] - 2026-11-09

### Changed

- The Node wrapper is published as `@tejl/dctx`, with platform packages
  `@tejl/dctx-<platform>`. The registry refused the unscoped name `dctx`;
  use `npx @tejl/dctx`.

### Fixed

- Segment store: publishing a new generation no longer fails with `InvalidRequest(generation)`
  when garbage collection runs at the same time. Publication now excludes a collection's
  mark-through-unlink, so a collector can no longer hide the newest generation from a writer.

## [1.3.0] - 2026-11-09

Install from the GitHub release archives. The npm, crates.io and PyPI packages and
the Go module are built and tested in CI, but registry publication is still pending;
until it happens, the release archives are the install path.

### Added

- `dctx rpc`: a versioned, newline-delimited JSON engine protocol over stdin/stdout
  (protocol 1.0.0, schema in `docs/protocol/`). Every reply carries `engine_version`;
  operation output is exactly the CLI stdout bytes.
- `dctx context TARGET...`: minimal ranked context for a file, symbol name or stable
  node id, with chunk ids, `--budget`, `--json` and `--session ID --dedupe`.
  `pack --for TEXT --json` now returns the same JSON context page.
- `dctx doctor [--json] [--probe-project]`: lists the dctx binaries visible from the
  current folder with path, ownership scope, version, build commit, SHA-256 and cache
  sizes. It changes nothing and uses no network.
- MCP `--profile lean|three` and `--tools NAME,...` select a smaller tool set with
  compact descriptions (lean start-up tool definitions: 6,278 -> 1,637 bytes). See
  [docs/guides/MCP.md](docs/guides/MCP.md).
- Python, Node (npm) and Go client packages over `dctx rpc`, each with CLI byte-parity
  tests in CI. They are not published to a registry yet.
- Release supply chain: keyless cosign signatures, CycloneDX SBOMs, GitHub build
  provenance attestations, a reproducible Linux musl build check and offline
  (air-gap) bundles. See [docs/VERIFYING.md](docs/VERIFYING.md). CI runs `cargo audit`.
  SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md describe the security and support policy.
- Robustness tests and a fuzz smoke workflow in CI.
- `dctx pack --for` prints a warning on stderr when the text names no identifiers;
  the page is unchanged.
- `dctx pack --clipboard` supports `xsel` on Linux.
- Experimental `tools/catalog-bench` for huge-tree catalog measurements (not part of
  the CLI).

### Changed

- `dctx pack` prints its `pack bytes=… files=… retention=… version=V1` status line on
  stderr. stdout is exactly the page and ends in a newline; `pack --json` stdout is
  exactly one JSON document. Scripts that read the status line from stdout must read
  stderr instead.
- Indexes live in an engine `major.minor` subdirectory of the cache parent
  (`DCTX_CACHE_DIR` or the platform `dctx/v2` root). 1.3 builds its own index on first
  use; patch releases share it, and older unscoped cache data is ignored, not deleted.
- Faster warm path: one fused inventory walk with directory-relative stats, rule files
  validated by stamps and cheaper decoding (measured checkout 288 -> 94 ms, 4k-file
  tree 88 -> 32 ms). Timestamp-only changes reuse the index generation.
- Each place keeps its own warm index; targeted queries no longer admit the whole
  place first; capacity errors name the exact limit and the flag that changes it.
- Pack output streams with bounded memory and spools large pages. Pack history uses
  compact manifest caches.
- Language extraction audit with new goldens; the default parser id is now
  `dctx-structural/3`.
- `dctx pack --for` keeps bare short names such as `main` and `run`, and keeps the
  case of capitalized words. Exact-case names and non-test code rank first, so
  `--for Session` finds the `Session` types before test functions.
- `dctx cache`, `dctx template`, `dctx context` and a bare `dctx` follow the exit-code
  contract in [docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md](docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md): 2 for usage errors,
  3 for I/O errors (naming the path), each with a `hint:` line. RPC `cache_status`
  returns the same codes. `dctx context` with no TARGET exits 2.
- A bare `dctx` whose stdin or stdout is not a terminal prints short usage and exits 2
  instead of starting the interactive menu.
- `dctx pack --help` prints only the pack usage and flags.
- `dctx plugin …` and `dctx git` text output is plain text. Refusals go to stderr as
  `[no] Error:` with a `hint:` line; a missing consent names
  `dctx plugin enable <id> --approve`. JSON output and exit codes are unchanged.
- `dctx cache auto` text shows a UTC time next to `last_auto_clean_ms` and
  `next_due_ms`; JSON is unchanged.
- Docs and package READMEs no longer present `npx dctx`, `npm install`,
  `cargo install dctx-cli`, `pip install dctx` or `go get` as working install paths.
  The Python missing-engine message no longer suggests a PyPI install.
- Bundled SQLite is 3.54.1 (rusqlite 0.41).

### Removed

- `dctx plugin run` and `dctx git` JSON replies no longer repeat the
  `facade_spawns` and `facade_git_children` keys. The facade counters remain once in
  `--json` output and are gone from text output.
- The cwd-relative plugin root fallback used when HOME was unset (see Security).

### Fixed

- Pack headers show `ID="UNIQUE_ID"` with clean quotes in the file-access
  instructions, including stamped and tree-only output. This changes pack output bytes.
- Pack rendering preserves literal template syntax in file bodies and paths, including
  backslashes, for default, stamped and compiled templates. Variable substitution
  applies only to template structure; `pack --for` also preserves source CRLF bytes.
- The last `</FILE_CONTENT_END …>` marker of a pack page is no longer glued to the
  status line.
- `dctx pack --for` with no usable terms says so and suggests backticks, instead of
  reporting that no name matched the index. Its flag refusal now lists `--json`.
- `dctx map` call edges stay within the caller's language family: a Rust `.all(..)`
  no longer resolves to a Makefile target. A guessed method call such as
  `iter.map(..)` links to a project method only when the caller can see that method's
  type. Hubs, neighbors, path and `pack --for` lose these false edges.
- `dctx plugin search` and the other text-mode plugin commands no longer mix JSON
  fields or internal counters (`facade_git= spawns= git_children=`) into the output;
  `dctx git status` without consent no longer prints `git: ConsentRequired`.
- `dctx pack --clipboard` with no clipboard tool names the tools it tried and suggests
  `--output FILE`.
- A symlinked or non-regular `.gitignore` or `.dctxignore` inside the project is
  skipped with a warning instead of failing the command; rule-file errors no longer
  print the absolute project path.
- Cache policy saves no longer get stuck on a `policy.v1.tmp` left by a crash.
- `dctx plugin` and `dctx git` work when the plugin root sits below a symlinked
  directory (macOS `/var` and `/tmp`, a linked home) instead of failing with
  `Interrupted`; a symlinked plugin root itself and symlinks inside it stay refused.
- Windows: `dctx plugin enable`, `disable`, `install`, `remove` and `update` say that the
  plugin store is read-only on Windows (`ReadOnlyStore`) instead of failing with
  `Interrupted`, and consent hints there no longer offer only a command that cannot work.
- `dctx doctor` shows each binary's build commit (`commit:` in text, `"commit"` in
  JSON) and names an invalid argument.
- `dctx --help` lists `map export`; the `dctx map --help` examples map a file that has
  symbols.
- The Python wrapper raises `BinaryNotFoundError`, not `RuntimeError`, when no home
  directory is available (Windows without `USERPROFILE`/`LOCALAPPDATA`).
- Windows: durable file replacement, inode identity and racy-window directory stamps
  in map refresh. macOS: symlinked ancestors of the project, config and cache roots
  (such as `/var` and `/tmp`) are resolved at the boundary while in-tree symlinks stay
  refused; file names that APFS refuses are handled. Other cross-platform test and
  code fixes.
- README CLI reference, map-mode guide, modalities, start, testing and exit-code docs
  match the current binary and CI: all commands, 50 languages, neighbors depth 1..4,
  exact `--lines`, the global ignore file path, and that `.git/info/exclude` and
  `core.excludesFile` are not read.
- `tools/sync-version.sh` also syncs the Python, Go and npm package versions and the
  release links in the docs and package READMEs.

### Security

- Bundled SQLite upgraded to 3.54.1 (rusqlite 0.41, libsqlite3-sys 0.39.1) for
  RUSTSEC-2026-0459.
- Hardening across the engine and CLI, documented in
  [docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md](docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md).
- Pack and diff output entity-encode `&`, `<`, `>`, `"` and control or line-separator
  characters in file paths, so a file name cannot forge file boundary markers.
  Ordinary paths are unchanged and output stays byte-stable.
- `dctx doctor` no longer executes dctx binaries found in `./node_modules/.bin`,
  `$VIRTUAL_ENV` or relative PATH entries, which an untrusted checkout can plant; they
  are listed with path and SHA-256. `--probe-project` opts in.
- MCP tool arguments are passed after `--` and taken literally, so a flag-shaped id or
  query (for example `--place`) cannot change the place outside the server root. MCP
  never forwards `--place` or `--output`.
- `pack --output`, `map export --output` and `template build --output` never follow a
  symlink or write into a non-regular target; pack and template write a fresh sibling
  file and rename it into place.
- Clipboard tools are looked up only in absolute PATH entries, so `.` or empty entries
  cannot run a repository's own `xclip` or `wl-copy`.
- The source reader checks an entry's type before opening it and never opens device
  nodes, FIFOs or sockets (Unix opens use `O_NOCTTY`). `StdFs` metadata, listings and
  link reads no longer follow symlinked path components; Windows ancestor guards block
  directory replacement.
- The store adapter refuses symlinked, foreign-owned or group/other-writable store
  roots and creates store directories with mode 0700.
- The plugin root no longer falls back to a directory relative to the working
  directory when HOME is unset; plugin commands refuse unless HOME or
  `DCTX_PLUGIN_ROOT` is an absolute path.
- The Python wrapper loads its `dctx_binary_<platform>` engine package only from the
  install directory that holds `dctx`, never from the working directory or other
  `sys.path` entries.
- The Python, Node and Go package READMEs warn that operation arguments carry full CLI
  authority.
- The no-follow open flag used by `map export --output`, the map store and the desktop
  snapshot rules now comes from the platform instead of a hard-coded x86 value, so it
  also holds on Linux ARM64.
- The npm wrapper tarball built in CI no longer lists the unpublished `@dctx/cli-*`
  platform packages, so installing it never resolves those names from the public
  registry; error messages point to the release archive and `DCTX_BIN`.
- The website playground rate limit can no longer be bypassed with a forged
  `X-Forwarded-For` header. The website deploy builds without secrets and deploys only
  from `main` through a protected environment; the desktop release workflow is
  disabled until the desktop app ships, with pinned toolchains, a frozen lockfile and
  provenance attestations.

## [1.2.0] - 2026-11-07

### Added

- Prebuilt release archives for Linux x64/ARM64 (static musl), macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64, with SHA256SUMS.
- Packaging support for npm (`npx dctx`, platform packages under `@dctx/cli-*`) and crates.io (`cargo install dctx-cli`); registry publication is coming soon. Install the prebuilt GitHub release archives now.
- Cross-platform CI: every push and pull request runs the full test suite on Linux, macOS (ARM64 and x64)
  and Windows, on stable Rust and the minimum supported version. See [docs/TESTING.md](docs/TESTING.md).
- The website redeploys automatically from `main`.
- GitHub Sponsors: individuals can support dctx at <https://github.com/sponsors/Eris-Margeta>.

### Changed

- Minimum supported Rust version is now declared: 1.91.
- The source tree is formatted with `cargo fmt`; no behaviour change.

### Removed

- The two internal pre-1.0 project rule files. Project ignore inputs are
  `.gitignore` and `.dctxignore`; built-in and explicit/global omission rules remain.
- The implicit `dctx PATH` snapshot command and its top-level flags, including
  `-d`/`--diff`, `-t`/`--tree` and `-r`/`--reset`. Use `dctx pack PATH`.
  The TUI now uses explicit pack commands without the old registry, state or project exports.
- `dctx cache gc --legacy` and its export-selection flags. Cache collection uses the managed ledger.
- Legacy-named selection test paths; current pure selection and privacy coverage remains.

### Fixed

- Windows CLI test environments now map `APPDATA` to the fixture config directory and provide `LOCALAPPDATA` for cache/data; missing or empty Windows directory variables return clear errors.
- Rust parser subprocess startup failures now stop indexing with a clear error instead of silently degrading source spans.
- `pack --for` keeps each section in source order when its budget runs out and recognizes file targets such as `src/lib.rs`.
- `serve` (including `serve --mcp`) uses the stdio MCP server in the current directory, including fixture folders; `read` routes to `map read`.
- Budget-cut reads move trailing closing delimiters and separators into the continuation, preserving every source line.
- The release recipe checks the current root `CHANGELOG.md` path.

## [1.1.0] - 2026-11-06

Release **1.1.0** (`v1.1.0`; release candidate `v1.1.0-rc1` 2026-11-04). It folds in the 1.0.1 line, which was never released on its own.

### Since rc1 (docs, CI, tooling and SPDX licence headers only; no change to dctx output)

- **Docs**: byte stability re-measured on 2026-11-06 — 33/33 text and 33/33 JSON map answers identical
  after unrelated edits and over five runs (see docs/research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md);
  SPEC and README status texts updated, historical 0/63 kept.
- **Formal**: the plugin TLC gate accepts the newer TLC wording 'Temporal property X was violated.' /
  'Invariant X was violated.' (all 8 baselines, 59 mutants, 37 witnesses pass); host-specific
  tla2tools.jar paths removed; TLC trace files ignored.
- **Self-hosted CI** (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`): the job run step by step on a self-hosted Linux runner (16 cores) from a clean
  `git archive` of the commit; results and badge recorded in `docs/ci/RESULTS.md` — 2279 run, 2279 passed, 0 skipped.
- **Third-party npm licence inventory**: `scripts/npm_licenses.py` indexes every repository `package-lock.json` into
  `THIRD_PARTY_NPM.md`; `npm_licenses.py --check` runs in CI and fails on a disallowed licence or a stale report.

### Added

- **Perl** (`.pl`, `.pm`, `.t`, `.psgi`): `package A::B;` and `package A { .. }` as `type` symbols holding every later
  `sub` (named `A::B::name`) as `fn` symbols (`guess` confidence, full tier). POD is masked like a comment; call edges
  come from `name(..)`, bareword calls with an argument and `&name`, never after `->`, `sub` or a sigil.
- **Fortran** (`.f90`, `.f95`, `.f03`, `.f08`, `.f`, `.for`): `module`, derived `type` and named `interface` as `type`
  symbols; `program`, `function` and `subroutine` as `fn` symbols named `module::name` (`guess` confidence, full tier).
  Keywords are case-insensitive, `!` comments only, fixed-form column rules are not modelled; call edges skip
  intrinsic and control keywords that precede `(`.
- **Verilog/SystemVerilog** (`.v`, `.vh`, `.sv`, `.svh`): `module`, `macromodule`, `interface`, `package` and `class`
  declarations as `type` outline symbols and `function`/`task` declarations as `fn` symbols (`guess` confidence, full tier),
  with module-scope call edges and `<module> <instance> (` instantiation links resolved through the call index.
- **Prefix-stable `pack` output**: tree lines carry the `ID` only, with no `MOD:` and no `SIZE:`, so a
  bare `touch` leaves the page byte-identical and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix
  for prompt caches. `--tree-stamps=on|off` (default `off`) selects the built-in tree template; `on` reproduces the
  1.0.0 bytes. The desktop tree-only export keeps its digest line last, behind a stable lead line.
- **Stat stamps in the manifest**: a stamp pass runs before the digest, with a racy-timestamp guard; a
  touch-only change is decided by content. A gate replays 200 random edits against a cold rebuild.
- **Record and entry caps**: checked during the scan and set by `DCTX_MAX_RECORDS` and
  `DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES`; the cache is reclaimed on publish, evicts before refusing, and readers share one lock.
- **Open-source maintenance model**: `MAINTENANCE.md`, `TRADEMARK.md`, a DCO in
  `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `FUNDING.yml`; the desktop app is open source too.

### Changed

- **Id lookup** uses a sorted hash index instead of a linear node scan.
- Large source files were split into submodules by pure moves (400-line rule): `pack.rs`, `path.rs`, `reuse.rs`,
  `bound.rs`, `plugin.rs`, `yaml.rs` and others. No behaviour change.
- The version is **1.1.0** for every `crates/*` and `plugins/*` package; the desktop app stays on 0.11.0.

### Fixed

- A closed stdout pipe (`dctx pack | head`) exits 0 without a panic.

## [1.0.0] — 2026-10-31

The first v1 release, folded from the 0.26 development line. Every `crates/*` and
`plugins/*` package, `VERSION`, `project-meta.yaml` and the README badge are at **1.0.0**
(`tools/sync-version.sh --check` keeps them and their `Cargo.lock` entries together). The
desktop app keeps its own version line (0.11.0) and its own release workflow.

### Shipped surface
- **Map verbs**: `dctx map map | find | neighbors | explain | read | skeleton | grep | hubs | path | export`,
  with hard token budgets, stable ids, cursor paging and precision labels; call and import edges are lexical.
- **`dctx mcp`**: a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools.
- **`dctx pack`**: the whole project as one structured block to stdout, the clipboard or `--output`.
- **`dctx pack --for "<text>" --budget N`**: task context for an agent card: `map find` on the names the text mentions,
  then neighbors and read of the best hits, whole lines only, within N estimated tokens (ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7),
  default 3000). `tools/cardgen/context.sh` prepends it to a card; `docs/guides/AGENTS-SNIPPET.md` is the `AGENTS.md` section that tells agents to run it first;
  `tools/cardgen/dogfood.py` records before/after prompt tokens for the ten v1 cards.
- **`dctx languages`**: one registry with three tiers (full, outline, docs) that also renders the README table.
- **Privacy deny**: sensitive files (env files, keys, credentials, ...), `.git` at any depth and symlinks are
  never read or printed by `pack`, any map verb or `mcp`; there is no override flag. Detection is by file name only.
- **Determinism**: two fresh indexes give byte-identical answers, and an unrelated edit changes only `hubs`;
  `scripts/release-check.sh` gates both, and counts network syscalls under `strace -f` (must be zero).
- **`dctx --version`** prints `dctx 1.0.0 (<git sha>)`; the sha is embedded at build time, `unknown` without git.
- **README benchmark section** rendered from the committed run 7 JSON by `scripts/render_readme.py`;
  `just readme-check` fails when the README differs.

### Out of scope for v1
- Any network or cloud feature.
- macOS and Windows support claims (untested); Linux x86_64 is the only tested platform.
- Watch or incremental mode beyond re-indexing.
- Fortran and Verilog (both shipped in 1.1.0).
- Shell call edges.
- Embeddings and semantic search.
- LSP-grade type resolution.
- A stable plugin ABI and desktop API (unstable, not a v1 contract).
- Cross-repository queries.
- Publishing to crates.io or GitHub (a maintainer decision).

### Added
- **Call and import edges** in the map index: `dctx map neighbors --edge calls|imports`
  now answers who calls what, resolved by lexical scope, imports and module paths, with
  `name`/`guess` confidence; ambiguous references are dropped.
- **New map verbs**: `skeleton <file>` (declaration signatures, no bodies), `grep <literal>`
  (hits grouped by enclosing symbol), `hubs` (most-called symbols and per-directory counts),
  `path <FROM> <TO>` (shortest edge path) and `export --format json|mermaid` (the whole graph).
  `neighbors --depth` goes up to 4 (breadth-first, each node once).
- **`dctx mcp`**: a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools.
- **`dctx languages`** (`--json`, `--markdown`): every supported language with its tag, file names, tier
  (full: symbols and lexical call edges; outline: symbols only; docs: sections) and confidence, from one facade
  registry (`dctx::LANGUAGES`) that also feeds `--version --verbose` and the README table, which a test diffs.
- **A CLI exit-code contract** (`docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md`) for `map`, `pack`, `mcp`, `languages` and unknown
  commands: 0 ok, 1 no result (an id not in the index, a binary file target, nothing to pack), 2 usage, 3 index
  error. Every failure prints a `hint:` line. Previously every failure exited 1. A non-UTF-8 argument is now a
  usage error instead of a panic, an unknown flag is named as unknown, and `dctx map <verb> --help` prints a page
  with an `Example:` line for each map verb.
- **Outline symbols (`guess` confidence) for 25 more formats**: Scala, Dart, Zig, Solidity,
  Gleam, Groovy; Elixir, Lua, OCaml, R, Julia, Haskell; Terraform/HCL, SQL, shell, Makefile,
  Dockerfile, protobuf, Pascal, GraphQL; and headed sections for `.txt`, `.rst`, `.adoc`,
  `.org` and `.tex` documents.
- **A three-way benchmark against graphify and Trail-Code** (`docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md`)
  and the gap matrix behind it (`docs/GAP-MATRIX-20261030.md`).

- **dctx Desktop is free, forever** for individuals, teams and companies
  ([announcement](https://dctx.app/news/desktop-free-forever/)).
- **The dctx Context Management Specification** (`docs/SPEC.md`): prompt-processing
  efficiency as the core belief, the ten RAG defect classes and how dctx rules
  them out, the seven-layer organization policy, prefix-stable tiers and delta
  answers, the persistent index, the plugin boundary and the roadmap.
- **An isolated, reproducible benchmark against Trail-Code**
  (`docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/`): methodology, raw data, scripts and
  numbered findings.
- **Map mode** (`dctx map`): `map`, `find`, `neighbors`, `explain` and `read`
  with hard token budgets (up to 2,000 per answer), cursor paging, stable ids,
  explicit `moved`/`gone`/`ambiguous` outcomes and precision labels on every answer.
- First-party structural extractors for JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Python, Go,
  Java, C/C++, C#, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Markdown and JSON/TOML/YAML; Rust
  through `syn`.
- A verified map generation reused across CLI invocations.
- **Plugin host**: capability grants, consent, receipts, liveness by progress,
  signed distribution verified with Ed25519, and Linux confinement; the bundled
  **Git plugin** (`.gitignore` protection and consented staging).
- **Cache lifecycle**: time-based expiry, a system size cap and a bounded
  automatic cleaner (`dctx cache status | gc | purge | config | auto`).
- `dctx pack`: an explicit pack to stdout, the clipboard or `--output`, without
  leaving files in the project.
- The template system's v2 compiler (a sealed plan IR) and organization ceilings.
- `crates/dctx`: one library facade for the CLI, the desktop app and future
  bindings.
- A new website with changelog and news, and the dctx film
  (`presentation/video/`).

### Changed
- **Byte-stable map answers**: the text header is `# <place> <verb>` and JSON no longer
  carries `snapshot`, `generation` or `freshness.age_s`, so answers stay identical across
  unrelated edits (prompt-cache friendly). `--meta` restores the old fields.
- **`dctx pack` never prints env-shaped files** (`.env`, `.env.*`, `*.env`, `.envrc`); they
  stay in the tree by name with their content omitted.
- **Strict sensitive-file deny for every command**: besides env files, `*.pem`, `*.key`,
  `*.p12`, `*.pfx`, `*.jks`, `*.keystore`, SSH private keys (`id_rsa`, `id_ed25519`, ...),
  `credentials`, `credentials.json`, `secrets.yaml` (and other data extensions), `.npmrc`,
  `.netrc`, `.pypirc`, `.pgpass`, `.htpasswd` and `.git-credentials` are never read or printed
  by `pack`, any `dctx map` verb (by id or raw path, with or without `--in`) or `dctx mcp`.
  There is no override flag (see ADR-014).
- **`.git` is closed for good**: a `.git` segment at any depth is never listed or read by the map
  verbs and never read by `pack`, even when `.gitignore` or `.dctxignore` says `!.git/`.
- **No symlink escapes**: `FsSource` opens files with `O_NOFOLLOW`, requires a regular file
  handle, and refuses symlinked directories, so a symlink swapped in after the stat cannot leak
  bytes from outside the root.
- `DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` (ignore files are not applied) is now documented in ADR-014; the
  sensitive-file deny, the `.git` guard and the symlink rules still apply when it is set.
- **Total-source ceiling raised from 64 MiB to 1 GiB**; `DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES` overrides it.
- The core never reads `.git/`, never spawns `git` and never uses VCS object ids;
  content identity is dctx's own SHA-256 (`crates/dctx-hash`).
- Repository ignore rules are applied before any read on the map path, and
  `--lines A-B` returns exact line ranges.
- Everything in the repository is licensed under Apache-2.0.

### Fixed
- Node spans resolve from one newline index per file instead of rescanning the
  source for every symbol (cold `find` on a 3,000-file repository: 141 s -> about 6 s).
- Queries share one generation instead of cloning it (peak memory down by about
  30 % on the same repository).
- One hostile file no longer fails every map verb for the whole repository: a Rust
  file that is not UTF-8 is indexed as a module with no symbols (like every other
  language), and a file name the confined path cannot carry (a backslash) is skipped
  and marks the snapshot `partial`, as `pack` already did.

### Known issues
Measured in the benchmarks and scheduled in the specification's roadmap:
- No incremental indexing: the first query after an edit re-indexes, and each
  edit adds a full generation to the cache.
- Outline-tier formats carry symbols and `contains` edges only; heuristic families are
  labelled `guess`. `dctx languages` lists the tier and confidence of every format.
- The 70-question task protocol (run 7: 140/140) was designed by the dctx team; an
  independently selected protocol (v1 card 6) is pending.

## [0.25.0] — 2026-05-29

The last release of the first Rust generation, with **zero third-party
dependencies** in the core and the CLI.

### Added
- Snapshot, diff and tree modes; clipboard output; an interactive TUI.
- Filters by extension, size, content and visibility; binary detection.
- Ahead-of-time compiled output templates.
- The privacy guarantee: ignored files are never read, not even in debug mode;
  omit rules list a file without reading its content.
- The desktop app (Tauri) on the shared core.

## [0.11.0] — 2026-01-26

### Added
- A redesigned desktop interface with light and dark modes.
- A sequential, fail-fast CI pipeline.

## [0.10.0] — 2026-01-25

### Added
- Advanced CLI filters and their documentation.

## [0.1.0] — 2026-01-08

### Added
- The Rust rewrite of `dircontxt` begins.

## dircontxt [1.0.0] — 2025-11-15

The original tool, written in pure C (`legacy-c/`).

### Added
- One LLM-ready `.llmcontext.txt` snapshot with a manifest and unique ids for
  every file and directory, plus a binary state file.
- Automatic versioning with diffs that carry only the changed files.
- A three-tier ignore system (built-in defaults, a global ignore file and a
  per-project `.dircontxtignore`) and a global configuration file.

# Contributing to dctx

Read the [specification](docs/SPEC.md), [crate map](docs/CRATE-MAP.md) and
[Code of Conduct](CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) before making changes. Project contributions
are licensed under [Apache-2.0](LICENSE), consistent with [NOTICE](NOTICE).

## Bugs, ideas and questions

Search existing [issues](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/issues) before opening
one. Use the bug or feature template and keep reproductions small. Include the
commit or version, OS/architecture, build features, exact command, expected result
and actual result. Redact source code, paths, credentials and generated context
that you do not have permission to share.

Report suspected vulnerabilities privately using [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md),
rather than in an issue or pull request. For other questions, open an issue with
what you tried and the relevant documentation link.

## CLI development setup

CI tests use `DCTX_CI_RUST` from `tools/release/toolchain.env`; bump it intentionally each Rust release.

Use a recent stable Rust toolchain with Cargo; the workspace includes Rust 2024
crates. Clone the repository and run commands from its root:

```zsh
git clone https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx
cd dctx
cargo build --locked -p dctx-cli
cargo run --locked -p dctx-cli -- --help
```

Cargo builds **`dctx-cli`**, while help text calls the tool **`dctx`**. See
[installation](README.md#installation) for aliases and install choices.

Keep changes focused on the relevant crates and preserve unrelated work. The
[`dctx` facade](crates/dctx/) serves the CLI and the desktop API; pure engine
crates should not acquire filesystem, network or process effects. The
[plugin guide](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md) describes effect boundaries and current
runtime limitations.

## Validation

Start with the CLI and facade checks (some tests validate documentation):

```sh
cargo test -p dctx-cli -p dctx --locked
```

For documentation changes, install the Python dependencies using
[the website setup](tools/website/README.md), then run
`tools/website/.venv/bin/python tools/check-markdown-links.py`. It checks local
paths and heading anchors across public Markdown, including HTML and reference links.
[Testing](docs/TESTING.md) documents the full Linux/macOS/Windows matrix and
local commands. The current [CI workflow](.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs workspace
tests on stable Rust and MSRV, plus formatting, Clippy, Rust documentation,
licence, website and release checks. Run `cargo fmt --all -- --check` and document
public APIs. Follow [Rust house style](docs/STYLE.md) for the plugin boundaries.

When editing website source documents, regenerate `website/` and check it using
[the website instructions](tools/website/README.md). Before committing, use
`check.py --working-tree` to compare your regenerated files with an independent
build; CI compares committed output. Capture CLI examples only if output changed.

Desktop changes need their platform prerequisites and separate validation; see
[the desktop guide](apps/dctx-desktop/README.md). The root `just ci` recipe also
invokes desktop setup and is broader than the main CI jobs.

## Developer Certificate of Origin

Contributions use the [Developer Certificate of Origin](https://developercertificate.org)
(DCO) instead of a contributor license agreement. Sign off each commit to certify that
you wrote the change, or otherwise have the right to submit it under Apache-2.0:

```zsh
git commit -s
```

The `-s` flag adds a `Signed-off-by:` line with your name and email. Pull requests with
unsigned commits will be asked to amend them with `git commit --amend -s`, or to rebase
with `--signoff`.

## Pull requests

Create a focused branch from `main` and describe the problem, resulting behavior
and any compatibility or privacy impact. Add regression coverage for behavior
changes and update affected documentation. Check Markdown links and paths when
editing guides. Use clear commit messages, for example `fix(cli): reject empty
output paths`.

In the PR, list the commands you ran, their results, and any checks you could not
run. Include relevant OS/build features for platform-specific changes. Avoid
unrelated formatting, generated governance files, local caches, credentials and
private research artifacts. Maintainers may ask for a smaller change or additional
validation before merging. Pull requests, including forks, run on GitHub-hosted CI runners.

# dctx maintenance

dctx is open source under the Apache-2.0 license and free for any use, including commercial use. A maintenance agreement is how organisations that depend on dctx pay for its upkeep. Paying never changes the license and never closes a feature.

## What an agreement covers

- **Security fixes.** Response targets are counted from the moment a report is confirmed:
  - Critical: a fix or mitigation within 72 hours.
  - High: a fix within 7 days.
  - Medium: a fix in the next release.
- **Long-term support.** The 1.x line receives backported fixes for 18 months after 2.0 is released.
- **Priority on bug reports.** Reports from covered organisations are triaged first.
- **A say in the roadmap.** Covered organisations can propose priorities in a regular review. The maintainer keeps the final decision.
- **Advance notice of breaking changes.** You hear about a breaking change before it ships, with a migration note.
- **Invoice and written commitment.** You receive invoices and a signed maintenance commitment for procurement and vendor review.

Security reports still go through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md), whatever your tier.

## Tiers

| Tier | Who it is for | What you get |
|------|---------------|--------------|
| Supporter | Individuals and teams who want to fund dctx | Sponsorship and your logo in the README. No service commitments. |
| Team | One organisation that depends on dctx | Everything under "What an agreement covers", for one organisation. |
| Partner | Organisations that build products on dctx | Team, plus integration help and a named contact. |

Supporter sponsorship runs through [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/Eris-Margeta). Team and Partner agreements are arranged directly.

## Pricing and contact

Pricing on request: info@tejl.com

Write to that address with your organisation, the tier you want and a contact name.

## Guarantees

- Paying never changes the license. dctx stays Apache-2.0 for everyone.
- Paying never closes or paywalls a feature. Every feature stays in the open source project.
- The core (`pack`) and every modality stay open.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F003">

<p align="center">
  <a href="#start-and-choose-your-path">Choose your path</a> •
  <a href="#which-mode">Which mode?</a> •
  <a href="#the-core-belief-prompt-processing-efficiency">Philosophy</a> •

  <a href="https://www.dctx.internet.technology/">Website</a>
</p>

<p>
  <strong>dctx turns any folder into the smallest correct context for a task, offline, with byte-stable output that prompt caches can reuse.</strong><br>
  dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts irrelevant text from selected tool answers. It does not save tokens by default; savings depend on a system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context. Extra calls can add tokens. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything.
</p>

---

Under ~200 files, use grep. dctx pays off on large repos, multi-hop questions and many agents sharing one index.

Run `dctx agent-setup --format agents` (or `--format claude`) for short rules to paste into `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md`.

## Project status

**dctx is not yet stable and not enterprise-ready.** It has been in development since January 2026. Until version 2.0, expect breaking changes often. AI providers keep changing how they optimize context on their side; dctx adapts to those changes quickly, but not in real time. Stability is the goal of 2.0, and the project is working toward it: we see an ultimate solution to this problem, and we are denoising it.

dctx began as an internal tool that was never meant to be open-sourced, so parts of it are still messy. It was opened up because colleagues who rely on it needed it in the open, and development continues in public.

The founding promise is zero dependencies. Today dctx still has dependencies. The goal is to become the single best context management tool.

## Installation

**System binary — available now.** Download the archive for your OS and architecture
from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/releases/tag/v1.3.1),
compare its SHA-256 with the matching entry in `SHA256SUMS`, extract it, and put
`dctx` (`dctx.exe` on Windows) on `PATH`. Archives cover Linux x64/ARM64,
macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64. Releases after 1.2.0 also ship cosign signatures,
a CycloneDX SBOM, build provenance and offline bundles; see
[verification, provenance and offline installation](docs/VERIFYING.md).

```sh
dctx --version
```

**Node wrapper — available on npm from 1.3.1.** Run `npm install @tejl/dctx` to install the
[Node wrapper](packaging/npm/dctx/README.md) and its matching pinned
`@tejl/dctx-<platform>` native package, then `npx @tejl/dctx --version` to check it.
The [Python](packages/python/README.md) and [Go](packages/go/README.md) wrappers
over `dctx rpc` are built and tested in CI; use their CI artifacts. The
[Rust facade](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade) is available from
tagged Git. Use the release archives for the CLI.

Follow [the safe path in ten minutes](docs/START.md#safe-path-in-ten-minutes)
for one project, lean MCP setup and whole-session measurement.

## What the output looks like

These are real runs on the tiny [kiosk sample](tools/website/sample), captured by [capture.py](tools/website/capture.py) from the release binary. Commands run inside a copy named `kiosk`. For source builds, the executable is `dctx-cli` (or define a `dctx` alias).

### Pack a project

The header explains the format, the tree assigns IDs, and file blocks carry paths and line counts. The first 40 output lines follow; only the tail is omitted. `.env` is listed without its contents.

```text
$ dctx pack .

   - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file.
2. Content Access: To read a specific file:
   - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree.
   - Search for the marker: <FILE_CONTENT_START ID="UNIQUE_ID">
   - The content is between this marker and </FILE_CONTENT_END ID="UNIQUE_ID">
</INSTRUCTIONS>
<DIRECTORY_TREE>
[D]  (ID:ROOT)
```

### Find a symbol, then read it

Pass the exact ID from `find` to `read` to get its metadata and verified source bytes:

```text
$ dctx map find greet
# kiosk find
s:src/util.rs#greet	fn	L2-4
s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting	fn	L10-12
```

```text
$ dctx map read 's:src/util.rs#greet'
# kiosk read
s:src/util.rs#greet	fn	src/util.rs
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}
```

For structured consumption, `--json` puts the same source bytes in `source_utf8` (one JSON line, shown verbatim):

```text
$ dctx map read 's:src/util.rs#greet' --json
{"v":2,"place":"kiosk","verb":"read","freshness":{"mode":"strict","state":"verified"},"precision":{"coverage":"syntax","completion":"complete","parser":"dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9"},"records":[{"id":"s:src/util.rs#greet","kind":"fn","path":"src/util.rs","lines":[2,4],"summary":"The greeting shown on the kiosk screen.","summary_source":"doc","signature":null,"span":[44,126],"source_utf8":"pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {\n    format!(\"Hello, {}!\", title_case(name))\n}","edge":null,"direction":null,"target":null,"confidence":null}],"more":0,"next":null}
```

### Pack for a task

`--for` uses the task terms to select find results, neighbors and source reads. `--budget 800` bounds estimated output tokens, not scan size; the footer reports usage and dropped records.

```text
$ dctx pack . --for 'greet store' --budget 800
# dctx pack --for budget=800 terms=2
## find greet
s:src/util.rs#greet	fn	L2-4
s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting	fn	L10-12
## find store
s:src/store.rs#Order	struct	L4-8
s:src/store.rs#checksum	fn	L22-24
s:src/store.rs#encode	fn	L17-19
## neighbors s:src/util.rs#greet
calls:in:s:src/main.rs#main	fn	src/main.rs	L7
calls:out:s:src/util.rs#title_case	fn	src/util.rs
contains:in:m:src/util.rs	module	src/util.rs
## neighbors s:src/store.rs#Order
contains:in:m:src/store.rs	module	src/store.rs
## read s:src/util.rs#greet
s:src/util.rs#greet	fn	src/util.rs
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}
## read s:src/store.rs#Order
s:src/store.rs#Order	struct	src/store.rs
pub struct Order {
    pub id: u32,
    pub item: String,
    pub qty: u32,
}
# end body_tokens=223 budget=800 dropped=0
```
<!-- output:end -->

## Which mode?

- [CLI and one-off chat](docs/MODALITIES.md#human-one-off-pack-to-clipboard): pack selected source for a prompt or use the interactive terminal.
- [Agents, short tasks](docs/MODALITIES.md#short-agent-task-grep-can-be-enough): compare with grep plus narrow file reads first.
- [Agents, long sessions and huge trees](docs/MODALITIES.md#huge-trees-scope-before-indexing): scope the root, find symbols and read exact source.
- [MCP](docs/guides/MCP.md): use the lean profile to start; ACP is planned.
- [Libraries](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade): embed the Rust facade today; install the [Node wrapper](packaging/npm/dctx/README.md) with `npm install @tejl/dctx`, or use CI artifacts for the Python and Go wrappers.
- [CI and prompt caching](docs/MODALITIES.md#ci--prompt-cache-prefix-stability): pin inputs and measure byte stability and provider cache behavior.
- [Desktop](docs/MODALITIES.md#desktop-app-tauri-preview-today): build the Tauri 0.11 preview; the GPUI rebuild is planned.

## Measured, in the open

<!-- bench:begin -->
<!-- Generated by scripts/render_readme.py. Whole-session results: docs/BENCHMARK-20261111.md; historical timing: docs/research/bench-3way-20261030/results/run7-53f8b6b/aggregate.json. -->

The baseline is **grep plus reading files**.

The [11 November whole-session benchmark](docs/BENCHMARK-20261111.md) measured 20 questions on a private 13-crate Rust workspace with `claude-sonnet-5-5`, dctx 1.3.0 and three repeats per arm. Median total tokens [min, max]: grep plus reads 14,904,014 [14,604,149, 15,622,381]; dctx CLI (warm index) 14,157,974 [11,221,908, 15,613,375]; dctx MCP (fresh cache, startup/indexing measured) 15,922,125 [15,513,198, 16,700,029].

**On this corpus and model dctx did not save 25 % tokens.** CLI median tokens were -5.01 % versus grep; the pre-registered success rule was not met. MCP cost +6.8 % tokens and +30 % wall time. The claim is **accuracy and bounded context**, not token savings: CLI and MCP named more required files at about equal or higher token cost.

dctx on its own does not save tokens by default. Savings come from a harness or agent system that reuses byte-identical, prefix-stable context across long sessions over a large body of work. It behaves like an advanced caching mechanism, with complete control over every byte of context. There is no measured, citable savings figure for such a system yet. [Why this matters](docs/WHY-DCTX.md#savings-belong-to-the-system).

Official strict citation recall medians [min, max]: grep 10.10 % [10.10, 20.73], CLI 14.46 % [8.36, 22.65], MCP 13.41 % [12.02, 66.72]. Diagnostic file-level recall medians: 53.77 %, 71.70 %, 76.42 %, respectively; this does not replace strict recall. One corpus, one model, three repeats; no significance claim. Corpus and raw answers are private and cannot be published; dctx 1.3.0 is not current HEAD. **Under ~200 files, use grep.**

Historical cold indexing of six benchmark corpora took dctx 0.13–1.20 s on one Linux x86_64 runner. This measures CLI wall time, not agent completion time or session cost.

[Choosing how to use dctx](docs/MODALITIES.md) covers scoping and MCP startup overhead. [Measurement evidence](docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md) describes what was measured (tool-output bytes and estimated tokens); other-tool protocols are retained only as secondary historical notes.
<!-- bench:end -->

## Start and choose your path

[What dctx is](docs/START.md), [four user paths](docs/START.md#choose-your-path),
[responsibilities](docs/START.md#responsibilities), and
[two scopes, one binary](docs/START.md#two-scopes-one-binary) explain setup and
ownership. The [documentation index](docs/README.md) groups modalities, scopes,
engine behavior, reference material, trust and evaluator evidence.

“Smallest correct context” is the goal: selection is lexical and bounded, not a
proof of task completeness or a mathematical minimum. Large folders need scoped
roots; budgets bound answers, not scans. Provider cache hits and whole-session
savings must be measured. See [current limits](docs/MODALITIES.md) and the
[specification and roadmap](docs/SPEC.md).

## The core belief: prompt-processing efficiency

Send fewer relevant bytes, keep their order stable, and verify exact source.
dctx does not use embeddings; it selects lexical symbols and document sections.

- **Bounded**: map answers use estimated token budgets and whole records.
- **Deterministic**: identical source snapshots and requests give identical bytes.

Read the [philosophy](docs/WHY-DCTX.md) and its
[testable constraints](docs/SPEC.md#2-the-core-belief-prompt-processing-efficiency).

## Quick Start

Try a tiny project (POSIX shell; on Windows use Git Bash):

```sh
mkdir dctx-demo
cd dctx-demo
printf 'def hello(name):\n    return f"Hello, {name}!"\n' > hello.py
dctx map skeleton hello.py
```

Use the [safe path](docs/START.md#safe-path-in-ten-minutes) or the
[runnable pack and map example](examples/README.md). For repeated agent work,
see [Map mode: context for agents](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md) and the
[MCP client guide](docs/guides/MCP.md).

## Map mode: context for agents

From this repository's root:

```zsh
dctx map find "Session"
```

Read exact IDs from the result with `dctx map read 'ID' --json`.
See the [map guide](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md) for commands, budgets and limits.

## From source

Requires Rust 1.91 or newer.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx
cd dctx
cargo build --locked --release -p dctx-cli
./target/release/dctx-cli --version
alias dctx="$PWD/target/release/dctx-cli"
```

Cargo builds `dctx-cli` (`dctx-cli.exe` on Windows); release archives supply
`dctx`. For a local source installation, use
`cargo install --locked --path crates/dctx-cli` and `alias dctx=dctx-cli`.
On Windows, invoke the executable directly or create a PowerShell alias.
See [CI coverage and desktop exclusions](docs/TESTING.md).

## Use as a library

The public Rust entry point is the [`dctx` facade](crates/dctx), available from
Git now; **crates.io publication is pending**.

```toml
[dependencies]
dctx = { git = "https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx", tag = "v1.3.1" }
```

This example is generated from the [workspace doctest](examples/library/README.md):

<!-- library:begin -->
```rust
use dctx::{memory::{CancelFlag, FixedClock, MemorySource}, *};
let mut source = MemorySource::new();
source.insert_file("hello.rs", b"pub fn hello() {}\n", 0)?;
let mut session = Session::builder(source).clock(FixedClock(Timestamp(0)))
    .cancellation(std::sync::Arc::new(CancelFlag::new())).ceiling(HostCeiling::base())
    .selection(SelectionPolicy::from_texts(&RuleTexts::default())).grants(HostGrants::PermitAll)
    .storage(StoragePolicy::Ephemeral { max_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }).place("demo").view("pack").build()?;
let mut output = VecSink::new();
session.pack(&PackRequest::new(), &mut output)?;
println!("{}", std::str::from_utf8(output.as_bytes())?);
```
<!-- library:end -->

The host supplies selection rules and storage policy; `FsSource` does not
load `.gitignore` automatically. Read the
[library integration boundary](docs/MODALITIES.md#rust-library-embed-the-facade)
before embedding it. Python, Node and Go wrappers over `dctx rpc` live in
[packages/python](packages/python/README.md), [packaging/npm](packaging/npm/dctx/README.md)
and [packages/go](packages/go/README.md); they are built and tested in CI.
Install the Node wrapper with `npm install @tejl/dctx`; use CI artifacts for Python and Go.

## CLI Reference

```
Usage: dctx <COMMAND> [OPTIONS]
       dctx pack [PATH] [--output PATH] [--clipboard] [--json]
       dctx pack [PATH] --for <TEXT> [--budget TOKENS]
       dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read|skeleton|grep|hubs|path> [--json]
       dctx context TARGET [--place PATH] [--budget N] [--json] [--session ID --dedupe]
       dctx rpc
       dctx mcp [PATH]
       dctx serve [--mcp] [PATH]
       dctx read <TARGET> [OPTIONS]
       dctx languages [--json|--markdown]
       dctx doctor [--json]
       dctx cache status [--json] [--root PATH]
       dctx cache gc [--dry-run] [--root PATH] [--max-bytes N]
       dctx cache purge --root PATH [--dry-run] [--yes]
       dctx cache purge --all [--dry-run] [--yes]
       dctx cache config [auto on|off] [--max-bytes N] [--ttl-days N]
       dctx cache auto [--json]
       dctx template build <PATH> [--output PATH]
       dctx template list [--dir PATH]
       dctx plugin search|install|list|info|enable|disable|remove|update|verify
       dctx git <status|protect>

Pack filters:
  --ext <extensions>    Only files with these extensions (comma-separated)
  --binary              Include binary files (omitted by default)
  --empty               Only 0-byte files
  --non-empty           Only files with content
  --large <MB>          Only files larger than this many megabytes
  --small <MB>          Only files smaller than this many megabytes
  --hidden              Only hidden files and directories
  --debug-ignored       List ignored directories without reading them
  --include <pattern>   Only files matching this ignore-rule glob (repeatable)
  --exclude <pattern>   Drop files matching this ignore-rule glob (repeatable)
  --output, -o <path>   Write the page to one file
  --clipboard, -c       Copy the page to the clipboard
  --json                Summary report; with --for, the facade JSON context page
  --tree-stamps=on|off  MOD: timestamp on tree lines (default off; on = the 1.0.0 text)
Task context (agent cards):
  --for <text>          Map find on the names in <text>, then neighbors and read of the best hits
  --budget <tokens>     With --for: estimated-token cap, 100..100000 (default 3000)
```

- `dctx context` returns ranked context for a file, symbol name or stable node id;
  repeated targets in one call share a delivery session.
- `dctx rpc` serves the versioned engine protocol used by the language wrappers
  ([protocol](docs/protocol/README.md)); send `hello` first.
- `dctx mcp` and `dctx serve [--mcp]` serve the map verbs as MCP tools over stdio;
  `dctx read` is `dctx map read`. `dctx map export` writes the whole graph as JSON or Mermaid.
- `dctx languages` lists every supported language and its tier.
- `dctx doctor` lists visible dctx binaries, their scopes, SHA-256 checksums and
  cache sizes, without network access or cache changes.

Run `dctx --help`, `dctx pack --help` and `dctx map --help` for the complete
reference and `dctx --version --verbose` for feature and precision limits.


See [map commands and limits](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md),
[MCP profiles](docs/guides/MCP.md), [exit codes](docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md),
[templates](docs/design/contracts/DTS-v2.md), and [plugins](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md).
Native plugin launch is currently refused by the product host; consent alone
does not enable it. Organization policy and `dctx policy explain` are planned.

### Language tiers


`dctx languages` prints this table (`--json` for tools, `--markdown` for this block) from the one registry that also drives `dctx --version --verbose`; a test fails when the block below differs from it.

- **full**: symbols and call edges. Call edges are lexical, not type-resolved: they come from names, scopes and imports, never from a type checker, and ambiguous references are dropped.
- **outline**: symbols only; no call edges are promised. Shell function bodies can yield same-file call guesses, but v1 does not promise shell call edges.
- **docs**: headed sections.
- **Confidence**: `guess` marks the heuristic outline families, and every record from those files carries confidence `guess`; `structural` means a dedicated lexer or deterministic document rules.

<details><summary>Full language table</summary>

## Security & Privacy

Pack, map and MCP run locally and have **no telemetry**, **call no model** and
**make no network calls**. Selection happens before any byte is read, hashed,
parsed or cached, and is checked again before output leaves the engine.

| Rule file | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `.gitignore`, `.dctxignore`, global ignore file | Excluded from normal selection; `--debug-ignored` shows ignored path metadata without reading content |

The global ignore file is `<config dir>/dctx/ignore`: `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore`
or `~/.config/dctx/ignore` on Linux and macOS, `%APPDATA%\dctx\ignore` on Windows.
dctx does not read Git metadata, so `.git/info/exclude` and Git's
`core.excludesFile` are **not** applied: copy those patterns into `.dctxignore` or
the global ignore file when they must keep files out of a pack.

`DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1` skips those ignore texts, so leave it unset when relying
on them. Built-in sensitive-file and `.git` exclusions still apply.

Sensitive files such as `.env`, private keys and credentials are omitted from
content reads even with ignore negations; pack may list their names.
`.git` at any depth is never listed or read by map, and is never read by pack.
Symlinks are never followed; final-component file opens use `O_NOFOLLOW`.
dctx decides by file name only: a secret pasted into an ordinary source file
is not detected. Inspect context before sharing it.
The [privacy contract and deny list](docs/ADR-014-Privacy-Guarantees-and-Ignore-Semantics.md)
and [map privacy guide](docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md#index-cache-and-privacy) explain
the boundary. Report vulnerabilities privately through [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).

The [release check](scripts/release-check.sh) tests socket activity under
`strace -f` and reports SKIP where tracing cannot run. Plugin network and
organization policy designs in the spec include planned features;
see [current plugin limits](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md#what-is-not-yet-available).

## Open source and maintenance

dctx and its desktop app are [Apache-2.0](LICENSE), copyright Eris Margeta.
Every modality stays open. [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/Eris-Margeta)
and [maintenance agreements](MAINTENANCE.md) fund upkeep without changing the
license. See [trademark policy](TRADEMARK.md), [NOTICE](NOTICE),
[Rust dependencies](THIRD_PARTY.md) and [npm dependencies](THIRD_PARTY_NPM.md).

## Where it comes from

dctx started in 2025 as `dircontxt` in C and was rewritten in Rust in 2026.
The [changelog](CHANGELOG.md) and [`legacy-c/`](legacy-c/) preserve that history.

# Releasing dctx

The current CLI packaging, registry publication, website deployment, secret setup
and rollback runbook is [docs/RELEASING.md](docs/RELEASING.md).

The desktop app retains its separate `desktop-v*` release workflow.

## Publication gate

Before any future production/public release, complete the required production
security review and full relevant audit for the exact candidate
revision and configuration, including independent review, validators and required
sandbox/runtime evidence. The focused DCX-03 static sweep and ordinary CI do not
satisfy this prerequisite. Keep findings, residual risks and coverage limits private.

Follow the owner policy: select an explicit
`<project-root>/.private/security-audits/<release-id>/run-<N>`
evidence directory, verify the entire tree is ignored before writing in a Git
project, and use owner-only permissions (exclude it from staging/export for a
non-Git project). Use the separate overlay instead of the vendor default path.
Any unresolved gate blocker needs explicit informed owner disposition tied to the
exact release. A gate pass is not a claim of complete security.

The owner must authorize the production tag/publication and deployment.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F005">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F006" PATH="SECURITY.md" LINES="76">
<!-- SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0 -->
<!-- SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2026 Eris Margeta -->
# Security Policy

## Supported versions

The current major release receives bug fixes and security fixes in its latest
release. When a new major is released, the previous major receives security fixes
for **six months after the new major's release date**, then reaches end of support.
Older majors receive no fixes. Upgrade to the latest patch within a supported
major before checking whether an issue is resolved. We publish fixes in new patch
releases; we do not promise a separate patch for every historical minor version.
This public policy has no LTS commitment beyond that six-month transition. Include the exact
version or commit and build features so maintainers can assess affected versions.

## Reporting a vulnerability

**Do not disclose vulnerabilities in public issues or pull requests.** Use
[GitHub private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/security/advisories/new)
or email [info@tejl.com](mailto:info@tejl.com) with a subject beginning
`[dctx security]`. If GitHub's private reporting form is unavailable, use email.
Maintainers must enable private vulnerability reporting in repository security
settings; that GitHub setting is separate from this policy file.

Include, where possible:

- Affected version or commit, OS/architecture and build features.
- The affected component and potential impact (for example ignored-file content
  disclosure, untrusted plugin execution, or signature verification bypass).
- Exact reproduction steps and a minimal synthetic fixture or proof of concept.
- Expected and actual results, with sanitized diagnostics.
- Whether the issue has been shared elsewhere, and a preferred contact method.
- A name or alias for credit, or a request to remain anonymous.

Never send private keys, tokens, production data or a generated context export
containing confidential code. Use synthetic examples and redact sensitive values.
Test only systems and data you own or have explicit permission to assess.

## What counts as a vulnerability

dctx is an offline tool, but untrusted repositories, files, archives and plugin
inputs still cross security boundaries. Report issues such as:

- Disclosure of ignored, excluded or secret-file contents, including through
  generated context, caches, diagnostics or plugin access.
- Arbitrary code execution, sandbox or capability bypass, unsafe plugin execution,
  or command injection caused by processing untrusted input.
- Path traversal, symlink escapes, unintended file modification or unsafe archive
  extraction outside an authorized destination.
- Signature, checksum, provenance or update verification bypass; compromised
  release artifacts or dependencies affecting supported builds.
- A reproducible resource-exhaustion attack from a small malicious input that
  defeats documented bounds and makes the tool unusable.

Ordinary output mistakes, unsupported language coverage, feature requests and
performance issues without a security boundary impact belong in public issues.
Use private reporting when unsure. Offline operation does not make confidential
local data or the release supply chain out of scope.

## Handling and disclosure

We acknowledge private vulnerability reports **within 7 days**. We investigate
impact, identify affected supported versions and coordinate a fix or mitigation
and public disclosure with the reporter. Remediation timing depends on severity
and available maintainers; the acknowledgment window is not a promised fix deadline.
If acknowledgment has not arrived within 7 days, follow up through the other
private channel. Credit is subject to the reporter's consent.

We will not take legal action against individuals who discover and report
security vulnerabilities in good faith and in accordance with this policy.

Please coordinate public disclosure so users can receive a fix or mitigation.
For architectural boundaries and current implementation limits, see the
[README](README.md#security--privacy) and [plugin guide](docs/guides/PLUGINS.md).
Those descriptions are not a security certification.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F006">

# dctx trademark policy

The "dctx" name and logo are trademarks of Eris Margeta. The Apache-2.0 license covers the code only, not these marks.

## Forks and redistribution

Forks and redistribution of dctx are welcome under Apache-2.0. Keep the LICENSE and NOTICE files, and state clearly what you changed.

## What needs permission

- Calling a modified build, fork or product "dctx", or any name that suggests it is the official dctx.
- Using the dctx logo on a modified build, fork, product, website or merchandise.

Name a modified build something else, for example "XYZ, based on dctx". Ask for permission if you want to use the logo.

## What is always fine

- Unmodified official builds of dctx, redistributed as they are.
- Descriptive use of the name, such as "works with dctx", "a dctx plugin" or "built on dctx".

To ask for permission, write to info@tejl.com.
