Choose your path Agent builder embedding a library
You build an agent, editor or tool and want dctx inside it.
you get Stable ids and the exact source bytes inside your own app, from the same engine as the CLI. modality Project library with its own pinned binary. Install the Node wrapper with npm install @tejl/dctx ; use CI artifacts for Python and Go, embed the Rust facade from a tagged Git dependency, or run a pinned CLI binary and read its --json output. version dctx 1.3.1
Setup Pin one version in your project, for example the Rust facade: dctx = { git = "https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx", tag = "v1.3.1" } . Pass your own ignore rules: the library does not load .gitignore by itself; the host supplies selection policy, storage limits and the clock. Move ids, not text: call find , keep the returned ids, call read with them.
First command shell Copy $ cargo test --locked -p dctx-library-example --doc
What to expect The ten-line library example compiles and runs against an in-memory source. With the CLI, --json answers carry the same records, and read puts the exact source in source_utf8 .
A real run on the kiosk sample project , recorded from the release binary by capture.py : ~/kiosk · dctx 1.3.1 $ dctx map read 's:src/util.rs#greet' --json { "v" : 2 , "place" : "kiosk" , "verb" : "read" , "freshness" : { "mode" : "strict" , "state" : "verified" }, "precision" : { "coverage" : "syntax" , "completion" : "complete" , "parser" : "dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9" }, "records" : [ { "id" : "s:src/util.rs#greet" , "kind" : "fn" , "path" : "src/util.rs" , "lines" : [ 2 , 4 ], "summary" : "The greeting shown on the kiosk screen." , "summary_source" : "doc" , "signature" : null , "span" : [ 44 , 126 ], "source_utf8" : "pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {\n format!(\"Hello, {}!\", title_case(name))\n}" , "edge" : null , "direction" : null , "target" : null , "confidence" : null } ], "more" : 0 , "next" : null } # exit 0 · 561 bytes · ~161 est. tokens
The pitfall Re-implementing engine logic: parsing or slicing pack text, recounting budgets, rebuilding ids. Treat answers as opaque pages and stable ids; if you need a different shape, ask the engine for --json .
Read next Rust library: embed the facade · Use as a library · Who is responsible for what

The safe path uses the lean MCP profile, dctx mcp --profile lean .

Choose your path Team or organisation admin
You roll dctx out to a team or a fleet of machines.
you get One verified, pinned version on every machine, with the same safety rules everywhere. modality System binary distributed through your own package channel, one pinned version everywhere. version dctx 1.3.1
Setup Download the release archives from GitHub Releases and verify them against SHA256SUMS and their cosign signatures; each release also ships an SBOM. Ship one pinned version through your own package manager, image or configuration tool. Ship shared ignore rules ( .dctxignore and a global ignore); the built-in deny for secrets, .git and symlinks always applies. Tighten the cache cap per machine if you need to: dctx cache config --max-bytes N can only lower it.
First command shell Copy $ dctx --version
What to expect One line with the version on every machine; dctx --version --verbose adds the feature list and precision and cache limits. Every machine should print the same line.
A real run on the kiosk sample project , recorded from the release binary by capture.py : ~/kiosk · dctx 1.3.1 $ dctx --version dctx 1.3.1 (<git sha>) # exit 0 · 23 bytes · ~7 est. tokens
The pitfall Mixing project and system versions without checking. Run dctx doctor to list every binary in reach, and check dctx --version on PATH and the version each project pins, as part of onboarding.

url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/for-ai-evaluators/
title: For AI evaluators
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/for-ai-evaluators/
---

For AI evaluators Facts and how to verify them
For people and models deciding what dctx is. Every line below comes from one file, tools/website/data/facts.json , plus the benchmark documents; llms-small.txt , llms.txt and llms-full.txt start with the same facts.
What dctx is, and is not dctx is an open-source (Apache-2.0) Rust context engine for AI-assisted coding: one local binary that packs a project into one structured block, or answers bounded, byte-stable symbol queries (find, read, neighbors, skeleton) as CLI output or MCP tools. No RAG: no embeddings, no vector search, and the engine never calls a model. No network: pack, map, cache and mcp make no network calls; the release check counts socket calls under strace and fails on any. No telemetry, not even opt-out. No agent loop: dctx answers one command at a time; the agent or the human decides what to ask next.
Current version dctx 1.3.1 , released 2026-11-09 (tag v1.3.1 ), Apache-2.0. Release on GitHub · Changelog
Each release on GitHub ships prebuilt archives for Linux x64/ARM64, macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64 with a SHA256SUMS file. Verify a download with sha256sum --check --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS . Releases from 1.3.0 also ship keyless cosign signatures, CycloneDX SBOMs, build provenance and offline bundles; see [verification](https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/VERIFYING.md).
Modalities CLI available : dctx pack PATH for one structured block (clipboard, file or stdout); dctx map find|read|neighbors|skeleton|... for bounded symbol answers. MCP server available : dctx mcp PATH over stdio for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex; --profile lean exposes only find and read. Task context available : dctx pack --for TEXT --budget N : find, neighbors and read of the names in TEXT, cut to an estimated-token budget. CI and prompt cache available : Deterministic pack and map output; tree lines carry no timestamps by default, so the prefix stays stable across a touch. Rust library available from Git : The dctx facade crate as a tagged Git dependency; crates.io publication pending. Desktop app preview : A Tauri preview you build from source; a GPUI rebuild is planned. Python, Node and Go wrappers Node on npm; Python and Go from CI : Thin dctx rpc wrappers, built and tested in CI. Install Node with npm install @tejl/dctx , which includes pinned @tejl/dctx-<platform> optional dependencies; use CI artifacts for Python and Go.
Two scopes, one binary System binary: the dctx on PATH belongs to you and your agents, and you upgrade it. Interactive agents and MCP call this one. Project binary (Node from npm; Python and Go from CI): a binary installed by a project library lives inside that project (virtualenv, node_modules), pinned and managed by that package manager. Application code and CI call this one; a library never silently falls back to PATH. Same engine, different owner. dctx doctor lists every binary in reach; verify each against SHA256SUMS and its cosign signature.
The notice This is the canonical wording, from What dctx is ( docs/START.md ) and the README; the home page and Choose your path carry it verbatim: dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts irrelevant text from selected tool answers. It does not save tokens by default; savings depend on a system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context. Extra calls can add tokens. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything. Status: Receipts are planned. The safe path uses the lean MCP profile, dctx mcp --profile lean .
Responsibilities Items marked planned or pending are not in dctx 1.3.x yet. Level dctx provides You are responsible for System binary Release archives with SHA256SUMS, cache caps; signed binary, doctor, journals and receipts (planned) Choosing roots, the ignore rules (a policy file is planned), keeping one version on PATH Project library Pinned vendored binary, protocol client, same bytes as CLI (Node on npm; Python and Go from CI; Rust facade from Git) Pinning the version, exclusions in the project policy, not re-implementing engine logic MCP and ACP agent setup Lean profile, tested client configs, measured start-up cost (MCP today; ACP planned) Turning off the host's own file tools, picking a profile, session ids and reading receipts (both planned) CI and cache Byte-stable pack, deterministic exit codes; prefix tiers (planned) Pinning the binary, caching the index between runs, treating pack drift as a signal not noise
Benchmark status Baseline: grep plus reading files . measured 11 November 2026: 20 questions, a private 13-crate Rust workspace, claude-sonnet-5-5, dctx 1.3.0, three repeats per arm. Median total tokens [min, max]: grep plus reads (A) 14,904,014 [14,604,149, 15,622,381]; warm dctx CLI (B) 14,157,974 [11,221,908, 15,613,375]; fresh-cache dctx MCP (C), startup/indexing measured, 15,922,125 [15,513,198, 16,700,029]. B versus A: -5.01 %. On this corpus and model dctx did not save 25 % tokens; the pre-registered rule was not met. Official strict citation recall medians [min, max], A/B/C: 10.10 % [10.10, 20.73] / 14.46 % [8.36, 22.65] / 13.41 % [12.02, 66.72]. Diagnostic file-level recall medians: 53.77 % / 71.70 % / 76.42 %; diagnostic, not a replacement metric. The claim is accuracy and bounded context, not token savings: B and C named more required files at about equal (B) or higher (C) token cost. C cost +6.8 % tokens and +30 % wall time. dctx on its own does not save tokens by default. Savings come from a harness or agent system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context across long sessions over a large body of work, with complete control over every byte. There is no measured, citable savings figure for such a system yet. One corpus, one model, no significance claim; corpus and raw answers private and cannot be published; dctx 1.3.0 is not current HEAD. Under ~200 files, use grep. Source measured Byte stability: the same query on unchanged code returns the same bytes; 33 of 33 text and JSON answers were byte-identical after unrelated edits (Linux only). Source historical The October and November in-house numbers (run 7: 140 of 140 task questions, cold index and warm latency) measure tool output only, as estimated stdout tokens and raw fact coverage without a model; they are not agent completion rates or session costs. Source hypothesis That a pack template changes model answer quality or cost is a hypothesis pending an A/B test; nothing on this site measures it. Source
Measured values, as the documents state them today: Parsed from the documents at build time; nothing is retyped. Value What it measures Source 33/33 text, 33/33 JSON map answers byte-identical after unrelated edits and over five runs, three Linux corpora docs/research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md 0 socket attempts by dctx in every traced benchmark variant docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md 0.13-1.20 s cold index of 6 benchmark corpora, median of 3 runs docs/research/bench-3way-20261030/results/run7-53f8b6b/aggregate.json 50 language families: 36 full, 8 outline, 6 docs dctx languages
Removed in 1.2.0 These existed before 1.2.0 and no longer work. A transcript that uses them describes an old version. No longer exists Use instead dctx PATH (the implicit snapshot command, for example dctx . ) dctx pack PATH the top-level snapshot flags -d / --diff , -t / --tree and -r / --reset dctx pack PATH with its filters the project rule files .legacyignore and .dctxomitcontent .gitignore and .dctxignore dctx cache gc --legacy and its export-selection flags dctx cache gc
How to verify a claim Claim How to check it Test suite cargo test --workspace --locked --exclude dctx-desktop --exclude dctx-desktop-api CI Every push and pull request runs the suite on Linux, macOS (ARM64 and x64) and Windows, on stable Rust and the minimum supported version 1.91. No network calls scripts/release-check.sh --quick target/release/dctx-cli Byte stability python3 docs/research/stability-20261105/verify.py Historical benchmark docs/research/bench-3way-20261030/run-3way.sh target/release/dctx-cli Every output on this site Recorded from the real binary by tools/website/capture.py; tools/website/check.py re-records and fails on drift.

The problem #
An AI coding assistant only knows what is in its context window : the text sent to the model with your request. It cannot see the rest of your project.
Each of these costs you. Models read text as tokens (small chunks of text, roughly a short word or part of one), and providers bill per token. The model reads every token before it answers, so more tokens also means more waiting. And answers get worse as irrelevant text piles up. The README sums it up: every token in front of a model is paid for three times, to read it, again when a cache is missed, and again in attention.
What dctx does #
dctx is a command-line tool that reads your project on your machine and answers precise questions about it: where a function is defined, what calls it, what its exact source is. Each answer fits a size budget and is built from whole pieces of syntax; a piece that is too long is marked as cut, with a way to get the rest. The same question about the same code gives the same bytes every time. An assistant can run the commands itself or call them through the built-in MCP server ( dctx mcp ; MCP is a standard way for AI tools to call other tools). dctx can also pack a whole project into one structured block for a chat.
Start with grep plus file reads #
surface that fits in Choosing how to use dctx .
A small worked example #
Run with dctx 1.1.0 on a copy of this repository's crates/dctx-lex-go folder. The output is real and complete.
s:tests/fixtures/basic.go#Add fn L 43 - 45
calls:in:s:tests/fixtures/basic.go#main fn tests/fixtures/basic.go L 59
find returns a stable id, the kind of thing it is (a function) and its lines. This is a historical 1.1.0 transcript; the current CLI also includes verified source bytes in text read output, or in source_utf8 with read --json . neighbors says that main calls it, on line 59.
The philosophy #
The specification turns this into five testable rules.
Bounded. Every map answer has a size ceiling, reserved before anything is written, and a record is never split. The budget is up to 2,000 estimated tokens (1,000 for explain ).
Why it matters to you: one question cannot flood the context window and crowd out your own instructions.
Deterministic. The same code and the same question give the same bytes.
Why it matters to you: results are repeatable, and repeated prompts can be served from a cache.
Prefix-stable. When context is sent again across turns, bytes that did not need to change do not change.
Why it matters to you: this is what keeps caching working across a conversation.
Non-redundant. Within one session, do not resend what was already sent unless it changed. This one is still a target.
Honest. Every answer states its freshness, precision and provenance, and dctx never asserts what it does not know. With --json , the read above carries "freshness":{"mode":"strict","state":"verified"} , a precision block, and more and next fields for anything that did not fit. Calls it cannot resolve are listed as unresolved , not guessed.
Why it matters to you: you and your assistant can tell a fact from a guess.
Offline. No telemetry, no update checks, no model calls. A release check counted zero network connections across 16 commands. Nothing leaves your machine.
Private by default. A file is classified before any byte of it is read. Secret-shaped files such as .env , *.pem and id_rsa are listed with content omitted, with no override in v1.
No embeddings. dctx does not turn code into vectors and search by similarity. It ranks by names and syntax.
Features must earn their place. A feature without a measured acceptance gate is not a dctx feature.
Prompt caching, in plain words #
Much of each request to an AI model repeats the last one: system instructions, project context, earlier turns. Providers keep a cache of prompt beginnings. If the start of a new prompt matches a cached one exactly, byte for byte, they reuse their earlier work on that part. Cached input costs a fraction of the normal price and is processed faster.
Prefix-stable, simply #
Timestamps are the classic problem. In 1.0.0, every line of the dctx pack file tree carried a modification time, and file lines a size. The tree sits near the top, so merely re-saving a file (a touch ) changed almost the whole page as far as a cache is concerned. Since 1.1.0 tree lines carry only an id. A bare touch leaves the output byte-identical, and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix. --tree-stamps=on brings back the old lines.
In the same folder we appended one comment line to the last file in the tree, tests/review_lexers_a.rs , and compared dctx pack . before and after:
The evidence #
The stability report measured map answers on 6 November 2026, on three pinned local corpora with 11 kinds of question each. 33 of 33 text answers and 33 of 33 JSON answers were byte-identical after an unrelated edit elsewhere in the project, and all were identical over five separate runs.
The report states its limits too. It measures dctx's answers, not a provider's cache hits. It ran on Linux only. The layered design that would keep context prefix-stable across a whole conversation ( SPEC §12.1 ) is still a target.
Savings belong to the system #
11 November benchmark , the dctx CLI arm used 5.01 % fewer
An illustration of money and time #
Made-up numbers, not any provider's prices. Assume:
Other reasons determinism matters #
Reproducible reviews. A colleague who runs the same command on the same code sees exactly what the assistant saw.
Meaningful diffs. If saved context changes, the code changed, not a clock or a sort order.
Trust. A tool whose answers shift for no reason is hard to rely on. In the spec's words, "trust is the product".
What dctx is not #
Not a type checker. Call edges come from names, scopes and imports; ambiguous references are dropped.
Not exact token counting. Budgets use an estimate, ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7) , not a model's tokenizer.
Not vector search or RAG. No embeddings in the core, and the engine never calls a model.
Not a hosted service or a daemon. One binary that runs when you call it. No telemetry, not even opt-out.
Limits still matter. Plain dctx pack sends the selected project without an output budget by default. A 100 GB tree needs scoping, and the cache has a 2 GiB hard cap. CI covers Linux, macOS and Windows; byte-stability measurements here ran on Linux only.

Measured, in the open Start and choose your path The core belief: prompt-processing efficiency Quick Start Map mode: context for agents From source Use as a library CLI Reference Security & Privacy Open source and maintenance Where it comes from Contributing
dctx turns any folder into the smallest correct context for a task, offline, with byte-stable output that prompt caches can reuse. dctx is an advanced tool with several ways to use it. Used well, it cuts irrelevant text from selected tool answers. It does not save tokens by default; savings depend on a system reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context. Extra calls can add tokens. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything.
Run dctx agent-setup --format agents (or --format claude ) for short rules to paste into AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md .
Project status #
dctx is not yet stable and not enterprise-ready. It has been in development since January 2026. Until version 2.0, expect breaking changes often. AI providers keep changing how they optimize context on their side; dctx adapts to those changes quickly, but not in real time. Stability is the goal of 2.0, and the project is working toward it: we see an ultimate solution to this problem, and we are denoising it.
Installation #
System binary — available now. Download the archive for your OS and architecture
from GitHub Releases ,
compare its SHA-256 with the matching entry in SHA256SUMS , extract it, and put
dctx ( dctx.exe on Windows) on PATH . Archives cover Linux x64/ARM64,
verification, provenance and offline installation .
Node wrapper — available on npm from 1.3.1. Run npm install @tejl/dctx to install the
Node wrapper and its matching pinned
@tejl/dctx-<platform> native package, then npx @tejl/dctx --version to check it.
The Python and Go wrappers
over dctx rpc are built and tested in CI; use their CI artifacts. The
Rust facade is available from
Follow the safe path in ten minutes
What the output looks like #
These are real runs on the tiny kiosk sample , captured by capture.py from the release binary. Commands run inside a copy named kiosk . For source builds, the executable is dctx-cli (or define a dctx alias).
Pack a project #
The header explains the format, the tree assigns IDs, and file blocks carry paths and line counts. The first 40 output lines follow; only the tail is omitted. .env is listed without its contents.
<INSTRUCTIONS >
1. Manifest: The <DIRECTORY_TREE > section lists all files.
- Search for the marker: <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "UNIQUE_ID" >
- The content is between this marker and </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "UNIQUE_ID" >
</INSTRUCTIONS >
<DIRECTORY_TREE >
</DIRECTORY_TREE >
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F001" PATH = ".env" LINES = "0" >
</FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F001" >
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F002" PATH = ".gitignore" LINES = "2" >
target /
</FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F002" >
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F003" PATH = "Cargo.toml" LINES = "9" >
Find a symbol, then read it #
Pass the exact ID from find to read to get its metadata and verified source bytes:
s:src/util.rs#greet fn L 2 - 4
s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting fn L 10 - 12
For structured consumption, --json puts the same source bytes in source_utf8 (one JSON line, shown verbatim):
{ "v" : 2 , "place" : "kiosk" , "verb" : "read" , "freshness" :{ "mode" : "strict" , "state" : "verified" }, "precision" :{ "coverage" : "syntax" , "completion" : "complete" , "parser" : "dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9" }, "records" :[{ "id" : "s:src/util.rs#greet" , "kind" : "fn" , "path" : "src/util.rs" , "lines" :[ 2 , 4 ], "summary" : "The greeting shown on the kiosk screen." , "summary_source" : "doc" , "signature" : null , "span" :[ 44 , 126 ], "source_utf8" : "pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {\n format!(\"Hello, {}!\", title_case(name))\n}" , "edge" : null , "direction" : null , "target" : null , "confidence" : null }], "more" : 0 , "next" : null }
Pack for a task #
--for uses the task terms to select find results, neighbors and source reads. --budget 800 bounds estimated output tokens, not scan size; the footer reports usage and dropped records.
# dctx pack --for budget = 800 terms = 2
s:src/util.rs#greet fn L 2 - 4
s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting fn L 10 - 12
s:src/store.rs#Order struct L 4 - 8
s:src/store.rs#checksum fn L 22 - 24
s:src/store.rs#encode fn L 17 - 19
calls:in:s:src/main.rs#main fn src/main.rs L 7
pub id: u 32 ,
pub qty: u 32 ,
# end body_tokens = 223 budget = 800 dropped = 0
Which mode? #
CLI and one-off chat : pack selected source for a prompt or use the interactive terminal.
Agents, short tasks : compare with grep plus narrow file reads first.
Agents, long sessions and huge trees : scope the root, find symbols and read exact source.
MCP : use the lean profile to start; ACP is planned.
Libraries : embed the Rust facade today; install the Node wrapper with npm install @tejl/dctx , or use CI artifacts for the Python and Go wrappers.
CI and prompt caching : pin inputs and measure byte stability and provider cache behavior.
Desktop : build the Tauri 0.11 preview; the GPUI rebuild is planned.
Measured, in the open #
The baseline is grep plus reading files .
The 11 November whole-session benchmark measured 20 questions on a private 13-crate Rust workspace with claude-sonnet-5-5 , dctx 1.3.0 and three repeats per arm. Median total tokens [min, max]: grep plus reads 14,904,014 [14,604,149, 15,622,381]; dctx CLI (warm index) 14,157,974 [11,221,908, 15,613,375]; dctx MCP (fresh cache, startup/indexing measured) 15,922,125 [15,513,198, 16,700,029].
On this corpus and model dctx did not save 25 % tokens. CLI median tokens were -5.01 % versus grep; the pre-registered success rule was not met. MCP cost +6.8 % tokens and +30 % wall time. The claim is accuracy and bounded context , not token savings: CLI and MCP named more required files at about equal or higher token cost.
dctx on its own does not save tokens by default. Savings come from a harness or agent system that reuses byte-identical, prefix-stable context across long sessions over a large body of work. It behaves like an advanced caching mechanism, with complete control over every byte of context. There is no measured, citable savings figure for such a system yet. Why this matters .
Official strict citation recall medians [min, max]: grep 10.10 % [10.10, 20.73], CLI 14.46 % [8.36, 22.65], MCP 13.41 % [12.02, 66.72]. Diagnostic file-level recall medians: 53.77 %, 71.70 %, 76.42 %, respectively; this does not replace strict recall. One corpus, one model, three repeats; no significance claim. Corpus and raw answers are private and cannot be published; dctx 1.3.0 is not current HEAD. Under ~200 files, use grep.
Choosing how to use dctx covers scoping and MCP startup overhead. Measurement evidence describes what was measured (tool-output bytes and estimated tokens); other-tool protocols are retained only as secondary historical notes.

The core belief: prompt-processing efficiency #
Bounded : map answers use estimated token budgets and whole records.
Deterministic : identical source snapshots and requests give identical bytes.
Read the philosophy and its
testable constraints .

From source #
alias dctx = "$PWD/target/release/dctx-cli"
Cargo builds dctx-cli ( dctx-cli.exe on Windows); release archives supply
dctx . For a local source installation, use
cargo install --locked --path crates/dctx-cli and alias dctx=dctx-cli .
See CI coverage and desktop exclusions .
Use as a library #
The public Rust entry point is the dctx facade , available from
Git now; crates.io publication is pending .
dctx = { git = "https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx" , tag = "v1.3.1" }
This example is generated from the workspace doctest :
use dctx::{memory::{ CancelFlag , FixedClock , MemorySource }, *};
let mut source = MemorySource :: new ();
source. insert_file ( "hello.rs" , b"pub fn hello() {}\n" , 0 )?;
let mut session = Session :: builder (source). clock ( FixedClock ( Timestamp ( 0 )))
. cancellation (std::sync:: Arc :: new ( CancelFlag :: new ())). ceiling ( HostCeiling :: base ())
. selection ( SelectionPolicy :: from_texts (& RuleTexts :: default ())). grants ( HostGrants :: PermitAll )
. storage ( StoragePolicy :: Ephemeral { max_bytes: 8 * 1024 * 1024 }). place ( "demo" ). view ( "pack" ). build ()?;
let mut output = VecSink :: new ();
session. pack (& PackRequest :: new (), & mut output)?;
println! ( "{}" , std:: str :: from_utf8 (output. as_bytes ())?);
The host supplies selection rules and storage policy; FsSource does not
load .gitignore automatically. Read the
before embedding it. Python, Node and Go wrappers over dctx rpc live in
packages/python , packaging/npm
and packages/go ; they are built and tested in CI.
Install the Node wrapper with npm install @tejl/dctx ; use CI artifacts for Python and Go.
CLI Reference #
dctx context returns ranked context for a file, symbol name or stable node id;
dctx rpc serves the versioned engine protocol used by the language wrappers
( protocol ); send hello first.
dctx mcp and dctx serve [--mcp] serve the map verbs as MCP tools over stdio;
dctx read is dctx map read . dctx map export writes the whole graph as JSON or Mermaid.
dctx languages lists every supported language and its tier.
dctx doctor lists visible dctx binaries, their scopes, SHA-256 checksums and
Run dctx --help , dctx pack --help and dctx map --help for the complete
reference and dctx --version --verbose for feature and precision limits.
See map commands and limits ,
MCP profiles , exit codes ,
templates , and plugins .
does not enable it. Organization policy and dctx policy explain are planned.
Language tiers #
dctx languages prints this table ( --json for tools, --markdown for this block) from the one registry that also drives dctx --version --verbose ; a test fails when the block below differs from it.
full : symbols and call edges. Call edges are lexical, not type-resolved: they come from names, scopes and imports, never from a type checker, and ambiguous references are dropped.
outline : symbols only; no call edges are promised. Shell function bodies can yield same-file call guesses, but v1 does not promise shell call edges.
docs : headed sections.
Confidence : guess marks the heuristic outline families, and every record from those files carries confidence guess ; structural means a dedicated lexer or deterministic document rules.
Security & Privacy #
Pack, map and MCP run locally and have no telemetry , call no model and
make no network calls . Selection happens before any byte is read, hashed,
.gitignore , .dctxignore , global ignore file
Excluded from normal selection; --debug-ignored shows ignored path metadata without reading content
The global ignore file is <config dir>/dctx/ignore : $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore
or ~/.config/dctx/ignore on Linux and macOS, %APPDATA%\dctx\ignore on Windows.
dctx does not read Git metadata, so .git/info/exclude and Git's
core.excludesFile are not applied: copy those patterns into .dctxignore or
DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1 skips those ignore texts, so leave it unset when relying
on them. Built-in sensitive-file and .git exclusions still apply.
Sensitive files such as .env , private keys and credentials are omitted from
.git at any depth is never listed or read by map, and is never read by pack.
Symlinks are never followed; final-component file opens use O_NOFOLLOW .
The privacy contract and deny list
and map privacy guide explain
the boundary. Report vulnerabilities privately through SECURITY.md .
The release check tests socket activity under
strace -f and reports SKIP where tracing cannot run. Plugin network and
see current plugin limits .

before warming an index; --in only filters after indexing.

Agent builder embedding a library #
Agent builder embedding a library: project library with its own pinned binary (Python, Node or Go wrapper over dctx rpc ); never parse or slice pack text. Pitfall: re-implementing engine logic.
The Python , Node
and Go wrappers over dctx rpc are built and tested in

@tejl/dctx-<platform> optional dependency; use CI artifacts or a checkout for

read tool with context: true . Delivery history lasts for the CLI invocation

1. Install the system binary #
Download the archive for your OS and architecture and SHA256SUMS from
GitHub Releases .
On Linux use sha256sum ARCHIVE , on macOS shasum -a 256 ARCHIVE , or on Windows
PowerShell Get-FileHash ARCHIVE -Algorithm SHA256 , replacing ARCHIVE with the
Extract the archive and put dctx ( dctx.exe on Windows) on your user PATH .
2. Choose one project and inspect one answer #
Use a small project or a relevant sub-root. Check .gitignore and .dctxignore
before scanning; leave DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED unset. From that directory:
Replace Config with a symbol or heading in your project. Read a returned ID
with dctx map read 'ID' --json . The JSON includes verified source bytes as
source_utf8 and reports precision, freshness and pagination. Keep the same
3. Configure the lean MCP profile #
In a client accepting mcpServers , replace both absolute paths:
"mcpServers" : {
"dctx" : {
"command" : "/absolute/path/to/dctx" ,
"args" : [ "mcp" , "--profile" , "lean" , "/absolute/path/to/project" ]
Restart the client and confirm that find and read are available. The lean
profile has two tools , not the planned context/read/find profile. For a
MCP guide for profile selection and measured startup overhead,
and client-specific configs for other formats.
4. Measure before changing anything #
It reports body_tokens , budget and dropped , using estimated tokens rather
See measurement evidence and
CI/cache guidance .
Responsibilities #
(planned) . Prebuilt archives with SHA256SUMS exist today; signed CLI binary
Release archives with cosign signatures, SBOM and provenance, cache caps, dctx doctor , journals (planned), receipts (planned)
For current CLI exclusions, use .gitignore and .dctxignore ; the unified policy
Two scopes, one binary #
The system dctx on PATH belongs to you and your agents. A binary installed by a project library lives inside that project (virtualenv, node_modules), pinned and managed by that package manager. Same signed engine, different owner. Interactive agents and MCP call the system binary; application code and CI call the project binary; a library never silently falls back to PATH.
DCTX_BIN , their own platform package (Python, Node) or a versioned user cache,
and never search PATH . Until they are published, install them from CI
The CLI cache lives in <cache-parent>/<engine-major.minor>/ under the
platform-specific dctx/v2 parent (or DCTX_CACHE_DIR ), so engines 1.2 and 1.3
scopes ). A version/path line in every pack is planned. Today
dctx rpc reports the engine version in hello , and dctx doctor lists the dctx
explicitly, and use separate absolute DCTX_CACHE_DIR locations when two
Continue with the documentation index , modalities
or engine specification .

Calling the engine over dctx rpc from Python, Node or Go projects
From version 1.3.1, the npm release publishes @tejl/dctx with pinned @tejl/dctx-<platform> optional
available for system installation or an explicit DCTX_BIN path.

Short agent task: grep can be enough #

For your project, use the exact ID returned by find . Both text read and
read --json include verified source bytes; JSON carries them in source_utf8 . Skeletons
show declaration signatures without bodies. If an answer has more and next ,
pass that opaque next value with --cursor on the same request, and count the
Huge trees: scope before indexing #
Map's shared cache stores a lifecycle ledger ( ledger.v1 ), policy ( policy.v1 ),
The product hard cap is 2 GiB (2,147,483,648 accounted bytes) across the shared
filesystem-size guarantee. cache config --max-bytes can only tighten it.
--place selects the scan root. --in src narrows find/grep matches after
indexing; --budget , --limit and --cursor bound answers, not the tree scan.
Use existing .gitignore and a .dctxignore at the chosen root to exclude data,
For example, merge these project-specific entries into .dctxignore :
/data /
/generated /
/archive /
The host loads the global ignore file, root and nested .gitignore rules, then
the root .dctxignore . Built-in sensitive-file and .git exclusions still apply.
The global ignore file is <config dir>/dctx/ignore : $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore
or ~/.config/dctx/ignore on Linux and macOS, %APPDATA%\dctx\ignore on Windows.
dctx does not read Git metadata, so .git/info/exclude and Git's
core.excludesFile are not applied; put those patterns in .dctxignore or the
Do not set DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1 when relying on these ignore rules.
The built binary documents these environment variables , not scan-limit flags:
DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES = 268435456 DCTX_MAX_RECORDS = 250000 DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES = 25000 \
cache cap. A different absolute DCTX_CACHE_DIR selects a separate cache
MCP server: convenient tools with startup context #
Client configuration #
executable and the project to index (on Windows, use dctx.exe and JSON-escaped
For a source build, point command at target/release/dctx-cli .
Claude Code ( .mcp.json at the project root)
and Cursor ( .cursor/mcp.json ) use this JSON:
"mcpServers" : {
"dctx" : {
"type" : "stdio" ,
"command" : "/absolute/path/to/dctx" ,
"args" : [ "mcp" , "/absolute/path/to/project" ]
Codex uses ~/.codex/config.toml
(or .codex/config.toml in a trusted project):
args = [ "mcp" , "/absolute/path/to/project" ]
Tools and startup cost #
It exposes ten tools: map , find , neighbors , explain , read , skeleton ,
grep , hubs , path , export . These are query tools, not a pack or cache-admin
Both text and JSON read answers include verified source bytes. Set the MCP
read argument "json": true for structured output with source_utf8 , equivalent
to the CLI's --json .
Complete tools/list response, request ID 2 , without trailing LF
Compact result.tools array alone (definitions and schemas)
The captured response includes its trailing LF.
Token estimates use ceil(2 × bytes / 7) , the CLI's byte heuristic, not an
actual model tokenizer . Clients may transform schemas, add wrappers or defer

python3 - < < 'PYCODE'

--tree-stamps=off for stable prefixes. For map,
leave --meta off to exclude changing snapshot, generation and age metadata.
The stability report measured 33/33 text
cache hits, billed tokens or whole-session latency. A bare touch leaves default
Rust library: embed the facade #
The supported entry point for Rust integrations is the dctx facade ,
which exposes Session , SnapshotRequest , MapRequest , PackRequest , sinks,
The facade is available from Git now; crates.io publication is pending . In your
application's Cargo.toml :
dctx = { git = "https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx" , tag = "v1.3.1" }
The ten-line pack example is compiled and run as a
workspace doctest . It uses an in-memory source and
The example's println! belongs to the caller. A VecSink collects the encoded
For filesystem use, open an FsSource at a scoped root and supply a live Clock .
The source does not automatically load .gitignore ; the host must pass its
ignore-rule texts through RuleTexts / SelectionPolicy . Choose storage ceilings
Desktop app: Tauri preview today #
The desktop app is a Tauri 2 app, currently the
0.11 preview. It uses dctx-desktop-api and the shared Rust facade. Build it from
source using the app's quick start ;
Python, Node and Go wrappers #
Thin wrappers over the versioned dctx rpc protocol live in
packages/python ,
packaging/npm/dctx (which also forwards the
dctx CLI command) and packages/go . Each starts the
npm install @tejl/dctx ; npm includes the matching pinned @tejl/dctx-<platform>
that has dctx rpc . Their arguments carry full CLI authority, so never pass
untrusted values as --place , --output or dash-leading arguments.
--json map answers. Use the Rust facade when you need an in-process engine.

Definitions outside the index #
For find , neighbors , explain , read , grep , trace , impact and context , a literal local
JSON adds defined_outside_index , an array of objects with path and hint .
path dependencies, plus sibling Python from and Rust use targets. It searches
--also DIR is repeatable on every map verb, pack and context . Directories
carry their root directory label, for example s:app/main.py#run and
s:lib/shared.py#shared . Root labels must be distinct. Each root keeps its own
changing the order of --also does not change identities or reuse another set's
Commands #
Read a node's verified source; a long node pages with --cursor . dctx read is the same verb.
A file's (or m:<path> 's) declaration signatures in source order, no bodies.
Shortest edge path (calls, imports, contains; either direction; at most 8 hops), or no path .
Copy node IDs from results: m:sample.py names a module and
s:sample.py#PythonBeacon names a symbol. dctx map <verb> --help prints each
The following option descriptions follow dctx map --help
( source ):
Stage timings and the five slowest files on stderr ( DCTX_PROFILE=1 is the same switch).
Output tokens, 1..2000; explain max: 1000. read with no --budget uses the 2,000-token hard cap.
map : 1..3; neighbors : 1..4. explain and read take no depth.
map , find , neighbors page size; explain and read accept only 1. hubs : 1..60 lines, default 20.
Refused. Pass the previous page's next value to --cursor .
find : comma-separated node kinds.
find or grep : restrict to a relative path.
-i , --ignore-case
grep : ASCII case-insensitive match.
neighbors : comma-separated edge filter.
neighbors : relation direction.
read : exactly those absolute source lines inside the node; --full permits 400.
Environment bounds: DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES (total source bytes one scan may read,
default 1 GiB), DCTX_MAX_RECORDS (files, symbols and edges one index may hold,
default 1000000), DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES (files and directories one scan may visit,
default 100000) and DCTX_FRESHNESS (see below).
The parser also accepts these --kind values: method , struct , enum ,
trait , impl , const , macro , class , interface , symbol , module ,
package , place , test . Edge names also include contains , implements ,
uses-type , tests , documents , reexports .
The token estimate is ceil(2 * UTF-8 bytes / 7) , not a tokenizer guarantee.
Trace: how A reaches B #
trace follows directed call and import/reference edges in the indexed graph.
ambiguous. Missing endpoints and disconnected symbols return no path within
bounds . A depth cutoff, excess shortest paths or a byte cutoff adds a
truncated: line. A path is retained whole or dropped whole.
--max-depth N ( --depth N )
--json emits an object with v: 2 , verb: "trace" , paths (arrays of
locations), counts.paths , bounds and truncated . A location contains id ,
file , line , symbol and depth (zero for trace hops). Counts describe the
returned paths. An empty result has paths: [] .
Impact: what depends on a symbol #
impact lists direct identifier references and call lines, then distinct
caller depth; cycles do not repeat a caller. A truncated: line reports a depth,
--max-depth N ( --depth N )
--json emits v: 2 , verb: "impact" , files , counts , bounds and
truncated . Each file group contains file , direct , callers and counts ;
locations use the same fields as trace, with direct depth: 1 and transitive
depth >= 2 . Page counts contain files , direct_sites and
transitive_callers ; group counts contain the latter two. Empty results have
files: [] and zero counts.
Both verbs also accept dctx map trace / dctx map impact , --place PATH and
repeatable --also DIR . They share the deny list, root labels, cache identity,
Neither verb uses --budget or cursors. Bounds errors name the verb, option,
MCP's default tool set exposes trace ( from , to ) and impact ( symbol ),
with max_depth , max_paths / max_sites , max_bytes , also (an array of
read-only roots) and json . They can also be selected with --tools trace,impact .

Tiers: full extracts symbols and call edges, outline symbols only, and
docs headed sections. Confidence guess marks heuristic outlines, whose
records carry confidence guess . See language coverage .
Rust uses syn in release builds (the syntax-rust feature, reported as parser
dctx-lex-rust/syn-<version> with syntax coverage), for supported Rust syntax
resolution or macro expansion. dctx --version --verbose lists the parsers and
JSON answers expose precision.coverage , precision.completion and
precision.parser (the default structural parser identity is dctx-structural/3 ).
The model distinguishes
structural , syntax and opaque coverage from complete , partial and
refused completion. These labels describe extraction, separately from edge
checks empty records for OpaqueBeacon in sample.unknown .
Index, cache and privacy #
DCTX_FRESHNESS=strict_live hashes every file on a warm start. Exact source
The retired per-worktree SQLite cache selector ( map/storage.rs ) has been
deleted; the CLI does not read DCTX_MAP_CACHE .
The shared cache stores ledger.v1 , policy.v1 , serialized generations and
copies of all source contents. See Choosing how to use dctx
Set DCTX_CACHE_DIR to an
$XDG_CACHE_HOME/dctx/v2 , or ~/.cache/dctx/v2
DX-ARCH-08 : time-based expiry, a system
status accepts --root PATH ; gc accepts --root PATH , --max-bytes N and
--legacy . Applying purge requires --yes and either --root PATH or --all .
cache config without arguments shows persisted policy; auto on|off controls
auto-clean, and --max-bytes can only tighten the cap. Pack, map, template,
--no-auto-clean or DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0 disables that slice.
( <config dir>/dctx/ignore : $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/dctx/ignore or
~/.config/dctx/ignore on Linux and macOS, %APPDATA%\dctx\ignore on Windows),
root and nested .gitignore rules, then the chosen root's .dctxignore .
DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1 skips those ignore texts; built-in sensitive-file and
.git exclusions still apply. The core does not read Git metadata or run Git, so
.git/info/exclude and Git's core.excludesFile are not applied.
The optional Git plugin has separately disclosed authority; see Plugins .

Paste the section below into a project's AGENTS.md (or CLAUDE.md ) so coding agents start from dctx context.
Notes for coding agents #
$TASK is the task description. dctx runs map find on the names the text mentions (backticked words, snake_case,
camelCase, a::b , then longer plain words), then map neighbors and map read on the best hits, and prints whole lines
Name things in the text: --for main or --for Session works, but a sentence such as "how does caching work" only
backticks, as in --for 'fix `run` in the pack command' .
Then narrow with dctx map find , dctx map neighbors <id> and dctx map read <id> as needed ( dctx map --help ).

Bundled Git plugin and consent #
The default CLI includes dctx/git version 1.0.0 , with alias dctx git and
the verbs status and protect . The catalog defaults to enabled. A fresh CLI
without a consent record reports enabled with needs-consent ; shipping the
dctx git is a plugin alias, not a general Git passthrough.
The bundled manifest capabilities
Required file.read
Project .gitignore , at most 1,048,576 bytes.
Required file.write
Existing project .gitignore only ( create=false ); growth at most 4,096 bytes, total at most 1,052,672 bytes.
Optional program.run
Program git , operation git.add-ignore , resource git-admin:stage-ignore , output at most 65,536 bytes.
does not run Git, read .git/ or use Git hashes for identity.
--approve records consent for the displayed capability set. New installations
remain inactive until enabled; combined install --enable requires --approve .
across updates. enable --project PATH scopes consent to a project; omitting it
uses user scope. disable --project PATH is accepted/reported, but the current
The CLI additionally separates enablement ( inactive , enabled , disabled )
from consent ( inactive , needs-consent , granted , disabled ) and reports
with consent unavailable and worker excluded .
CLI reference #
( render.rs ) and
parse.rs :
dctx plugin , dctx plugin help , --help and -h show plugin help.
metadata; search --refresh requests a fetch. List and help start no worker,
fetch nothing and do not create a project .dctx/ directory.
offline bundle. URL/file sources require --id ; the parser also accepts
--enable --approve with those sources. update --check reports a candidate
verify --refresh-trust requests a revocation freshness check. Bundled updates
come with the containing CLI/app release. remove masks the bundled copy when
run requires the -- separator. The Git alias rejects that separator.
The parser recognizes --json for plugin and alias requests, including run ,
Desktop: Settings > Plugins #
Open Settings > Plugins to inspect bundled/installed source, version,
state, requested capabilities and the last failure. Refresh plugins reloads
the list. Enable and Disable call the host management API.
Grant consent opens a review dialog with plugin ID, version, artifact
SHA-256, capability descriptions and exact grants/bounds. Confirm grant
records user-wide consent for all projects; Cancel closes the dialog.
Check for update reports cached information and explicitly states that
plugins.ts ; opening settings does
Strict build #
The dctx library includes the optional
plugin-runtime feature in its defaults. Hosts requiring the engine without
that runtime must disable defaults and select pack , map , templates , fs ,
segments , cache as needed. The runtime adds the host, platform and protocol
For the CLI , select
--no-default-features --features strict when building. Cargo features are
additive: selecting strict alone leaves defaults enabled. This composition
excludes dctx-plugin-host , dctx-plugin-platform and dctx-plugin-git from
strict does not mean that every crate whose name contains plugin disappears.

(test fixtures use test keys). Unverified: a completed production release
What is not yet available #
Public plugin publication through this CLI. There is no plugin publish
command. The default discovery URL is https://example.invalid/dctx/index.json ;
a live public registry/release publication is unverified . Local index

and the crate map .

docs/research/trail-code-2026-10 (dctx 17dff0b , Trail-Code 0.23.1)
This document specifies dctx , a context engine for AI-assisted software development.
It is normative where it uses MUST , MUST NOT , SHOULD and MAY (RFC 2119).
Every claim it makes about the product is either marked landed (present in the
repository today), contract (a versioned contract in docs/design/contracts/ that is
partly implemented) or target (specified here, not yet built), and every target
values cite the pinned benchmark in docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/REPORT.md or the
Contents #
1. Purpose and the workflows served #
dctx turns a directory of source code into the smallest, most cache-stable, provably
authorized set of bytes that lets a model or a human act correctly — and it can prove
dctx map outline, find , read ; desktop app (free)
dctx pack (full / diff), templates, clipboard
library facade ( crates/dctx ), bindings
MCP surface ( dctx serve --mcp )
2. The core belief: prompt-processing efficiency #
philosophy and
whole-session benchmark .
MUST satisfy the five PPE constraints:
landed ( dctx_core::budget , API-PORTS-v1 BoundedSink )
tier layering remains target (§12.1); on 2026-11-06, 0495f5f preserved 33/33 text and 33/33 JSON answers after unrelated comment edits on three pinned local corpora; all identical over five runs, paired-answer M7 = 1.0 ( protocol and limits ); historical baseline 0/63 (§31.0)
landed ( precision.* , freshness.* in the wire format)
Rule. A feature without an acceptance gate stated in M1–M8, or in a latency,
3. Zero RAG defects #
defect corpus — fixtures with a positive control per class — that dctx conformance
Records are syntax-owned spans; read returns the whole node or a marked prefix with a continuation; records are never split
There is no incremental index and no stale flag. Every CLI process re-walks the tree and re-hashes the selected files; a persisted generation is reused only when every content digest still matches, and any change rebuilds the whole generation. Inside one session read re-hashes the bytes against the snapshot digest and refuses with SourceChanged when they differ. The CLI always takes strict snapshots, so freshness.state is always "verified" (the library reports "metadata" only for a FreshnessMode::Metadata request)
Path + qualified-name ids with ordinals; explicit moved , gone , ambiguous outcomes
contract — lexical ranking landed; graph edges are not emitted by the shipped CLI (TC-F01); the resolver is landed in crates/dctx-map-resolve but not wired (§7); typed rung target
landed for map verbs; the legacy tree ( dctx . -t ) and pack are unbounded (974 KB and 8.7 MB measured) and are not conformant surfaces
M5 inside M2; dctx bench tokens (§28)
embedding:<model> — labeled, optional, never default.
4. Privacy and authority #
Selection before content. A path is classified ( Include , Exclude ,
OmitContent , DebugVisible ) before any byte of it is read, hashed, parsed or
cached. Exclude , OmitContent and DebugVisible never authorize content. Landed;
evidence: read-spy tests in crates/dctx-adapter-fs/tests/privacy.rs and
crates/dctx-map-query/tests/source_privacy.rs .
Rules. Built-in defaults, repository .gitignore files (read as plain text),
.dctxignore and policy ( privacy.ignore ) combine. Landed for
Secret-shaped files (landed for v1). A strict, built-in deny covers .env ,
.env.* , *.env , .envrc , *.pem , *.key , *.p12 , *.pfx , *.jks , *.keystore ,
id_rsa , id_dsa , id_ecdsa , id_ed25519 (and _ / - suffixed variants), .netrc ,
_netrc , .npmrc , .pypirc , .pgpass , .htpasswd , .git-credentials , credentials ,
credentials.<data> , *.credentials.json and secrets.<data> (data = json, yaml, yml,
v1 has no override: no --allow-sensitive flag, and no local rule can negate the deny.
Policy MAY later add named classes ( aws , gcp , ssh , jwt ). dctx never scans contents
to decide. Gate: the adversarial corpus's planted .env value is
absent from pack output and from the map cache; the path is listed. Checked for every
shape and every command by <repo>/scripts/checks/V1-1.zsh (TC-F08 is closed).
No VCS in the core. The core never reads .git/ , never spawns git , never uses
Landed ( crates/dctx-map-query/tests/no_git.rs ).
No network in the core. No telemetry, no update checks, no model calls. The only
legal telemetry value in policy is "none" . Measured: zero socket system calls in
Re-check at emission. Policy is checked again before bytes leave the engine, even
5. Identity #
Identity is defined by docs/design/contracts/IDENTITY-v1.md and summarized here.
Algorithm-tagged first-party SHA-256 of the exact authorized bytes, plus byte length ( crates/dctx-hash )
ObjectKey + language + parser identity and revision + extraction-rule digest
Sorted manifest of (path, stamp, ObjectKey ) for the authorized view
view digest (target)
SHA-256 over the ViewKey framing and the canonical request bytes; printed in the provenance trailer ( --provenance , §11) so a caller can name what it already holds
One per layer plus the effective digest (§15); part of ViewKey
6. The graph: nodes, ids, outcomes #
Nodes: place , package , module , symbol (with kinds fn , method , struct ,
enum , trait , impl , const , macro , class , interface , type , test ) and
doc sections. Ids are stable, human-copyable strings:
A request for an id that no longer resolves returns an outcome , never a silent
empty answer: moved (with the new id, from body-fingerprint evidence), gone , or
ambiguous (with candidates).
7. Edges, confidence and provenance #
Edge kinds: contains , imports , calls , implements , uses-type , tests ,
documents , reexports .
Status. Kinds and the confidence lattice are landed in dctx-map-model ;
crates/dctx-map-resolve . The facade index ( crates/dctx/src/index ) emits only
contains edges today , so neighbors --edge calls|imports was empty on 140 of 140
Bound by syntax and scope, or by an import that resolves to a file in the view, or supplied by a compiler-grade overlay. Measured expectation: a comparison tool reaches precision 0.94–1.00 at recall 0.10–0.96 with syntax-and-scope binding alone; dctx MUST reach precision ≥ 0.95 before its edges may be shown without a guess label
lexer + resolver; lsp:<server>@<version> overlays
typed (target)
An edge labeled exact that is wrong is a defect , not a statistic.

8. Precision labels #
Every answer carries precision.coverage ( structural | syntax | opaque ),
precision.completion ( complete | partial | refused ) and precision.parser
(for example dctx-structural/1 , syn/2 ). Unsupported files are opaque : listed,
Omissions (target, P1). precision.omitted counts paths excluded for reasons other
than policy — {binary, unnamed, oversize, capped} — so an agent knows the map is
extraction.max_facts_per_file are labeled partial (TC-F07: one 6.7 MB JSON fixture
9. Freshness #
read always verifies its own bytes, in every mode (landed). Answers carry
freshness.mode and freshness.state . The age in seconds ( age_s ) and the snapshot
digest are opt-in ( --provenance , §11), because either in the default page defeats
prefix caching (PPE-3). Status: target; today both are in every default answer.
Shipped behaviour (v1): the modes above are a target. The CLI always takes a strict
snapshot, so freshness.state is always "verified" ; there is no stale flag (R3, §3).

11. Page formats and byte stability #
Two formats: the text page (default; one record per line; ids first) and JSON v2
( --json ; no insignificant whitespace; LF-terminated; field order fixed). Both obey:
generation, age) is a trailer line behind --provenance , or a JSON field behind
--json --provenance (P0 header prerequisite measured on 2026-11-06: all 33 tested
text answers start with # <place> <verb> ; all 33 tested default JSON answers omit
snapshot, generation and age_s , and are identical over five runs and after an
unrelated comment edit. Shipped opt-in flag: --meta ; the specified provenance
trailer and --provenance interface remain target. Evidence , TC-F03);
the text page carries content: find and map records are
id<TAB>kind<TAB>path:L1-L2<TAB>summary ; explain prints signature, summary and edge
counts by kind; read prints the source span (P0 status, 2026-11-06: text read
carried source in all three measured cases; text explain still printed only
id/kind/path. Richer text fields remain target; evidence , TC-F04);
JSON v2 omits null fields (target, P0: today thirteen keys per record, many null,
so a JSON find fit 4 records where the text page fit 10);
paths are root-relative with / separators on every OS;
Note (1.0.1, legacy source page). The dctx pack / dctx . text page (the [DCTX_LLM_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_V1] envelope) follows the same no-timestamp rule by default: its tree and root lines carry the ID only, with no MOD: and no SIZE: (a size changes on every ordinary edit, and the tree precedes the file blocks), so a bare touch leaves the page byte-identical and an edit keeps the bytes before the edited file as a common prefix. --tree-stamps=on reproduces the 1.0.0 page with MOD:<ms> and SIZE: on every tree line; {{{node.mod}}} and {{{node.size_part}}} remain available to custom templates.
Gates. (P0) ≥ 95 % of text answers byte-identical after an unrelated edit (0 of 63

12.2 View digests #

12.3 Delta answers (target) #
--since <view-digest> recomputes the answer and emits only records whose content
digest changed, -<id> lines for removed records, and a header
base=<view> changed=<n> removed=<m> unchanged=<u> . An unknown base yields the full
answer with base=none , never an error. The engine stores record ids and digests per
view (not bytes) in a small, user-private, TTL-bound ledger. dctx pack --since
<snapshot> applies the same rule to whole files: unchanged files appear as one tree

session renders as =<id> unless its digest changed or --full is given. Session
12.5 Budget planner (target) #
dctx map plan --budget N <requests…> allocates a total budget by marginal value —
planned , used , left . Deterministic greedy over already-scored records.
12.6 Compression levels (target) #
--level signature | skeleton | body for read and for pack blocks:
Signature, nested declarations and control-flow keywords; bodies elided as … N lines
The level is part of the view digest. Defaults: map records use signature , read
uses body ; DTS MAY set levels per selection (for example skeleton for tests/** ).

15. The seven-layer policy lattice #
Today's rule — effective_permission = host_grant ∩ organization_ceiling ∩
session_selection (product contract C03) and the plugin grant lattice
M ∩ U ∩ O ∩ H ∩ S(t) ∩ A — generalizes to seven layers. Each layer can only
narrow the layers above it.
Hard caps (2,000 tokens, 8 MiB per file, 2 GiB cache), network = none , telemetry = none
.dctx/policy.dts : selections, omit rules, templates, learnings location
Monotone narrowing. effective = fold(narrow, L0 … L6) per field: set
AND for permissions and OR for required / deny . A widening attempt is a typed
compile error naming the layer and field — never a silent clamp.
Unreadable policy refuses. A present bundle that fails verification blocks every
mode except dctx policy explain .
Policy epoch. The effective digest is part of ViewKey and of every plugin
Tenants. A tenant is a named narrowing selected by L3 or L4, or requested by a
Property P9 (monotone policy). For random layer stacks, the effective value is
within every layer field-wise, and a widening at layer k fails naming k . Mutation

is Ed25519 over dctx-org-policy-v1 ‖ manifest bytes , verified by crates/dctx-ed25519 .
Enrollment. dctx policy enroll --fingerprint <hex> <bundle> pins the
Updates. A monotonic sequence is accepted forward only; downgrades are refused;
Distribution is any file channel: MDM, configuration management, a repository the

24.5 Desktop #

25. Blast radius (target) #
dctx blast traverses reverse adjacency (callers, implementors, tests, documents) from a
set of changed spans, bounded like neighbors . The graph side is core. The change side
Snapshot diff (default). dctx blast --from <snapshot> compares the current
VCS supply. The git plugin's vcs.changes returns hunks for --staged ,
--branch <name> and similar; the core maps hunks to node spans.
Formats: text records, JSON, and --format pr-comment (Markdown). Posting the comment
is a network plugin. Gate: ≤100 ms warm for a 10-hunk change on the pinned corpus.

.dctx/learnings/<kind>/<slug>.md ; kinds decisions , guardrails , preferences , skills ; policy may narrow kinds and size
Markdown; first heading is the title; a fenced dctx block with applies: ids, since: snapshot, status: active \| retired , optional enforce: true
Ordinary d: doc nodes with documents edges to the ids they name; find --kind learning ; boost when applies meets the focus set
dctx learn add <kind> "<title>" [--applies <id>…] . The core writes only into .dctx/learnings/ and only on an explicit user action
For each changed node (§25), lists guardrails whose applies covers it or its neighbors at depth 1. Advisory; exit non-zero only with --strict and an enforced active guardrail
A learning that applies to a gone id is reported orphaned ; nothing is deleted automatically
Only via dctx learn import with body-fingerprint binding; labeled src=import:<tag> ; served only while fingerprints match

27.1 The rules #
Core crates are std-only. dctx-hash , dctx-core , dctx-ports , dctx-map-model
(without wire-json ), dctx-map-segment , dctx-template , dctx-pack ,
dctx-map-resolve , dctx-map-bind , dctx-plugin-protocol , the hand-written lexers,
dctx-adapter-fs , dctx-adapter-store , dctx-adapter-cache and dctx-map-scan
have zero third-party normal dependencies and forbid unsafe ; CI checks
cargo tree -e normal per crate.
Every third-party crate in a default build is listed in docs/DEPENDENCIES.md
with version, licence, unsafe count, reason and the plan for it. CI fails if the
Ed25519 stays for security and trust. ed25519-dalek (exact pin, std feature
only, verify-only) is a vetted, widely audited security crate and the single
disclosed exception to the zero-third-party rule, behind feature trust . It
trust has no third-party crate and cannot verify signatures; it refuses unsigned
27.2 Planned removals #
syn from the strict feature
Today strict implies syntax-rust ; a minimal feature set MUST NOT (structural Rust extractor with precision.parser = dctx-structural/1 )

The facade's hand-written canonical JSON; std Error ; dctx-hash
rusqlite and bundled SQLite
syn stack from the default build
Held-out precision ≥ syn − 1 point; zero wrong exact edges
Kept as a disclosed, target-specific adapter dependency outside the minimal closure (plugins unavailable in that build), or a reviewed first-party syscall boundary in dctx-plugin-platform
Confinement property tests; written unsafe review
27.3 Maintenance #
dctx is Apache-2.0 open source, including the desktop app, with no license fee. Organizations that depend on dctx can sign a maintenance agreement for security response targets, long-term support and priority work; see MAINTENANCE.md . Build-closure targets are engineering goals.

Status: current — architectural principle retained; historical examples describe their original release.
For shipped behavior and limitations, see the README , testing guide and specification . Earlier “formally proven” wording refers to historical tests; tests and defense layers do not constitute a formal proof of all implementations.
Date: 2026-02-02
Approved: 2026-02-02
Implemented: 2026-02-02 (WO-050 through WO-054)
Deciders: Operator, AI Assistant
Context: Phase 10.6 - Safety-Critical Privacy & Performance Audit
Context and Problem Statement #
Users trust dctx with their entire codebases, including sensitive files like .env , .git/ , API keys, credentials, and proprietary source code. Our ignore and omit systems were implemented primarily for output cleanliness and token efficiency, but we have not formally guaranteed that ignored files are NEVER read into memory.
1. Are ignored files ( .env , credentials) ever read into memory?
2. Does the --debug-ignored flag compromise privacy?
Risk: Without formal privacy guarantees, users cannot trust dctx with sensitive codebases. A single accidental file read could expose credentials, leak proprietary code, or violate security policies.
Decision Drivers #
Privacy First: Ignored files must NEVER be read, regardless of flags or configuration
Performance: Ignored folders must be skipped entirely (no recursion)
Semantic Clarity: IGNORE vs OMIT must have clear, enforced meanings
Debug Transparency: Users must be able to verify their ignore rules work correctly
Template Safety: Custom templates must not accidentally trigger I/O on ignored files
Zero Trust: Assume users handle classified/sensitive information
Option 1: Status Quo (No Formal Guarantees) #
Pro: No code changes required
Pro: Current behavior is already safe (but undocumented)
Con: No formal verification or tests
Con: Users cannot trust the system
Con: Template variables could be unsafe in the future
Verdict: [no] Rejected - Privacy must be provable, not assumed
Option 2: Full Privacy Audit + Formal Guarantees (SELECTED) #
Pro: Provable privacy through code analysis and tests
Pro: Clear semantic distinction between IGNORE and OMIT
Pro: Template variable safety system prevents accidental reads
Pro: Performance optimizations (skip ignored folders)
Pro: Debug mode that doesn't compromise privacy
Con: Requires implementation work (2-3 hours)
Verdict: [yes] SELECTED - Only acceptable solution for sensitive codebases
Option 3: Encryption-Based Approach #
Pro: Could encrypt ignored file contents in memory
Con: Massive complexity, performance overhead
Con: Doesn't solve the problem (still reading files)
Verdict: [no] Rejected - Overengineered, doesn't address root issue
Decision Outcome #
Chosen Option: Option 2 - Full Privacy Audit + Formal Guarantees
Rule System Definition #
IGNORE (default)
[no] NEVER
IGNORE ( --debug-ignored )
[yes] Shown with [IGNORED] marker
[no] NEVER
OMIT (always)
[warning] [Content omitted by pattern rules]
[no] NEVER
IGNORE #
Meaning: "This file/folder does not exist for our purposes."
- .git/ - Version control internals
- node_modules/ , target/ , __pycache__/ - Build artifacts
- .env , .secrets - Credentials and sensitive configuration
- *.log , *.tmp - Temporary files
- Debug Mode: Visible in tree with [IGNORED] marker, folder recursed, but files never read
- Configuration: .dctxignore (project) or ~/.config/dctx/ignore (global)
OMIT #
Meaning: "This file exists and is relevant to the project structure, but we don't care about its contents."
- package-lock.json , Cargo.lock - Lockfiles (structure matters, content doesn't)
- *.svg - Image files (relevant to project, but binary/verbose)
- go.sum , yarn.lock - Dependency checksums
- Content section shows: [Content omitted by pattern rules]
Debug Mode ( --debug-ignored ) #
Purpose: Allow users to verify their ignore rules are working correctly.
- Shows ignored files/folders in directory tree with [IGNORED] marker
- CRITICAL: Files are still NEVER read into memory
- Grayed-out metadata: SIZE from stat() only, never from content reading
SENSITIVE (strict deny, v1) #
Meaning: "This file holds credentials. No dctx command ever reads, hashes, indexes or prints its bytes."
Shapes (final path component, ASCII case-insensitive; the single list is
dctx_core::filter::is_secret_shaped_name ):
- env files: .env , .env.* , *.env , .envrc
- keys, certificates and keystores: *.pem , *.key , *.p12 , *.pfx , *.jks , *.keystore
- SSH private keys: id_rsa , id_dsa , id_ecdsa , id_ed25519 , and those names with a _ / - suffix
without a dot ( id_rsa_deploy ); id_rsa.pub is not matched
- credentials: credentials , credentials.<data> , *.credentials.json , secrets.<data>
(data = json , yaml , yml , toml , ini , xml ); credentials.py and secrets.rs stay ordinary source
- token files: .netrc , _netrc , .npmrc , .pypirc , .pgpass , .htpasswd , .git-credentials
- Applies whether or not the file is git-tracked, to every surface: pack (all view filters, including
--include , --ext , --hidden and --debug-ignored ), every dctx map verb (map, find, read, explain,
skeleton, grep, neighbors, hubs, path, export; by stable id or by raw path; with or without --in ) and the
dctx mcp tools, which run the same code path.
- Enforced in the map policy ( PolicyView::decide ), again before any map read ( Session::read_verified ),
in map grep, in the pack scan ( dctx-pack snapshot) and in the dctx-map-query source adapter.
- No override. v1 has no --allow-sensitive flag, and repository or global rule files cannot
Verification: crates/dctx/tests/map_sensitive_files.rs , the unit tests next to
is_secret_shaped_name , PolicyView::decide and the pack scan, and the end-to-end check
<repo>/scripts/checks/V1-1.zsh (a git-tracked fixture with one canary per shape, run against every command).
.git (hard guard, v1) #
Any path with a .git segment, at any depth, is excluded by PolicyView::decide before the rule layers are
consulted, so !.git/ , !.g*/ or !nested/.git/** in .gitignore or .dctxignore cannot re-include it: the
map verbs never list or read it, and Session::read_verified refuses it too. pack excludes it as well
( dctx-pack snapshot); only --debug-ignored still lists it by name, never reading it. Tests:
git_negations_never_list_or_read_git in crates/dctx/tests/git_and_symlink_privacy.rs and in the pack snapshot.
Symlinks (v1) #
dctx::FsSource never follows a symlink: a symlinked final component is refused before the open, and the open
itself uses O_NOFOLLOW (raw platform values; crates/dctx has no libc dependency), so a symlink swapped in after
refused for listings and reads. Tests: crates/dctx/src/adapters/fs.rs and crates/dctx/tests/git_and_symlink_privacy.rs .
DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1 #
This environment switch (dctx-cli host::project_rules ) makes pack and the map verbs ignore every ignore file
(global ignore, .gitignore , nested .gitignore , .dctxignore ); omit files and the built-in rules still load.
It does not touch the SENSITIVE deny, the .git guard or the symlink rules above: those do not come from rule
files. <repo>/scripts/checks/V1-1.zsh reruns its canary checks with the switch set.
Guarantee 1: Ignored Files Never Enter Read Queue [yes] #
Assertion: Files matching ignore rules are excluded at tree construction time ( walker.rs:136-146 ) via should_ignore_item() check. They never appear in the DirContextTreeNode tree, therefore never collected by collect_file_paths() , therefore never read by populate_file_contents_parallel() .
Verification: [yes] PROVEN
- [yes] Unit test: test_collect_file_paths_skips_ignored - ignored file never in read queue
- [yes] Unit test: test_collect_file_paths_skips_ignored_subtree - entire subtrees skipped
Guarantee 2: Ignored Folders Skip Recursion #
Assertion: When a folder matches ignore rules, walk_recursive() uses continue (walker.rs:146) to skip the item entirely. The function is never called recursively on that folder's children.
- Performance benchmark: 500MB node_modules/ should take < 100ms to skip
Guarantee 3: Debug Mode Does Not Compromise Privacy [yes] #
Assertion: When --debug-ignored is active, the system recurses into ignored folders and shows them in the tree, but the files are marked with is_ignored: true flag. The populate_file_contents_parallel() function respects this flag and never calls fs::read() on ignored files.
Verification: [yes] PROVEN
- [yes] Test: test_ignored_files_shown_with_marker - .env appears in tree with [IGNORED]
- [yes] Test: test_ignored_files_never_have_content - no content blocks for ignored files
- [yes] Test: test_collect_file_paths_skips_ignored - ignored files never enter read queue
Guarantee 4: Template Variables Cannot Trigger Unsafe Reads [yes] #
Assertion: Template variables are classified by I/O requirement:
- Metadata-Only: {{{file_id}}} , {{{file_path}}} , {{{file_size}}} , {{{mod}}} (safe - from stat() )
- Content-Requiring: {{{lines}}} , {{{content_preview}}} (unsafe - requires fs::read() )
For ignored/omitted files, content-requiring variables are never resolved due to !node.is_ignored guard preventing content block rendering.
Verification: [yes] PROVEN
- [yes] Test: test_template_variable_safety_for_ignored_files with 6 comprehensive assertions (WO-054)
Ignored Folder Skip (Primary Optimization) #
Scenario: Project with 500MB node_modules/ (50,000 files)
fs::read() Calls
Performance Gain: 50-100x faster for large ignored folders.
Omit Pattern Performance #
Scenario: Lockfiles in monorepo (20 files, 10MB each)
Performance Gain: 20x faster, 100x less memory.

title: Language coverage (ADR-018)
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/docs/ADR-018-Language-Coverage.md
---

Document: `docs/ADR-018-Language-Coverage.md` in [Documents](#documents). [Read the page](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/language-coverage/).

Rendered text and page details not already verbatim in the document pack:

All documents Start What dctx is Choose your path Safe path in ten minutes Why dctx README and quick start Modalities Choosing how to use dctx CLI and agents: map mode Agent snippet MCP Libraries CI and caching Plugins guide Scopes Two scopes, one binary Who is responsible for what Engine Specification Privacy guarantees Cache and limits Language coverage (ADR-018) Template contract (DTS v2) Templating engine (ADR-003) Crate map Reference CLI reference CLI exit codes Languages Templates Examples Trust Benchmarks Measurement evidence Byte-stability report Earlier two-way study Philosophy Security policy Releasing Contributing Trademark Maintenance For AI evaluators Facts and verification llms.txt ADR-018: Language Coverage View source · Edit on GitHub · Markdown · docs/ADR-018-Language-Coverage.md · 516 words · updated 7 November 2026 On this page Context Decision Implementation Results Trade-offs Alternatives Considered References Lessons Learned Future Work
Status: superseded — historical design and implementation record.
The original 13-family scope below is superseded by the current language registry table ; confidence and completion principles remain relevant.
The Problem #
Map facts need explicit coverage and completion claims across source/configuration languages; precision is separate from edge confidence ( crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs ).
Root Cause Analysis #
Structural extraction is not a full grammar claim, and incomplete extraction must not silently become complete facts ( crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs , crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs ).
Decision #
Use pure structural extraction for 13 families: Rust, JavaScript/TypeScript, Markdown, Python, Go, Java, C/C++, configuration (JSON/TOML/YAML), C#, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP and Swift ( crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs , docs/CRATE-MAP.md ).
The facade's default profile uses hand-written extraction, including line-oriented Rust and the first-party Markdown extractor. Qualification: dctx-lex-rust itself uses syn ; it is optional behind facade syntax-rust , so “13 hand-written lexers” is not a claim about every lexer crate or map-parse Rust implementation ( crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs , crates/dctx/Cargo.toml , crates/dctx-lex-rust/src/lib.rs ).
Keep one shared facade dispatch and fact-to-symbol conversion in crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs ; Rust and Markdown retain specialized entry paths in crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs .
Carry coverage ( syntax , structural , opaque ), completion ( complete , partial , refused ) and bounded parser identity separately from confidence ( crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs ).
Phase 1: Pure Lexers and Facade Projection #
The shared dispatch converts nodes without reading source or retaining bodies. New language branches expose only complete extraction; JavaScript/TypeScript preserve their existing partial-fact projection ( crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs ).
The facade rejects NUL/non-UTF-8 symbol extraction and assigns stable ids and containment after extraction ( crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs ).
Phase 2: Map-parse Adapters #
PureParser dispatches the language adapters over caller-provided bytes; partial/diagnostic extraction is refused as ParseError::Syntax , and unknown languages have a module-only fallback ( crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs ).
Shared fact assembly records file precision and finalizes source-ordered facts with duplicate-id handling ( crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/facts.rs ).
Phase 3: Store Invariants Gate #
The parser gate checks file ownership, unique/kind-correct ids, source-bounded spans, valid confidence/kind combinations, existing edge endpoints and containment reachability. It also simulates query insertion of Place/Package nodes to catch duplicate ids ( crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/lexers.rs , crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs ).
Phase 4: Fuzz Gate #
Seeded bounded property tests exercise arbitrary bytes, Unicode, malformed inputs, deterministic results, successful-result store invariants and fixture prefixes without executing source ( crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs ).
Results #
The gate source defines successful fixture controls as well as refusal/robustness cases; this record asserts test obligations, not a new passing execution ( crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/lexers.rs , crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs ).
Benefits #
Structural facts can be produced without a default tree-sitter runtime, with explicit precision and conservative abstention ( crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs , crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs ).
Costs #
The facade's structural Rust profile and optional syn path differ; the shared facade dispatch also deliberately differs from PureParser on JavaScript partial facts ( crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs , crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs , crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs ).
Alternatives Considered #
The earlier spec proposed tree-sitter as the parser dependency. Current adapters retain it only behind syntax-tree-sitter as an optional oracle; languages without an included grammar use pure adapters even in that oracle ( docs/SPEC-MAP-MODE.md , crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs ).
References #
Inventory: docs/CRATE-MAP.md ; facade: crates/dctx/src/index/lex_dispatch.rs ; adapters: crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs ; robustness: crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs .
Lessons Learned #
Language family count, structural coverage, grammar completeness and edge confidence are distinct claims; the Rust implementation qualification must remain visible ( docs/CRATE-MAP.md , crates/dctx-map-model/src/domain/precision.rs , crates/dctx-lex-rust/src/lib.rs ).
Future Work #
Keep tree-sitter optional and preserve precision/refusal and store-invariant gates when extending adapters; optional oracle coverage is limited to its included grammars ( crates/dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/mod.rs , crates/dctx-map-parse/tests/fuzz_all.rs ).

title: Templating engine (ADR-003)
