---

Document: `docs/ADR-003-Templating-Engine.md` in [Documents](#documents). [Read the page](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/templating/).

Rendered text and page details not already verbatim in the document pack:

All documents Start What dctx is Choose your path Safe path in ten minutes Why dctx README and quick start Modalities Choosing how to use dctx CLI and agents: map mode Agent snippet MCP Libraries CI and caching Plugins guide Scopes Two scopes, one binary Who is responsible for what Engine Specification Privacy guarantees Cache and limits Language coverage (ADR-018) Template contract (DTS v2) Templating engine (ADR-003) Crate map Reference CLI reference CLI exit codes Languages Templates Examples Trust Benchmarks Measurement evidence Byte-stability report Earlier two-way study Philosophy Security policy Releasing Contributing Trademark Maintenance For AI evaluators Facts and verification llms.txt ADR-003: Extensible Templating System (DTS) & Compilation Strategy View source · Edit on GitHub · Markdown · docs/ADR-003-Templating-Engine.md · 508 words · updated 7 November 2026 On this page 1. Decision: Explicit Marker Definition 2. Decision: "Ahead-of-Time" (AOT) Template Compilation 3. Decision: Two-Pass Rendering Engine 4. Template File Structure 5. Available Data Variables (Runtime)
Status: current — architectural principle retained; historical examples describe their original release.
For shipped behavior and limitations, see the README , testing guide and specification .
Date: 2026-01-08
Author: dctx Team
Context: Users require granular control over the output format to support various AI models. The system must maintain high performance (avoiding expensive parsing on every run) and ensure robustness (instructions matching output).
1. Decision: Explicit Marker Definition #
* start_marker_open (Default: < )
* start_marker_close (Default: > )
* end_marker_open (Default: </ )
* end_marker_close (Default: > )
This allows users to redefine tags completely, e.g., to [SECTION] ... [/SECTION] or {{#SECTION}} ... {{/SECTION}} .
2. Decision: "Ahead-of-Time" (AOT) Template Compilation #
Parsing text templates, validating variable references, and checking for cycles is expensive. We will not do this during the standard dctx runtime.
The "Baked-In" Default #
The default template (defined in the ADR) is parsed at Rust Compile Time (or hardcoded as a static struct). This ensures dctx runs with zero parsing overhead out-of-the-box.
User Custom Templates #
Users can edit templates in ~/.config/dctx/templates/ . However, dctx does not read these text files directly during snapshot generation.
* Action: User edits .dctx_template file.
* Command: User runs dctx template build <path> .
* Process:
1. dctx parses the text file.
3. Serializes the parsed structure into an optimized binary format (e.g., bincode ).
4. Saves the result to ~/.cache/dctx/templates/user_custom.bin .
* Runtime: When dctx runs, if configured to use a custom template, it loads this pre-validated binary directly into memory.
3. Decision: Two-Pass Rendering Engine #
Pass 1 (Config Resolution): Occurs during the "Template Build" phase. Resolves all {{VAR}} placeholders within the [VARIABLES] section.
Pass 2 (Data Injection): Occurs during runtime. Injects {{{DATA}}} into the pre-compiled Partial structures ( [PARTIALS] section) and assembles the [LAYOUT] .
4. Template File Structure #
1. [VARIABLES]: Key-Value pairs for static strings.
2. [PARTIALS]: Definitions for repeated elements ( TREE_ENTRY , FILE_BLOCK ).
3. [LAYOUT]: The global document structure.
5. Available Data Variables (Runtime) #
* {{{node.id}}} : Optimized incremental ID (e.g., 1, 2, 10).
* {{{node.path}}} : Relative path.
* {{{node.type_char}}} : [D] or [F] .
* {{{node.mod}}} : Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Available to custom templates. The built-in default template does not print it since 1.0.1, because a timestamp changes on a bare touch and breaks the byte-stable prefix of the page; --tree-stamps=on selects the built-in stamped template (the 1.0.0 text, MOD: and SIZE: on every tree line, MOD in the instructions). The default entry also leaves out {{{node.size_part}}} , since a size changes on every ordinary edit; {{{node.size}}} and {{{node.size_part}}} stay available to custom templates.
* {{{node.size}}} : File size in bytes.
* {{{file.lines}}} : Line count of the file.
* {{{file.content}}} : Actual file content.

40 non-fixture Cargo packages: 36 under crates/ , one plugin, one desktop,
and two standalone tools. Root Cargo.toml includes crates, plugins and desktop;
each tool declares its own workspace. bindings/README.md describes planned
How to read the inventory #
external normal dependencies. none means std-only at that crate boundary;
first-party only means no direct external normal dependency, not an assertion
Resolved transitive dependencies and runtime behavior are unverified here.
Source convention: for every row named X , purpose is taken from
crates/X/src/lib.rs:1 (first six lines), and dependency names from
crates/X/Cargo.toml [dependencies] . These two paths are the row's evidence.
apps/dctx-desktop/README.md:3 ; its lib header has no purpose description.
boundaries in docs/design/ARCHITECTURE-DECISIONS.md (DX-ARCH-01).
Shipped CLI path (v1) #
What the dctx binary ( crates/dctx-cli ) actually runs, as of v1. No refactor: the other crates stay in the workspace.
Shipped: dctx-cli and the crates/dctx facade session (index, find, grep, callers, callees, neighbors, skeleton, hubs, pack, read), with dctx-core (selection), dctx-hash, dctx-ports, dctx-pack, dctx-template, dctx-adapter-cache, dctx-adapter-fs (compatibility IO), dctx-map-model (records and rendering) and the dctx-lex-* extractors.
Request types only: dctx-map-query . The CLI imports Request , Verb , Direction , Format , AnswerBudget and EdgeKind ; its Index engine is never called.
Internal or legacy (compiled as dependencies of dctx-map-query , not run by the CLI): the dctx-map-query Index engine, dctx-map-store , dctx-map-scan , dctx-map-resolve , dctx-map-segment , dctx-adapter-store ; dctx-map-parse likewise. docs/SPEC-MAP-MODE.md sections 6–8 and 10 describe this engine.
Unstable (no stability promise in v1): dctx-plugin-host, dctx-plugin-platform, dctx-plugin-protocol, dctx-plugin-distribution and dctx-desktop-api. The default dctx-cli build enables the plugin runtime and the bundled Git plugin process; --no-default-features --features strict builds without them.

title: CLI exit codes

Document: `docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md` in [Documents](#documents). [Read the page](https://www.dctx.internet.technology/docs/exit-codes/).

Rendered text and page details not already verbatim in the document pack:

All documents Start What dctx is Choose your path Safe path in ten minutes Why dctx README and quick start Modalities Choosing how to use dctx CLI and agents: map mode Agent snippet MCP Libraries CI and caching Plugins guide Scopes Two scopes, one binary Who is responsible for what Engine Specification Privacy guarantees Cache and limits Language coverage (ADR-018) Template contract (DTS v2) Templating engine (ADR-003) Crate map Reference CLI reference CLI exit codes Languages Templates Examples Trust Benchmarks Measurement evidence Byte-stability report Earlier two-way study Philosophy Security policy Releasing Contributing Trademark Maintenance For AI evaluators Facts and verification llms.txt CLI exit codes View source · Edit on GitHub · Markdown · docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md · 1,017 words · updated 9 November 2026 On this page Details Outside the contract Engine RPC
dctx map , dctx pack , dctx context , dctx doctor , dctx rpc , dctx mcp , dctx languages , dctx cache , dctx template , a bare dctx without a terminal, an unknown command and a non-UTF-8 argument follow one contract:
dctx serve [PATH] and dctx serve --mcp [PATH] are aliases for dctx mcp [PATH] .
fixtures ; tools index paths relative to that directory. dctx read is an alias
for dctx map read , with the same flags and exit codes.
a find page, including one with no hits; --help
map read m:nope.py (an id not in the index); map read logo.png (a binary file); pack of a directory with no packable file
an unknown command or flag; a missing target ( dctx context with no TARGET); --depth 9 ; an empty find query; a stale --cursor ; m:../outside ; a non-UTF-8 argument; cache purge without --root / --all or --yes ; a template that does not compile; a bare dctx whose stdin or stdout is not a terminal
--place /no/such/dir ; a corrupt or busy cache; a source over DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES ; an --output file that cannot be written; template build /no/such/file (the message names the path)
Every failure prints two lines on stderr: [no] Error: <what went wrong> (prefixed with the command, as map: … ), then hint: <what to do next> . No input should reach a Rust panic; crates/dctx-cli/tests/cli_errors.rs and <repo>/scripts/checks/V1-5.zsh run twelve bad inputs and assert the code, the message, the hint and the absence of panicked .
Details #
An id the index does not hold is a facade outcome ( gone ), not an error. dctx map prints the gone page on stdout, then exits 1 with the hint. dctx mcp returns the same page to the client as a normal tool result.
An empty find or grep page is an answer and exits 0. Exit 1 is for a named target that is not there.
A binary target is detected before the scan: a NUL byte in the first 8 KiB of the file named by map , skeleton , explain or read (path or m: id). neighbors and path still accept such a module, since source files can import it.
dctx pack exits 1 only when no view filter is set ( --ext , --include , --exclude , --binary , --empty , --non-empty , --large , --small , --hidden , --debug-ignored ). A filter that matches nothing still prints an empty page and exits 0. The page (stdout) and the pack bytes=… status line (stderr) are printed before the exit-1 message. pack exit 3 covers source, scan, render and output failures.
A reader that closes stdout early ( dctx pack . | head -1 ) ends the run with exit 0 and no message, as cat does; every other failure keeps its code.
dctx pack --for <TEXT> exits 1 when no name in TEXT matched the index (the page is printed first), 2 for a bad flag or a --budget outside 100..100000 (or --budget without --for ), and 3 when PATH is not a directory or the index fails.
dctx mcp [--profile default|lean|three | --tools NAME,...] [PATH] exits 3 when PATH cannot be entered and 2 for invalid arguments (including unknown tool names/profiles). See the MCP guide . Once serving, a failed tool call goes back to the client as a result with isError: true ; unknown or unselected tools return JSON-RPC -32602 . The server exits 0 at end of input.
A facade refusal of the query ( InvalidRequest , BudgetTooSmall , StaleContinuation , Stale , UnsupportedCapability , UnsupportedVersion ) is 2; PolicyDenied and PolicyUnavailable are 1; every other facade error, and every error of the snapshot build, is 3. The mapping is dctx_cli::exit::from_facade .
map hubs , map path and map export report their facade errors as text: an unknown id end of map path is 1, anything else 3.
dctx context with no TARGET is 2; dctx context --help prints usage and exits 0. A TARGET that names nothing prints its empty page, then exits 1.
dctx cache exits 2 for a bad flag or value, a purge without --root PATH / --all or --yes , and a --max-bytes that would loosen the cap; 1 for a --root id the ledger does not hold; 3 when the cache directory, policy or ledger cannot be read or written (the message names the directory).
dctx template exits 2 for a bad flag and for a template that does not compile, and 3 when the template, the --dir directory or the --output file cannot be read or written (the message names the path). --output never writes through a symbolic link and refuses a target that is not a regular file.
dctx with no command opens the interactive menu only when stdin and stdout are terminals; otherwise it prints the short usage as a hint and exits 2.
dctx doctor follows the contract; dctx rpc keeps exit 0 at end of input (see Engine RPC below).
Outside the contract #
dctx plugin … and dctx git … return the plugin host's own codes.
Engine RPC #
dctx rpc uses the same operation paths and numeric taxonomy over
versioned NDJSON . Each reply carries engine_version
the same codes and hints as dctx cache status . An error reply does not change the server's process exit
pack --for TEXT --json now emits the facade's context JSON page; its text
member contains the same budgeted context page as plain pack --for TEXT .

Grep plus file reads #
The 11 November whole-session benchmark measured grep plus reads against dctx CLI and MCP: CLI median total tokens -5.01 %; the pre-registered 25 % savings rule was not met.

Historical three-way summary #
Run 7: dctx 140 of 140, Trail-Code 122, graphify 96 , with dctx using 29.3k tokens against Trail-Code's 88.9k and graphify's 197k. See "Run 7" below.
Run 5: dctx P 0.995 / R 0.851 (first page), R 0.968 following 5 pages. Run 1 below: dctx P 0.993 / R 0.461 (first page), P 0.995 / R 0.706 following up to 5 pages. Trail-Code P 0.986 / R 0.436, graphify P 0.989 / R 0.196. Per corpus, Trail-Code wins ripgrep and trailcode, and dctx wins flask and pocketbase. Before tonight dctx recall was 0.
dctx fastest on all 6 corpora : 0.16–1.16 s against 1.17–58.3 s for Trail-Code and 4.5–59 s for graphify. Peak RSS 19–90 MB against 121–1,020 MB and 74–394 MB.
dctx fastest on search, callers and skeleton everywhere: 44–226 ms against 0.98–1.9 s for Trail-Code and 0.38–1.4 s for graphify. graphify's overview is a 7 ms read of a pre-written file.
dctx map hubs gives the smallest overview on 4 of 6 corpora (Trail-Code on trailcode and docs) (30–652 tokens; Trail-Code 18–2,538; graphify 3,827–11,591). graphify gives the smallest callers and skeleton answers. dctx's skeleton is the largest of the three on ripgrep (1,784 tokens). Before tonight dctx's only overview was a 0.45–2.6 M-token pack .
dctx and Trail-Code tie. Both are byte-identical across runs, and after an unrelated edit only the overview changes. graphify changed find, skeleton and overview after update , and 1 of 6 ripgrep queries was not deterministic.
dctx and graphify made 0 socket attempts in every variant. Trail-Code made 49 blocked connect attempts when DO_NOT_TRACK is unset, and 0 with it set.
Symbols: dctx 10 of 10, Trail-Code 7, graphify 5. Call edges, run 3: dctx 10 of 10, Trail-Code 7, graphify 5 (run 1: dctx 0). dctx's new outline tier is symbols only, labelled guess . Terraform and SQL get symbols only from dctx.

Method #
latencies are noisy. Every measured command ran as nice -n 10 taskset -c 24-31 unshare -Urn env -i … , with no
network, scratch HOME and caches, and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 . One heavy process ran at a time. The network audit is a
Corpora are pinned by SHA in research/bench-3way-20261030/corpora-shas.json : flask 3.1.3, ripgrep 15.2.0,
Tokens are ceil(stdout_bytes / 3.5) for every tool. That is an estimate, not a tokenizer.
The callers gold set is the regex oracle of the October protocol ( goldlib.py ) on 20 seeded targets per corpus.
Query mapping: dctx map find / map neighbors --dir in --edge calls / map skeleton / map hubs .
Trail-Code ask / callers / skeleton / map . graphify query / affected --relation calls /
explain <file> / GRAPH_REPORT.md .
Not claimed #
Whole-session cost or task-level answer quality from these historical protocols. Historical fact scores describe raw tool outputs only; the 11 November study measures whole sessions with a frozen model.
Changes included in the October baseline #
Call and import edges ( 19e90a1 ), byte-stable answers ( ce18608 ), .env omission in pack ( 6d4deec ),
outline symbols for 25 formats and plain-text sections ( 9c61ac9 , e0821e3 , 839bd45 , a32dad3 ),
neighbors depth 4 ( 0de5ce1 ), hubs ( 6bc0cbc ), grep ( 5691234 ), skeleton ( 2243c38 ), path ( 670e9e3 ),
export ( ac8408c ), dctx mcp ( 50bbce4 ) and a 1 GiB source ceiling ( 5d26781 ). Each feature's focused check, and
then all 15 checks together on ac8408c , passed on the Linux benchmark host before the benchmark ran.

Each prefix is copied in full using git ls-tree -r --name-only <pin> -- <prefix>
and git show <pin>:<path> , retaining paths relative to the prefix. Every file's
size and SHA-256, and the CLI binary SHA-256, are in corpora.json .
Work copies and isolated cache/config directories live in a disposable /tmp
The original applicable map query shapes are retained: find --limit 10 , inbound
neighbors --edge calls at depths 1 and 2, outbound neighbors, map --depth 2
--limit 40 , read , and explain . Each now runs in both formats. The current
bounded skeleton , grep , hubs , and path verbs add four shapes per corpus,
find --json --limit 40 , matching exact path and symbol. path tests a file's
containment edge to that symbol. grep is confined to the target file.
Default budgets and default output are used, without --meta in the measured
after appending exactly \n// STAB-01 unrelated comment\n to the named unrelated
search hits or hub counts. Original bytes are restored in a finally block and
verified. Configuration and caches are isolated using XDG_CONFIG_HOME ,
XDG_CACHE_HOME and DCTX_CACHE_DIR ; inherited DCTX_* overrides are removed.
helper and Add . Their empty answers are included. All three inbound-neighbor
cases have records, all paths are found, and render_answer_at has nine returned
followed. Whole-graph export has no unrelated graph input and is outside this
M7 and acceptance limits #
For each transition, M7 = longest common byte prefix of previous and current
stdout / current stdout byte length. Both block lengths and the prefix length
are stored in turn-prefixes.csv ; there are no empty blocks.
tier-context M7 ≥ 0.9 gate. Tier layering remains target . No cross-platform,
The three text read pages actually include their selected source bodies. Text
explain still consists of header and id/kind/path, so §11's richer text-page

export PATH = $HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH
export CARGO_TARGET_DIR = $PWD/.target-stab
cargo --offline build --locked -p dctx-cli > /tmp/stab-01-build.log 2 > & 1
Exit 101 : configured sccache failed with Operation not permitted , before
compilation. A retry after unset RUSTC_WRAPPER , with output redirected to
/tmp/stab-01-build-no-wrapper.log , also exited 101 : Cargo's user config still
specified build.rustc-wrapper = "sccache" .

and one synthetic adversarial corpus. Every number below comes from data/raw/*.jsonl and can be

dctx at commit 17dff0b454c24f43848abad1c88ea982e02731f7 (branch internal ), dctx-cli v0.25.0 ,
agent interface dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read> .
Trail-Code @trailhq/trail-code@0.23.1 from npm (repository HEAD b1211efd , whose
package.json is also 0.23.1), CLI trail plus its MCP server.
1. Summary #
Trail-Code wins decisively. Trail precision 0.94 to 1.00, recall 0.10 to 0.96 per corpus. dctx returns no call or import edges at all (recall 0 on 140 targets): the CLI facade only emits contains edges.
dctx wins. One 9.2 MB binary (libc, libm, libgcc_s) versus 405.6 MB of node_modules (8,567 files, 50 package versions) plus a Node runtime.
dctx wins on all seven corpora: 0.09 to 6.05 s versus 2.44 to 94.9 s (2.8 to 69 times faster); peak RSS 8 to 567 MiB versus 181 to 2,111 MiB. Trail's index is smaller only on core (65 MB versus 158 MB).
dctx wins on small and medium repos (30 to 260 ms versus 0.6 to 1.4 s; Node startup sets Trail's floor near 0.6 s). On the largest Rust corpus dctx re-reads a 158 MB generation per process (1.45 s, 370 MiB per query) and Trail's callers is faster (0.83 s).
Tie on correctness : both see unstaged, untracked and staged edits and drop reverted symbols. Trail also adds the caller edge to the new function; dctx cannot. dctx's first query after an edit costs a full re-index (core: 7.5 s), and every edit adds a full new generation to the cache (core: 158 MB to 946 MB).
Trail wins. Trail text outputs are byte-identical across runs and across unrelated edits. Every dctx answer starts with a header containing the snapshot digest, so any edit anywhere changes byte 21 to 50 of every answer; dctx JSON is never byte-identical twice ( age_s ).
dctx wins for map verbs (hard 2,000-token cap, never exceeded; budgets below the minimum record size are refused with exit 1). Trail has no budget flag; single answers reached 142 KB (40.6k tokens). dctx's legacy tree and pack are unbounded (974 KB tree on django; 8.7 MB pack).
dctx wins. Zero sockets in every audited dctx run and no writes to the repository in map mode. Trail does a daily npm version check that ignores DO_NOT_TRACK , records an install telemetry event in postinstall and tries to send it, and modifies .gitignore and adds .ignore on every trail build . dctx pack printed a fake .env secret; Trail never read .env .
Host, isolation, contention #
VM build-host : 32 vCPU Intel Xeon E5-2680 v2 @ 2.80 GHz, 94 GB RAM, Debian 13, kernel
6.12.111, Node v24.22.0, npm 11.19.1, rustc/cargo 1.99.0 ( data/env.txt ).
taskset -c 24-31 (8 CPUs). The other batch was not pinned, so it could share those CPUs.
(each row in data/raw/*runs.jsonl records load before and after; phases.jsonl records each phase).
The ripgrep and pocketbase query phases ran at load 8 to 10, so treat their Trail find times
Both tools ran as the dedicated unprivileged user dctxbench , with HOME , npm prefix, npm cache,
XDG_CACHE_HOME and DCTX_CACHE_DIR inside /path/to/workdir/dctx-vs-trail , through scripts/benv
( env -i , then sudo -u dctxbench unshare -rn , then taskset ). After installs, clones and builds,
DO_NOT_TRACK=1 (Trail's documented opt-out, dist/telemetry/gate.js ) was set for every measured
Timing: GNU time 1.9 ( /usr/bin/time -v , 10 ms resolution) records wall, user+sys CPU and peak RSS for
Output size: raw stdout bytes and ceil(bytes / 3.5) estimated tokens for both tools (identical to
dctx's own ceil(2*bytes/7) ). This is an estimate, not a tokenizer.

sha256 26c3cb70...cbce . ldd : libgcc_s , libm , libc , ld-linux only.

Trail's own postinstall and node-gyp builds; Node headers were downloaded into ~/.cache/node-gyp ).

Gold sets and scoring #
Targets. scripts/select_targets.py picks 20 definitions per corpus with a fixed seed: 4 hubs
scripts/goldlib.py , not either tool.
Oracle. Comments and strings are blanked (a cross-line state machine for Rust and Go, per-line for
JS/TS, triple-quote aware for Python). A line is a call site of N only if N is directly followed by an
file or package, explicit import, self / this , Type:: ); receiver calls to names that also exist on
standard-library types, and anything else unresolvable, are ambiguous and excluded from both
in-repo definition of the name, plus self calls.
Adjudication. A Trail calls hit is a true positive if its span contains a gold site of the target,
listed in data/targets/*.targets.json ). The hand check found one oracle bug: a /* inside a Rust
multi-line doc string started a fake block comment. After the fix the gold was rebuilt for the same
targets ( scripts/regold.py ; one target changed, ripgrep unwrap_switch , 61 to 69 sites), and the ripgrep
accuracy and task phases were rerun. The earlier rows are kept in data/raw/*.pre-regold . A remaining
one true Trail hit (flask dumps ) count as a false positive.
Tasks. scripts/phase_tasks.py builds 10 questions per corpus from the same oracle with fixed

- core's dctx cost is dominated by configuration extraction. --profile on a cold run: parse/lex 3.39 s,

5. Query latency and output size (section 3 and 4) #
find = dctx map find N --limit 10 / trail ask N ; callers = dctx map neighbors <id> --dir in --edge calls
/ trail callers N ; outline = dctx map map FILE --depth 2 --limit 40 / trail skeleton FILE ;
read = dctx map read <id> --json / trail ask N --source --full -n 1 ; overview = legacy dctx . -t
(the map verbs have no root overview, TC-F05) / trail map ; grep = none / trail grep 'N\(' .
0.83 / 1,366
0.81 / 1,196
dctx text mode is thin: find prints id kind path without line numbers, and read / explain in text
mode print only the id line (152 to 247 bytes, no source and no signature). Source needs --json
dctx --json repeats thirteen keys per record, many of them null . Under the same default budget a
JSON find returned 4 records where the text find returned 10 (flask, dispatch_request ).
pocketbase 0.72 s, trailcode 0.31 s ( data/queries_cold_dctx.csv ). Trail cannot answer without a graph
("no graph found ... run trail build first"), so its cold first answer is the cold build plus a query.
Trail prepends a banner to callers , skeleton , grep , map and source answers. The banner estimates
call, 6.3% of all Trail warm-query bytes and 54% of the callees answers.

7. Call-graph and definition accuracy (section 5) #
Interface/trait targets are scored at name level separately. Per-target rows: data/accuracy_targets.csv .

Def in results: dctx / Trail ask
dctx has no call graph in the shipped CLI. neighbors --edge calls returned empty on all 140
targets; --edge imports on module ids was also empty in spot checks (ripgrep, pocketbase). The lexers do extract references (for example
EdgeKind::Calls in dctx-lex-* , dctx-map-parse/src/adapters/rust.rs ), but the facade index
( crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs ) only emits contains edges, and dctx-map-resolve is linked only
through dctx-map-query .

variables (pocketbase Record.Verified , 0 of 39; Record.ValidatePassword , 0 of 36); Python methods
called on module-level objects ( apps.get_app_configs() , 3 of 69); calls through a re-exported module
name ( flask.abort(...) , 2 of 22); classmethods called on subclasses ( Index.as_view(...) , 0 of 20).

Trail ask ) and listed it in 139/140 first pages versus 109/140. Trail callers N also lists every

15. Where dctx wins / where Trail-Code wins / ties #
- Privacy: no sockets in any run; no repository or home writes in map mode; .gitignore honoured even
without .git ; gitignored secrets never indexed.
- Finding definitions: rank 1 in 103/140 cases versus 79/140 for trail ask .
- Cheap no-op verification (0.04 to 1.34 s) versus trail build --check (2 to 86 s).
- Text search ( trail grep , grouped by enclosing symbol) and a bounded repository map (1 to 15k tokens).
- On the largest Rust corpus, warm callers and skeleton are faster than dctx (0.8 s versus 1.45 s) with
- Neither follows symlink loops or escaping symlinks; both skip node_modules/ and non-UTF-8 file names;
16. Findings #
Evidence: neighbors --edge calls empty for 140 of 140 targets across seven corpora ( data/accuracy.csv );
--edge imports empty on module ids in spot checks; Trail precision 0.94 to 1.00 and recall up to 0.96 on the same gold.
callees and 6/14 on colliding names. The facade ( crates/dctx/src/index/extract.rs ) only emits contains
edges, although the lexers already produce Calls / Imports references and dctx-map-resolve exists.
Recommendation: wire reference facts from the lexers through dctx-map-resolve into the facade segment,
with explicit confidence ( exact , name , guess ) on every edge and a record of dropped ambiguous
instead of adding a type checker. Use scripts/phase_accuracy.py as the acceptance test.
generations were byte-identical; cache gc --dry-run reclaimed 0 bytes ( unlink_grace ). Total cache
Evidence: every map answer starts with # <place> <verb> v1:sha256:<digest>:<bytes> g=<n> , so any edit
anywhere changes byte 21 to 50 of every answer ( data/stability.csv , 0 of 63 dctx answers unchanged after
an unrelated edit versus 59 of 70 for Trail). JSON answers contain freshness.age_s , so no two JSON calls
Evidence: dctx map read <id> and explain <id> in text mode print only the id line (152 to 247 bytes,
no source, no signature); find text has no line numbers; JSON carries thirteen keys per record, often
null , so a default-budget JSON find returned 4 records versus 10 in text.
Recommendation: print source for read and the signature and summary for explain in text mode; add
path:start-end to text records; drop null keys from JSON v2 (or add a compact JSON).
Evidence: dctx map map p:<place> and k:<dir> answer gone , and directories are refused ("is a
directory; pass a file path or a stable id"), although the guide says map outlines "the project root".
The only overview is the legacy dctx . -t : 974 KB (278k tokens) on django, written into the repository
as .dctx/<place>.llmcontext.txt , and it fails on trees deeper than 128. Trail's map answered in 1.7 to
Recommendation: implement map p: and directory targets as a budgeted overview (directories, file
counts, top symbols by in-degree once TC-F01 lands), paging through next , written to stdout only.
Evidence: config-key questions scored 0/14 for dctx and 14/14 for Trail ( trail grep ).
Recommendation: add a bounded dctx map grep verb in the core (pure Rust, same ignore rules, no Git),
grouped by enclosing symbol id and capped by --budget with a continuation cursor.
as opaque in the precision label, and load only the segment parts a query touches instead of the whole
TC-F08 (major, privacy): dctx pack emits .env contents by default.
Evidence: dctx pack . printed DCTXBENCH_FAKE_SECRET=sk-test-... from a non-gitignored .env
( data/raw/adversarial.jsonl , both variants). Map answers and the map cache did not contain it. Trail
never read .env .
Recommendation: ship a default sensitive-content omit list ( .env* , *.pem , *.key , id_* ,
credentials* , *.p12 ) that shows the path but never reads the content unless the user opts in. This
Evidence: --budget 20 and JSON --budget 100 exit 1 ("budget too small: needs at least 336 bytes").
Recommendation: return the largest prefix that fits (ids only, then more / next ), or clamp to the floor
100 bytes, header only); Trail ask found the target in 6 of 7.
Recommendation: split queries and identifiers on case and _ boundaries, rank by token overlap with names
and first-line doc summaries (already present as summary ), all in the core without models.
Evidence: cargo tree -p dctx-cli -e normal lists 46 external crates, including rusqlite with bundled
SQLite C, ed25519-dalek , landlock , seccompiler , serde_json and syn 3, all compiled into the
release build ( target/release/deps ). The binary itself only needs libc, libm and libgcc_s at run time.
TC-F12 (minor, docs): docs/guides/MAP-MODE.md and --version --verbose are stale.
Evidence: the guide says .gitignore rules are not loaded and --lines drops the start line; observed:
gitignored files are excluded on the map path even without .git , and --lines 240-246 returned exactly
lines 240 to 246. The guide says map outlines the project root (it does not, TC-F05) and that the default
CLI extracts "conservative calls" (none are exposed, TC-F01). dctx --version --verbose lists
languages: rust,javascript,typescript,markdown and parser dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9 , while answers report
dctx-structural/1 and Python, Go and others work.
Recommendation: count omitted paths by reason in precision (for example omitted: {binary: 1,
unnamed: 2} ) so an agent knows the map is incomplete.
DO_NOT_TRACK and an install-time telemetry event; no repository writes versus .gitignore / .ignore
to the user (~89 tokens per call, 54% of callees output). It is prompt steering inside tool output and it
dctx cache status or a JSON field the caller can drop.
Evidence: trail build --check 49.5 s on pocketbase and 86.5 s on django, the same as cold builds;
TC-F18 (info): Trail indexes gitignored files when .git is absent.
Evidence: in the no-git adversarial variant, Trail indexed ignored_dir/ and app.secret.py ; the fake
secret value appeared in graft/.cache/extract.*.json and trail grep output. dctx excluded both.
17. Not tested, and deviations #
Trail build --deep (needs an LLM key) and --lsp (no language servers installed on the host);
trail blast , check , note , team , viz and the learnings features; Trail cloud workspaces.
dctx plugins, TUI, templates and the optional syntax-rust build.
Deviation: DO_NOT_TRACK was not set during npm install , so Trail's postinstall recorded an install
scripts; the other corpora ran in one chained pass ( data/raw/phases.jsonl ).
18. Reproducing #
On a Linux host with passwordless sudo: scripts/setup_host.sh (user, workspace, dctx build, pinned
Trail install, pinned clones). Copy scripts/ to $BENCH_ROOT/scripts .
scripts/run_all.sh runs every phase. Each phase script appends JSONL under $BENCH_ROOT/results .
python3 scripts/aggregate.py RESULTS data/ regenerates data/*.csv and data/SUMMARY-TABLES.md .
For a private corpus, run scripts/redact_private.py data/ <corpus> before publishing.
Cleanup: sudo userdel -r dctxbench && sudo rm -rf /path/to/workdir && sudo apt-get remove -y time strace .
Data index #
data/env.txt , data/tool-help.txt
host, versions, pins, binary hash, ldd , CLI help of both tools
data/raw/runs.jsonl and *_runs.jsonl

Bugs, ideas and questions #
Search existing issues before opening
Report suspected vulnerabilities privately using SECURITY.md ,
CLI development setup #
CI tests use DCTX_CI_RUST from tools/release/toolchain.env ; bump it intentionally each Rust release.
Cargo builds dctx-cli , while help text calls the tool dctx . See
installation for aliases and install choices.
dctx facade serves the CLI and the desktop API; pure engine
plugin guide describes effect boundaries and current
the website setup , then run
tools/website/.venv/bin/python tools/check-markdown-links.py . It checks local
Testing documents the full Linux/macOS/Windows matrix and
local commands. The current CI workflow runs workspace
licence, website and release checks. Run cargo fmt --all -- --check and document
public APIs. Follow Rust house style for the plugin boundaries.
When editing website source documents, regenerate website/ and check it using
the website instructions . Before committing, use
check.py --working-tree to compare your regenerated files with an independent
the desktop guide . The root just ci recipe also
Developer Certificate of Origin #
Contributions use the Developer Certificate of Origin
The -s flag adds a Signed-off-by: line with your name and email. Pull requests with
unsigned commits will be asked to amend them with git commit --amend -s , or to rebase
with --signoff .
Pull requests #
Create a focused branch from main and describe the problem, resulting behavior
editing guides. Use clear commit messages, for example fix(cli): reject empty
output paths .

Reference CLI reference
Captured from dctx 1.3.1 when this site was built; a check fails the build when the binary prints anything else. Help text is shown verbatim, so it is the CLI's own wording, including the legacy snapshot options it still lists.
What the output looks like #
These are real runs on the tiny kiosk sample , captured by capture.py from the release binary. Commands run inside a copy named kiosk . For source builds, the executable is dctx-cli (or define a dctx alias).
Pack a project #
The header explains the format, the tree assigns IDs, and file blocks carry paths and line counts. The first 40 output lines follow; only the tail is omitted. .env is listed without its contents.
$ dctx pack .
[DCTX_LLM_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_V1]
[DIRECTORY:kiosk]
<INSTRUCTIONS >
1. Manifest: The <DIRECTORY_TREE > section lists all files.
- Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH (ID:UNIQUE_ID)
- TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file.
2. Content Access: To read a specific file:
- Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree.
- Search for the marker: <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "UNIQUE_ID" >
- The content is between this marker and </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "UNIQUE_ID" >
</INSTRUCTIONS >
<DIRECTORY_TREE >
[D] (ID:ROOT)
[F] .env (ID:F001)
[F] .gitignore (ID:F002)
[F] Cargo.toml (ID:F003)
[F] README.md (ID:F004)
[F] config.toml (ID:F005)
[D] src (ID:D006)
[F] src/main.rs (ID:F007)
[F] src/store.rs (ID:F008)
[F] src/util.rs (ID:F009)
[D] tools (ID:D010)
[F] tools/report.py (ID:F011)
[D] web (ID:D012)
[F] web/app.ts (ID:F013)
[F] web/format.ts (ID:F014)
</DIRECTORY_TREE >
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F001" PATH = ".env" LINES = "0" >
[Content omitted by pattern rules]
</FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F001" >
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F002" PATH = ".gitignore" LINES = "2" >
target /
</FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F002" >
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F003" PATH = "Cargo.toml" LINES = "9" >
[package]
name = "kiosk"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"
… (147 more lines)
Find a symbol, then read it #
Pass the exact ID from find to read to get its metadata and verified source bytes:
$ dctx map find greet
# kiosk find
s:src/util.rs#greet fn L 2 - 4
s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting fn L 10 - 12
$ dctx map read 's:src/util.rs#greet'
# kiosk read
s:src/util.rs#greet fn src/util.rs
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}
For structured consumption, --json puts the same source bytes in source_utf8 (one JSON line, shown verbatim):
$ dctx map read 's:src/util.rs#greet' --json
{ "v" : 2 , "place" : "kiosk" , "verb" : "read" , "freshness" :{ "mode" : "strict" , "state" : "verified" }, "precision" :{ "coverage" : "syntax" , "completion" : "complete" , "parser" : "dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9" }, "records" :[{ "id" : "s:src/util.rs#greet" , "kind" : "fn" , "path" : "src/util.rs" , "lines" :[ 2 , 4 ], "summary" : "The greeting shown on the kiosk screen." , "summary_source" : "doc" , "signature" : null , "span" :[ 44 , 126 ], "source_utf8" : "pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {\n format!(\"Hello, {}!\", title_case(name))\n}" , "edge" : null , "direction" : null , "target" : null , "confidence" : null }], "more" : 0 , "next" : null }
Pack for a task #
--for uses the task terms to select find results, neighbors and source reads. --budget 800 bounds estimated output tokens, not scan size; the footer reports usage and dropped records.
$ dctx pack . --for 'greet store' --budget 800
# dctx pack --for budget = 800 terms = 2
## find greet
s:src/util.rs#greet fn L 2 - 4
s:web/app.ts#renderGreeting fn L 10 - 12
## find store
s:src/store.rs#Order struct L 4 - 8
s:src/store.rs#checksum fn L 22 - 24
s:src/store.rs#encode fn L 17 - 19
## neighbors s:src/util.rs#greet
calls:in:s:src/main.rs#main fn src/main.rs L 7
calls:out:s:src/util.rs#title_case fn src/util.rs
contains:in:m:src/util.rs module src/util.rs
## neighbors s:src/store.rs#Order
contains:in:m:src/store.rs module src/store.rs
## read s:src/util.rs#greet
s:src/util.rs#greet fn src/util.rs
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}
## read s:src/store.rs#Order
s:src/store.rs#Order struct src/store.rs
pub struct Order {
pub id: u 32 ,
pub item: String,
pub qty: u 32 ,
}
# end body_tokens = 223 budget = 800 dropped = 0

dctx languages [ --json | --markdown ]
dctx doctor [ --json ]
dctx agent-setup [ --format claude|agents|plain]
dctx cache status [ --json ] [ --root PATH ]
dctx cache gc [ --dry-run ] [ --root PATH ] [ --max-bytes N]
dctx cache purge --root PATH [ --dry-run ] [ --yes ]
dctx cache purge --all [ --dry-run ] [ --yes ]
dctx cache config [auto on|off] [ --max-bytes N] [ --ttl-days N]
dctx cache auto [ --json ]
dctx template build <PATH> [ --output PATH ]
dctx template list [ --dir PATH ]
dctx plugin search|install|list|info|enable|disable|remove|update|verify
dctx git <status|protect>
`dctx languages` lists every supported language with its tier: full (symbols and call edges), outline (symbols only) or docs (sections).
`dctx rpc` serves the versioned engine protocol for language packages (send hello first; docs/protocol/ README .md).
`dctx mcp` serves the map verbs as MCP tools over stdio ( JSON - RPC 2 .0, one message per line) for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
`dctx serve` and `dctx serve --mcp` use that same server; `dctx read` uses `dctx map read` .
Explicit `dctx pack` writes stdout, the clipboard, or `--output` . It does not create a project text file.
`dctx pack --for <TEXT>` prints task context for an agent card instead: map find, neighbors and read of the names in TEXT , cut to `--budget` estimated tokens (default 3000 ).
`dctx plugin list` and `dctx --help` do not create a project `.dctx/` directory or start a plugin.
`dctx git` routes to the bundled dctx /git plugin. It is not a Git passthrough.
Cache purge requires `--root PATH` or `--all` , and `--yes` unless `--dry-run` is set.
`dctx cache config` shows the persisted policy. `auto on|off` enables auto-clean, `--max-bytes` tightens the system cap, and `--ttl-days` sets idle overlay and preview lifetime.
`dctx cache auto` prints the last auto-clean time, the bytes it reclaimed and the next due time.
`dctx doctor` lists visible binaries, ownership scopes, SHA -256 checksums and cache sizes without changing the cache or using the network.
`dctx agent-setup` prints concise rules to paste into CLAUDE .md or AGENTS .md (default: agents).
pack, map, template, plugin and the TUI run one bounded auto-clean when it is due. They print nothing unless bytes were reclaimed.
`--no-auto-clean` and `DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0` disable that slice. `DCTX_CACHE_DIR` selects the cache parent; indexes live in its engine-major.minor subdirectory. General Options verbatim Copy -h , --help Show help
-v , --version Show version
--verbose With --version , also show executable path, scope and limits
Run `dctx pack --help` for pack options and filters. Template Commands verbatim Copy template build <PATH> Compile a template through the facade
template list List explicit compiled plans; no home-directory scan Examples verbatim Copy dctx pack . Pack to stdout and write no project text file
dctx pack . --output out.txt
dctx languages --json
dctx cache status --json
dctx cache gc --dry-run
dctx cache purge --root /path --dry-run
dctx cache config auto off --max-bytes 1000000 --ttl-days 7
dctx cache auto
dctx template build policy.dctx_template Feature and precision limits verbatim Copy facade_version: 1 .3.1
profile: enhanced
wire_version: 2
segment_version: 1
storage: buffered-segments
features: pack,map,templates,fs,segments,cache,syntax-rust
parsers: dctx -structural/3,dctx-lex-js:1,dctx-lex-md:1,dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9
languages: rust,javascript,typescript,python,go,java,c,csharp,kotlin,ruby,php,swift,web,scala,dart,zig,solidity,gleam,fortran,perl,groovy,powershell,elixir,lua,ocaml,r,julia,haskell,erlang,verilog,hcl,sql,clojure,lisp,scheme,elisp,config,shell,make,docker,proto,pascal,graphql,nix,markdown,text,rst,asciidoc,org,tex
unsafe_boundary: syn-dependency
native_code: false
git: false
subprocess: none
precision: the structural extractor reports declarations, imports, headings and conservative calls.
It does not promise exact semantic calls, name or type resolution, or macro expansion.
A syntax-rust build adds syn for supported Rust syntax only, still without type checking.
token estimate: ceil(2 * UTF -8 bytes / 7 ) is an estimate, not a tokenizer guarantee.
cache cap: 2 GiB hard, 1 .5 GiB soft watermark, 1 .2 GiB eviction target.
cache ttl: idle overlays and previews 7 days, unpinned roots 30 days, staging 1 day.
auto-clean interval: 1 day.
dctx map --help
verbatim Copy Usage: dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read|skeleton|grep> <TARGET> [ OPTIONS ]
dctx trace <A> <B> [ --max-depth 1..16 ] [ --max-paths 1..100 ] [ --max-bytes 256..1048576 ] [ --json ]
dctx impact <SYMBOL> [ --max-depth 1..16 ] [ --max-sites 1..10000 ] [ --max-bytes 256..1048576 ] [ --json ]
dctx map hubs [ --limit N] [ --json ] [ --place PATH ] [ --budget TOKENS ] [ --meta ]
Most-called symbols (incoming calls and imports, 1..60 lines, default 20 ) and per-directory file and symbol counts. No TARGET .
dctx map path <FROM> <TO> [ --json ] [ --place PATH ] [ --budget TOKENS ] [ --meta ]
Shortest edge path (calls, imports, contains; either direction; at most 8 hops), one `edge:out|in<TAB>id<TAB>kind<TAB>path` line per hop, or `no path` .
dctx map export [ --format json|mermaid] [ --output PATH ] [ --place PATH ]
The whole graph as one deterministic document (default json: nodes and edges; mermaid: a flowchart of calls and imports). No TARGET , no token cap; --output writes a file.
TARGET Required. map accepts a stable id or a place-relative file.
skeleton takes a file (or m:<path>) and prints its declaration signatures, no bodies,
in source order: id, kind, L<start>-<end>, signature.
A file path is read as m:<path>. Omitting TARGET does not scan.
--json Facade JSON v2, including the precision label
--also DIR Add a read-only root (repeatable); paths and ids carry directory labels
--place PATH Place or worktree root (default: current directory)
--meta Restore the snapshot digest and generation in the text header and the snapshot, generation and age_s JSON fields.
Without it the answer bytes do not change across unrelated edits or time.
--profile Stderr stage timings and the five slowest files. DCTX_PROFILE = 1 is the same switch.
DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES Env: total source bytes one scan may read, 1..17179869184 (default 1073741824 = 1 GiB).
DCTX_MAX_RECORDS Env: files, symbols and edges one index may hold, 1..100000000 (default 1000000 ). A bigger place is refused while it is scanned.
DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES Env: files and directories one scan may visit, 1..100000000 (default 100000 ).
DCTX_FRESHNESS Env: strict_live hashes every file on a warm start; the default (stamp) trusts a file whose size, mtime and inode are unchanged and older than 2 s.
--budget TOKENS Output tokens, 1..2000 (explain max: 1000 ).
Read with no --budget uses the 2 ,000-token hard cap.
--depth N Map: 1..3 ; neighbors: 1..4 . Explain and read take no depth.
--limit N Map, find and neighbors page size. Explain and read accept only 1 .
--offset N Refused. Pass the previous page's next value to --cursor .
--cursor TOKEN Opaque continuation. A stale token is rejected.
--kind fn,type,doc Find kinds
--in PATH Find or grep within a relative path
grep LITERAL Exhaustive literal search of indexed files, hits grouped by enclosing symbol
-i , --ignore-case Grep: ASCII case-insensitive match
--edge calls,imports Neighbor edge filter
--dir in|out|both Neighbor direction
--lines A-B --full Read those absolute source lines inside the node; full permits 400
--rev SHA Refused: this build does not link git
Precision: structural declarations, imports, headings and conservative calls.
Not exact semantic calls, type resolution or macro expansion.
Token estimate ceil(2 * UTF -8 bytes / 7 ) is not a tokenizer guarantee.
Example: dctx map find 'ignore rules' --json
Example: dctx map map crates/dctx-cli/src/main.rs --depth 2
Example: dctx map map m:crates/dctx-cli/src/main.rs --cursor '<next from the previous page>'
Each verb's own page and example: dctx map <verb> --help
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 no result (an id not in the index, a binary file), 2 usage, 3 index error; see docs/ CLI - EXIT - CODES .md.

Outline of a file (m:<path> or a place-relative path) or a symbol and what it contains.
Example: dctx map map src/lib.rs --depth 2

dctx languages
verbatim Copy Usage: dctx languages [ --json | --markdown ]
Lists every language the map index recognises: name, tag, file names, tier and symbol confidence.
Tiers: full = symbols and call edges (lexical, not type-resolved); outline = symbols only, no call edges promised;
docs = headed sections. Confidence `guess` marks heuristic outlines, whose records carry confidence `guess` .
Options:
--json One JSON document with the tiers and the languages
--markdown The README language table
-h , --help Show this help
Example: dctx languages --json
50 languages: 36 full, 8 outline, 6 docs. The table with every tag and file name is on /languages/ .
Environment variables
Variable Help text Printed by DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES Env: total source bytes one scan may read, 1..17179869184 (default 1073741824 = 1 GiB). dctx map --help DCTX_MAX_RECORDS DCTX_MAX_RECORDS Env: files, symbols and edges one index may hold, 1..100000000 (default 1000000). A bigger place is refused while it is scanned. dctx map --help DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES Env: files and directories one scan may visit, 1..100000000 (default 100000). dctx map --help DCTX_FRESHNESS DCTX_FRESHNESS Env: strict_live hashes every file on a warm start; the default (stamp) trusts a file whose size, mtime and inode are unchanged and older than 2 s. dctx map --help DCTX_CACHE_DIR --no-auto-clean and DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0 disable that slice. DCTX_CACHE_DIR selects the cache parent; indexes live in its engine-major.minor subdirectory. dctx --help DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN --no-auto-clean and DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0 disable that slice. DCTX_PROFILE=1 is the same switch. dctx map --help
Exit codes
CLI-EXIT-CODES.md · full contract Code Meaning Examples 0 ok: the command answered a find page, including one with no hits; --help 1 no result: the command ran, but the named target or input has no answer map read m:nope.py (an id not in the index); map read logo.png (a binary file); pack of a directory with no packable file 2 usage: the arguments are wrong an unknown command or flag; a missing target ( dctx context with no TARGET); --depth 9 ; an empty find query; a stale --cursor ; m:../outside ; a non-UTF-8 argument; cache purge without --root / --all or --yes ; a template that does not compile; a bare dctx whose stdin or stdout is not a terminal 3 index error: the place, source, cache or index could not be opened, read, built or written --place /no/such/dir ; a corrupt or busy cache; a source over DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES ; an --output file that cannot be written; template build /no/such/file (the message names the path)
MCP tools
dctx mcp answers tools/list with 13 tools (captured over stdio; * marks a required argument). The full exchange .
Tool Description Arguments map Map file/directory symbols and relations. target * string Node id or relative file path. depth integer Levels, 1..3. limit integer budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean find Find definitions by name or words; use read context=true for source and callers. query * string kind array fn, method, struct, enum, trait, impl, const, type, macro, class, interface, symbol, module, package, place, doc, test. in string limit integer budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean neighbors Follow calls/imports by node id; dir=in finds callers. id * string Node id from find/map. edge array dir string in, out, both. depth integer Hops, 1..4. limit integer budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean explain Show a node signature, location and relations. id * string budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean read Read source/lines. context=true locates a name/file and includes source plus callers/imports. id * string Node id; context also accepts names/files. lines string Absolute lines A-B within the node. full boolean Allow 400 lines. context boolean Source + callers/imports. session string Context session id. dedupe boolean Reference prior session chunks. budget integer Source 1..2000 (default 2000); context 100..100000 (default 3000). cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean hubs Rank called symbols and count files/symbols by directory. limit integer budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. json boolean grep Search indexed files literally, grouped by symbol. query * string ignore_case boolean in string limit integer budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean skeleton List file/directory signatures without bodies. target * string Node id or relative file path. budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. json boolean path Find a shortest undirected graph path (up to 8 hops). from * string to * string meta boolean budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. cursor string Resume previous next. json boolean trace Trace shortest directed call/reference paths between names or ids. from * string to * string max_depth integer Hops, 1..16. max_paths integer Paths, 1..100. max_bytes integer Output bytes, 256..1048576. also array Read-only roots (up to 16). json boolean impact Find direct reference sites and transitive callers by name or id. symbol * string max_depth integer Caller depth, 1..16. max_sites integer Sites/callers, 1..10000. max_bytes integer Output bytes, 256..1048576. also array Read-only roots (up to 16). json boolean export Export the whole graph as JSON or Mermaid (unbounded). format * string json or mermaid. budget integer Tokens, 1..2000. pack Get task context: definitions, callers/imports and source in one bounded call. task * string budget integer Tokens, 100..100000. json boolean
Token estimate
Every byte and token count on this site uses the estimate dctx itself prints:
verbatim Copy token estimate: ceil(2 * UTF -8 bytes / 7 ) is an estimate, not a tokenizer guarantee.

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/languages/
title: Languages
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/languages/
---

Reference Languages
50 language families in three tiers: 36 full, 8 outline and 6 documentation formats. The table is the output of dctx languages --markdown , captured from dctx 1.3.1.
dctx languages prints this table ( --json for tools, --markdown for this block) from the one registry that also drives dctx --version --verbose ; a test fails when the block below differs from it.
full : symbols and call edges. Call edges are lexical, not type-resolved: they come from names, scopes and imports, never from a type checker, and ambiguous references are dropped.
outline : symbols only; no call edges are promised. Shell function bodies can yield same-file call guesses, but v1 does not promise shell call edges.
docs : headed sections.
Confidence : guess marks the heuristic outline families, and every record from those files carries confidence guess ; structural means a dedicated lexer or deterministic document rules.
Full language table README: Language tiers

Examples Examples
41 runs of dctx 1.3.1 on one small project, recorded when this site was built: the exact stdout and stderr, the exit code, the bytes and the estimated tokens ( ceil(2 × bytes / 7) ). Each run starts from an empty home, config and cache (DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, COLUMNS=100), in a copy of the sample named kiosk . Wall time is not recorded.
The 13 files of the sample, and what dctx pack . did with each (derived from the captured runs). tools/website/sample File Bytes In pack .env 29 listed-not-read .gitignore 8 packed Cargo.toml 185 packed README.md 473 packed assets/logo.png 69 binary config.toml 78 packed src/main.rs 331 packed src/store.rs 698 packed src/util.rs 404 packed target/debug/kiosk.d 42 ignored tools/report.py 484 packed web/app.ts 596 packed web/format.ts 350 packed Only three values are not stable between runs and are replaced with … , each where it occurs: the commit hash in --version , the MOD: times of --tree-stamps=on and age_s of --meta . The help pages are on /cli/ , the template builds on /templates/ . The same commands run live in the playground .
Pack (6) Map, text (9) Map, JSON (4) Graph export (2) MCP (1) Errors and exit codes (3)

( "{}" , util:: greet (&name)); let order = store:: Order { id: 1 , item: "coffee" . to_string (), qty: 2 }; store:: save (&order). expect ( "save order" ); } </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F007" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F008" PATH = "src/store.rs" LINES = "25" > use std::io; /// One order as the kiosk records it. pub struct Order { pub id: u32 , pub item: String , pub qty: u32 , } /// Write the order to orders/<id>.tsv. pub fn save (order: & Order ) -> io:: Result <()> { std::fs:: create_dir_all ( "orders" )?; std::fs:: write ( format! ( "orders/{}.tsv" , order.id), encode (order)) } /// One tab-separated line with a checksum of the item name. fn encode (order: & Order ) -> String { format! ( "{}\t{}\t{}\t{:08x}\n" , order.id, order.item, order.qty, checksum (&order.item)) } /// FNV-1a over the bytes of the text. fn checksum (text: & str ) -> u32 { text. bytes (). fold ( 0x811c9dc5 , |hash, byte| (hash ^ u32 :: from (byte)). wrapping_mul ( 0x0100_0193 )) } </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F008" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F009" PATH = "src/util.rs" LINES = "14" > /// The greeting shown on the kiosk screen. pub fn greet (name: & str ) -> String { format! ( "Hello, {}!" , title_case (name)) } /// Upper-case the first letter of a name, leave the rest as typed. pub fn title_case (name: & str ) -> String { let mut chars = name. chars (); match chars. next () { Some (first) => first. to_uppercase (). chain (chars). collect (), None => String :: new (), } } </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F009" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F014" PATH = "tools/report.py" LINES = "19" > """Sum the quantities of every saved order: python3 tools/report.py orders/""" import sys from pathlib import Path def read_orders (folder): for path in sorted ( Path (folder). glob ( "*.tsv" )): order_id, item, qty, _checksum = path. read_text (). rstrip ( "\n" ). split ( "\t" ) yield order_id, item, int (qty) def main (folder= "orders" ): total = sum (qty for _, _, qty in read_orders (folder)) print ( f"{total} items" ) if __name__ == "__main__" : main (*sys.argv[ 1 :]) </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F014" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F016" PATH = "web/app.ts" LINES = "20" > import { formatName, formatPrice } from "./format" ; interface Line { item: string ; cents: number ; qty: number ; } /** The greeting banner of the kiosk web screen. */ export function renderGreeting (name: string ): string { return `Hello, ${formatName(name)}!` ; } /** One receipt line per order line, then the total. */ export function renderReceipt (lines: Line []): string [] { const rows = lines. map ((l) => `${l.qty} x ${l.item} ${formatPrice(l.cents * l.qty)}` ); const total = lines. reduce ((sum, l) => sum + l.cents * l.qty, 0 ); return [...rows, `total ${formatPrice(total)}` ]; } </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F016" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F017" PATH = "web/format.ts" LINES = "10" > /** Price in cents to a display string, e.g. 250 -> "2.50 EUR". */ export function formatPrice (cents: number , currency = "EUR" ): string { return `${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)} ${currency}` ; } /** The customer's name as the screen shows it. */ export function formatName (name: string ): string { return name. trim () === "" ? ---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/templates/
title: Templates
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/templates/
---

Templates Templates
The dctx Template System (DTS) defines the text dctx pack prints. dctx 1.3.1 ships two built-in templates; both are shown here with their real output on the sample project.
Which template pack uses
dctx pack renders the default template; --tree-stamps=on selects the stamped one, the 1.0.0 text. legacy_output.rs
dctx template build <PATH> parses and validates a template file and prints its compiled plan; with --output PATH it writes the plan. dctx template list lists explicit compiled plans. The 1.1.0 pack command has no option that selects a compiled plan, so this page shows no third, custom template.
dctx template build $ dctx template build default.dctx_template template source_version = 1 plan_bytes = 2191 digest = 5fdd4d1fd3ef127241bc661a6057dad7cf812b0081eec51e58b2bf09f3b802fb views = 1 retention = stdout # exit 0 · 139 bytes · ~40 est. tokens $ dctx template build stamped.dctx_template template source_version = 1 plan_bytes = 2243 digest = e55e481eef9bec67a82232802068e28037389d0bdd1efbce5e3dcda73a327364 views = 1 retention = stdout # exit 0 · 139 bytes · ~40 est. tokens
What changes between them
This file defines how the LLM context is formatted. The only difference is the tree entry and its instruction line: the default leaves out MOD and SIZE , because a timestamp changes on a bare touch and a size on every edit, and either breaks the byte-stable prefix a prompt cache reuses. The tree of the sample, word by word ( default to stamped ; the MOD digits are replaced with … since they are file times):
DIRECTORY_TREE: pack . -> pack . --tree-stamps=on [D] (ID:ROOT) (ID:ROOT, MOD:…)
[F] .env (ID:F001) (ID:F001, MOD:…, SIZE:29)
[F] .gitignore (ID:F002) (ID:F002, MOD:…, SIZE:8)
[F] Cargo.toml (ID:F003) (ID:F003, MOD:…, SIZE:185)
[F] README.md (ID:F004) (ID:F004, MOD:…, SIZE:473)
[F] config.toml (ID:F005) (ID:F005, MOD:…, SIZE:78)
[D] src (ID:D006) (ID:D006, MOD:…)
[F] src/main.rs (ID:F007) (ID:F007, MOD:…, SIZE:331)
[F] src/store.rs (ID:F008) (ID:F008, MOD:…, SIZE:698)
[F] src/util.rs (ID:F009) (ID:F009, MOD:…, SIZE:404)
[D] tools (ID:D010) (ID:D010, MOD:…)
[F] tools/report.py (ID:F011) (ID:F011, MOD:…, SIZE:484)
[D] web (ID:D012) (ID:D012, MOD:…)
[F] web/app.ts (ID:F013) (ID:F013, MOD:…, SIZE:596)
[F] web/format.ts (ID:F014) (ID:F014, MOD:…, SIZE:350)
default.dctx_template
crates/dctx-template/templates/default.dctx_template source Copy # ==============================================================================
# DCTX TEMPLATE DEFINITION V1
# ==============================================================================
# This file defines how the LLM context is formatted.
# It consists of three sections: [VARIABLES], [PARTIALS], and [LAYOUT].
#
# SYNTAX GUIDE:
# - {{VAR_NAME}} : Inserts a configuration variable defined in [VARIABLES].
# - {{{DATA_FIELD}}} : Inserts dynamic data from the project (e.g., file content).
#
# ==============================================================================
[VARIABLES]
# --- 1. Syntactic Markers (Granular Control) ---
# Defines the exact characters used to wrap tags.
# Allows handling XML, HTML, or Custom formats safely.
start_marker_open = "<"
start_marker_close = ">"
end_marker_open = "</"
end_marker_close = ">"
# --- 2. Semantic Marker Names ---
# Defines the keywords used inside the tags.
instr_marker = "INSTRUCTIONS"
tree_start_marker = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
tree_end_marker = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
file_start_marker = "FILE_CONTENT_START"
file_end_marker = "FILE_CONTENT_END"
# --- 3. Attribute Keys ---
# Used inside tags to denote properties.
attr_id = "ID"
attr_path = "PATH"
attr_size = "SIZE"
attr_lines = "LINES"
attr_mod = "MOD"
# --- 4. Branding & Header Config ---
folder_denotation_marker = "DIRECTORY"
# --- 5. Instructions Block Text ---
# This text explains the format to the LLM. It references the variables above
# to ensure the instructions always match the actual format used.
# Use '\n' for new lines.
instructions_text = "1. Manifest: The {{start_marker_open}} {{tree_start_marker}} {{start_marker_close}} section lists all files. \n - Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH ( {{attr_id}} :UNIQUE_ID) \n - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file. \n 2. Content Access: To read a specific file: \n - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree. \n - Search for the marker: {{start_marker_open}} {{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}} =" UNIQUE_ID " {{start_marker_close}} \n - The content is between this marker and {{end_marker_open}} {{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}} =" UNIQUE_ID " {{end_marker_close}} "
# ==============================================================================
# [PARTIALS]
# Defines the look of repeated elements (Tree items and Files).
# ==============================================================================
# --- Tree Entry Partial ---
# Context: 'node' object
# Available Data: {{{node.type_char}}}, {{{node.path}}}, {{{node.id}}}, {{{node.mod}}}, {{{node.size}}}
# The default entry leaves {{{node.mod}}} and {{{node.size_part}}} out: a timestamp or a size changes on an edit or a touch
# and would break the byte-stable prefix of the page. Custom templates may still use {{attr_mod}}, {{{node.mod}}},
# {{{node.size}}} and {{{node.size_part}}}; `--tree-stamps=on` selects the stamped built-in (the 1.0.0 text).
[PARTIAL:TREE_ENTRY]
{{{node.type_char}}} {{{node.path}}} ( {{attr_id}} : {{{node.id}}} )
# --- File Block Partial ---
# Context: 'file' object
# Available Data: {{{file.id}}}, {{{file.path}}}, {{{file.lines}}}, {{{file.size}}}, {{{file.content}}}
[PARTIAL:FILE_BLOCK]
{{start_marker_open}} {{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}} = " {{{file.id}}} " {{attr_path}} = " {{{file.path}}} " {{attr_lines}} = " {{{file.lines}}} " {{start_marker_close}}
{{{file.content}}}
{{end_marker_open}} {{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}} = " {{{file.id}}} " {{end_marker_close}}
# ==============================================================================
# [LAYOUT]
# The master structure of the final output file.
# Note: The Version Header (e.g. [DCTX_SNAPSHOT_V1]) is hardcoded in the binary
# and NOT included here.
# ==============================================================================
[LAYOUT]
[ {{folder_denotation_marker}} : {{{project}}} ]
{{start_marker_open}} {{instr_marker}} {{start_marker_close}}
{{instructions_text}}
{{end_marker_open}} {{instr_marker}} {{end_marker_close}}
{{start_marker_open}} {{tree_start_marker}} {{start_marker_close}}
{{{comp.tree}}}
{{end_marker_open}} {{tree_end_marker}} {{end_marker_close}}
{{{comp.files}}}

( "orders/{}.tsv" , order.id), encode (order)) } /// One tab-separated line with a checksum of the item name. fn encode (order: & Order ) -> String { format! ( "{}\t{}\t{}\t{:08x}\n" , order.id, order.item, order.qty, checksum (&order.item)) } /// FNV-1a over the bytes of the text. fn checksum (text: & str ) -> u32 { text. bytes (). fold ( 0x811c9dc5 , |hash, byte| (hash ^ u32 :: from (byte)). wrapping_mul ( 0x0100_0193 )) } </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F008" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F009" PATH = "src/util.rs" LINES = "14" > /// The greeting shown on the kiosk screen. pub fn greet (name: & str ) -> String { format! ( "Hello, {}!" , title_case (name)) } /// Upper-case the first letter of a name, leave the rest as typed. pub fn title_case (name: & str ) -> String { let mut chars = name. chars (); match chars. next () { Some (first) => first. to_uppercase (). chain (chars). collect (), None => String :: new (), } } </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F009" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F011" PATH = "tools/report.py" LINES = "19" > """Sum the quantities of every saved order: python3 tools/report.py orders/""" import sys from pathlib import Path def read_orders (folder): for path in sorted ( Path (folder). glob ( "*.tsv" )): order_id, item, qty, _checksum = path. read_text (). rstrip ( "\n" ). split ( "\t" ) yield order_id, item, int (qty) def main (folder= "orders" ): total = sum (qty for _, _, qty in read_orders (folder)) print ( f"{total} items" ) if __name__ == "__main__" : main (*sys.argv[ 1 :]) </FILE_CONTENT_END ID = "F011" > <FILE_CONTENT_START ID = "F013" PATH = "web/app.ts" LINES = "20" > import { formatName, formatPrice } from "./format" ; stamped.dctx_template
crates/dctx-template/templates/stamped.dctx_template source Copy # ==============================================================================
# DCTX TEMPLATE DEFINITION V1
# ==============================================================================
# This file defines how the LLM context is formatted.
# It consists of three sections: [VARIABLES], [PARTIALS], and [LAYOUT].
#
# SYNTAX GUIDE:
# - {{VAR_NAME}} : Inserts a configuration variable defined in [VARIABLES].
# - {{{DATA_FIELD}}} : Inserts dynamic data from the project (e.g., file content).
#
# ==============================================================================
[VARIABLES]
# --- 1. Syntactic Markers (Granular Control) ---
# Defines the exact characters used to wrap tags.
# Allows handling XML, HTML, or Custom formats safely.
start_marker_open = "<"
start_marker_close = ">"
end_marker_open = "</"
end_marker_close = ">"
# --- 2. Semantic Marker Names ---
# Defines the keywords used inside the tags.
instr_marker = "INSTRUCTIONS"
tree_start_marker = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
tree_end_marker = "DIRECTORY_TREE"
file_start_marker = "FILE_CONTENT_START"
file_end_marker = "FILE_CONTENT_END"
# --- 3. Attribute Keys ---
# Used inside tags to denote properties.
attr_id = "ID"
attr_path = "PATH"
attr_size = "SIZE"
attr_lines = "LINES"
attr_mod = "MOD"
# --- 4. Branding & Header Config ---
folder_denotation_marker = "DIRECTORY"
# --- 5. Instructions Block Text ---
# This text explains the format to the LLM. It references the variables above
# to ensure the instructions always match the actual format used.
# Use '\n' for new lines.
instructions_text = "1. Manifest: The {{start_marker_open}} {{tree_start_marker}} {{start_marker_close}} section lists all files. \n - Each entry: [TYPE] RELATIVE_PATH ( {{attr_id}} :UNIQUE_ID, {{attr_mod}} :TIMESTAMP) \n - TYPE is [D] for directory, [F] for file. \n 2. Content Access: To read a specific file: \n - Find its UNIQUE_ID from the directory tree. \n - Search for the marker: {{start_marker_open}} {{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}} =" UNIQUE_ID " {{start_marker_close}} \n - The content is between this marker and {{end_marker_open}} {{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}} =" UNIQUE_ID " {{end_marker_close}} "
# ==============================================================================
# [PARTIALS]
# Defines the look of repeated elements (Tree items and Files).
# ==============================================================================
# --- Tree Entry Partial ---
# Context: 'node' object
# Available Data: {{{node.type_char}}}, {{{node.path}}}, {{{node.id}}}, {{{node.mod}}}, {{{node.size}}}
[PARTIAL:TREE_ENTRY]
{{{node.type_char}}} {{{node.path}}} ( {{attr_id}} : {{{node.id}}} , {{attr_mod}} : {{{node.mod}}} {{{node.size_part}}} )
# --- File Block Partial ---
# Context: 'file' object
# Available Data: {{{file.id}}}, {{{file.path}}}, {{{file.lines}}}, {{{file.size}}}, {{{file.content}}}
[PARTIAL:FILE_BLOCK]
{{start_marker_open}} {{file_start_marker}} {{attr_id}} = " {{{file.id}}} " {{attr_path}} = " {{{file.path}}} " {{attr_lines}} = " {{{file.lines}}} " {{start_marker_close}}
{{{file.content}}}
{{end_marker_open}} {{file_end_marker}} {{attr_id}} = " {{{file.id}}} " {{end_marker_close}}
# ==============================================================================
# [LAYOUT]
# The master structure of the final output file.
# Note: The Version Header (e.g. [DCTX_SNAPSHOT_V1]) is hardcoded in the binary
# and NOT included here.
# ==============================================================================
[LAYOUT]
[ {{folder_denotation_marker}} : {{{project}}} ]
{{start_marker_open}} {{instr_marker}} {{start_marker_close}}
{{instructions_text}}
{{end_marker_open}} {{instr_marker}} {{end_marker_close}}
{{start_marker_open}} {{tree_start_marker}} {{start_marker_close}}
{{{comp.tree}}}
{{end_marker_open}} {{tree_end_marker}} {{end_marker_close}}
{{{comp.files}}}
Output: dctx pack . --tree-stamps=on kiosk $ dctx pack . --tree-stamps= on [DCTX_LLM_CONTEXT_SNAPSHOT_V1] [DIRECTORY:kiosk] <INSTRUCTIONS > 1. Syntax
From ADR-003 , sections 1, 3, 4 and 5. The contract of the source and the compiled plan is DTS v2 .
1. Decision: Explicit Marker Definition #
To ensure future compatibility with non-HTML-like syntax, the templating language separates "Opening" and "Closing" logic for tags into four distinct definitions:
* start_marker_open (Default: < )
* start_marker_close (Default: > )
* end_marker_open (Default: </ )
* end_marker_close (Default: > )
This allows users to redefine tags completely, e.g., to [SECTION] ... [/SECTION] or {{#SECTION}} ... {{/SECTION}} .
3. Decision: Two-Pass Rendering Engine #
The rendering engine operates in two distinct passes to separate Configuration from Data.
Pass 1 (Config Resolution): Occurs during the "Template Build" phase. Resolves all {{VAR}} placeholders within the [VARIABLES] section.
Pass 2 (Data Injection): Occurs during runtime. Injects {{{DATA}}} into the pre-compiled Partial structures ( [PARTIALS] section) and assembles the [LAYOUT] .
4. Template File Structure #
The file format uses a custom INI-like syntax with three specific sections:
1. [VARIABLES]: Key-Value pairs for static strings.
2. [PARTIALS]: Definitions for repeated elements ( TREE_ENTRY , FILE_BLOCK ).
3. [LAYOUT]: The global document structure.
5. Available Data Variables (Runtime) #
These variables are populated by the Rust core:
* {{{node.id}}} : Optimized incremental ID (e.g., 1, 2, 10).
* {{{node.path}}} : Relative path.
* {{{node.type_char}}} : [D] or [F] .
* {{{node.mod}}} : Unix timestamp in milliseconds. Available to custom templates. The built-in default template does not print it since 1.0.1, because a timestamp changes on a bare touch and breaks the byte-stable prefix of the page; --tree-stamps=on selects the built-in stamped template (the 1.0.0 text, MOD: and SIZE: on every tree line, MOD in the instructions). The default entry also leaves out {{{node.size_part}}} , since a size changes on every ordinary edit; {{{node.size}}} and {{{node.size_part}}} stay available to custom templates.
* {{{node.size}}} : File size in bytes.
* {{{file.lines}}} : Line count of the file.
* {{{file.content}}} : Actual file content.

Playground Playground
Run the real dctx 1.3.1 on a bundled sample or on text files you paste. Each run gets a fresh directory and an empty environment, and is limited to 3 s, 2 s of CPU and 256 MiB; nothing is stored. Commands are checked against the CLI's own options and never reach a shell.

Evidence Benchmarks
Compare dctx with grep plus file reads, then measure the whole agent session. Startup instructions, tool definitions and extra turns can outweigh smaller answers.
Grep plus file reads
Measured whole-session results, 11 November 2026. Full report and method
Measured on 11.11.2026. NOT STABLE : dctx remains an advanced tool.
On this corpus and model dctx did not save 25 % tokens. The pre-registered
success rule was not met : CLI median total tokens were -5.01 % versus grep.
The claim supported here is accuracy and bounded context , not token savings.
Method #
Corpus: a private 13-crate Rust workspace; it is not public.
Questions: 20, covering code location, call sites and multi-hop traces.
Model: claude-sonnet-5-5 via Claude CLI.
dctx: 1.3.0 ( 156e1bb ), not current HEAD.
Three repeats per arm. Only tool exposure differs; prompt, model and question
order are identical. Blind grading uses opaque ids without arm labels.
Arm
Tools and cache conditions
A
Read + Grep/Glob: grep plus file reads baseline
B
Read + Bash restricted to dctx * ; index warm before measurement
C
Read + dctx MCP only; fresh cache, with start-up and indexing measured
These are whole-session measurements, including conversation replay and provider
cache usage, rather than estimates of tool stdout. The warm index in B excludes
its preparation cost; C includes start-up and indexing. This difference limits
direct comparisons between the two dctx modalities.
Cost and turns #
Totals per arm cover all 20 questions; each cell is the median [min, max] of three runs.
Total tokens = uncached input (including cache creation) + cached input + output.
Each metric is summarized independently, so component medians need not sum to
the median total. Turns are CLI num_turns , an assistant-turn proxy, not exact
tool calls.
Metric
A: grep plus reads
B: dctx CLI
C: dctx MCP

14,157,974 [11,221,908, 15,613,375]

B versus A median total tokens: -5.01 % . C versus A: +6.8 % tokens
and +30 % wall time .
Accuracy: both metrics #
The official metric is strict citation recall: exact repo-relative path and line,
with a tolerance of +/-3 lines, against 574 required line references per run.
The diagnostic metric is file-level recall: the required file named in full
anywhere in the answer, against 106 file/question pairs per run.
Metric
A: grep plus reads
B: dctx CLI
C: dctx MCP
Official strict citation recall, median [min, max]
10.10 % [10.10, 20.73]
14.46 % [8.36, 22.65]
13.41 % [12.02, 66.72]
Diagnostic file-level recall, median
53.77 %
71.70 %
76.42 %
A grader audit found no grader defect. Low strict recall comes from answers
citing shorthand paths such as store.rs:313 , and from line-level granularity:
10 trace questions hold 82 % of required lines. File-level recall is a
diagnostic, not a replacement metric. No file-level spread is supplied.
Where savings would come from #
dctx on its own does not save tokens by default. Token savings come from
systems that use dctx: a harness or agent system built around its cache-hit
philosophy, reusing byte-identical, prefix-stable context across long sessions
over a large body of work. In that setting it behaves like any sufficiently
advanced caching mechanism, with one difference: you have complete control
over every byte of the context. The system must arrange that reuse; merely
exposing dctx tools does not do it. There is no measured, citable savings figure
for such a system yet. See the philosophy .
Verdict and limitations #
The pre-registered rule required B to save at least 25 % median total tokens
and match or exceed A's recall. NOT MET on tokens (-5.01 %) , even though
B's median official recall exceeded A's. On this corpus and model dctx did not
save 25 % tokens.
B and C named more of the required files than grep at about equal (B) or higher
(C) token cost. This supports an accuracy and bounded context claim, not a
whole-session token-savings claim. The bounded context behavior is described in
Choosing how to use dctx ; these results do not establish a
general accuracy advantage.
Limitations: one corpus, one model, three repeats, and no significance claim.
The corpus and raw answers are private and cannot be published; these aggregate
results cannot be independently reproduced from the public repository alone.
dctx 1.3.0 is not current HEAD. The guidance Under ~200 files, use grep stays.
The earlier measurement evidence preserves the historical
tool-output protocols separately from this whole-session study.
Secondary historical evidence
All other-tool tables below preserve the October research record. Their tokens are tool stdout estimates, not whole-session cost; scores measure gold facts in raw output without an agent model. The dctx team designed the 70-question protocol. The independent run selected repositories by seed and used language-server gold.

Independent benchmark, 31 October 2026
Seeded selection of 3 repos the tools never saw (zoxide, requests, gin), gold from language servers and repo history, published regardless of outcome. Tasks: dctx 22/28 points, 31/36 facts, 6.85 facts per 1k tokens (Trail-Code 19/28, graphify 14/28). Callers against LSP gold, first page: dctx P 0.730 / R 0.341, Trail-Code P 0.731 / R 0.313, graphify P 0.920 / R 0.264. Honest read: dctx leads on task answers and token efficiency; caller recall on unseen repos is far below the in-house corpus (0.851), so the caller floors above hold only for the curated corpora.
