Rendered text and page details not already verbatim in the document pack:

Changelog Changelog
Every release, including known issues we have measured and not yet fixed. Generated from CHANGELOG.md ; also an Atom feed .
Unreleased In development Added Repository-scale map-find latency fixtures ( --scale-files ) with settled mtimes, recorded shape, and informational Windows/Linux CI samples for 1,551 files. Opt-in DCTX_TIMINGS=1 emits map-find phase microseconds as stderr JSON, with phase medians in the Windows CI latency report. Publish the first whole-session grep-versus-dctx benchmark: CLI median tokens -5.01 %, below the 25 % savings rule; both recall metrics and spread reported in the study . dctx trace A B returns bounded shortest directed call/reference paths, and dctx impact SYMBOL returns direct sites plus transitive callers grouped by file. Both support JSON, explicit depth/record/byte bounds, --place , --also , outside-index notices, MCP tools and engine RPC. dctx agent-setup [--format claude|agents|plain] : short, deterministic rules for choosing dctx or grep and using dctx from coding agents. Windows CI reports warm per-call dctx map find p50/p95 latency over 50 separate process invocations on a fixed fixture, with raw samples uploaded as an artifact. The measurement is informational and does not fail CI. First result (release build, GitHub-hosted windows-2022, stable): p50 10.2 ms, p95 11.3 ms. Map and context pages report eligible definitions outside the index with a relative path and an --also hint. A bounded local-import fallback respects ignore, omit and sensitive-file rules and refuses symlinks. Repeatable --also DIR on map verbs, pack and context joins read-only roots with root-labeled IDs and a cache identity covering the complete root set. Fixed Windows generation opening reuses guarded traversal directories and enumeration metadata, avoiding repeated ancestor opens per file while retaining identity, permission and racy-window checks. Python, Go and npm bindings expose trace and impact with CLI byte parity, including bounded/no-path and empty-impact results. Windows outside-index notices and trace / impact now normalize native separators and verbatim drive prefixes, keeping relative paths and --also hints slash-separated. Map query bounds errors name the offending option, its value, the user-facing verb (including grep ) and its allowed range; usage errors still exit 2. Windows: a file briefly locked by another process (antivirus, indexer, editor) no longer fails the whole pack; dctx retries for up to ~0.3 s. Changed Measure shell versus MCP-default stdout sizes on 1,551 files; the study reports 260 calls, a negative default-size result, and exact shell bounds. MCP discovery uses compact descriptions and advertises text/limit defaults. Map, hubs, trace and impact have smaller default answer bounds; explicit limits still override them. A bounded pack tool returns task definitions, callers/imports and source in one call. Tool names and opt-in JSON remain compatible; byte budgets guard catalog and response size in tests. See the payload study . Node wrapper is published as @tejl/dctx on npm; the unscoped name dctx was refused by the registry. Clarify npm stability and binary verification, and guard every npm package manifest against install hooks. Release version checks now cover the bundled git plugin, its fixtures and their digests. Compare in the repository 1.3.1 2026-11-09 Changed The Node wrapper is published as @tejl/dctx , with platform packages @tejl/dctx-<platform> . The registry refused the unscoped name dctx ; use npx @tejl/dctx . Fixed Segment store: publishing a new generation no longer fails with InvalidRequest(generation) when garbage collection runs at the same time. Publication now excludes a collection's mark-through-unlink, so a collector can no longer hide the newest generation from a writer. 1.3.0 2026-11-09 Install from the GitHub release archives. The npm, crates.io and PyPI packages and the Go module are built and tested in CI, but registry publication is still pending; until it happens, the release archives are the install path. Added dctx rpc : a versioned, newline-delimited JSON engine protocol over stdin/stdout (protocol 1.0.0, schema in docs/protocol/ ). Every reply carries engine_version ; operation output is exactly the CLI stdout bytes. dctx context TARGET... : minimal ranked context for a file, symbol name or stable node id, with chunk ids, --budget , --json and --session ID --dedupe . pack --for TEXT --json now returns the same JSON context page. dctx doctor [--json] [--probe-project] : lists the dctx binaries visible from the current folder with path, ownership scope, version, build commit, SHA-256 and cache sizes. It changes nothing and uses no network. MCP --profile lean|three and --tools NAME,... select a smaller tool set with compact descriptions (lean start-up tool definitions: 6,278 -> 1,637 bytes). See docs/guides/MCP.md . Python, Node (npm) and Go client packages over dctx rpc , each with CLI byte-parity tests in CI. They are not published to a registry yet. Release supply chain: keyless cosign signatures, CycloneDX SBOMs, GitHub build provenance attestations, a reproducible Linux musl build check and offline (air-gap) bundles. See docs/VERIFYING.md . CI runs cargo audit . SECURITY.md and SUPPORT.md describe the security and support policy. Robustness tests and a fuzz smoke workflow in CI. dctx pack --for prints a warning on stderr when the text names no identifiers; the page is unchanged. dctx pack --clipboard supports xsel on Linux. Experimental tools/catalog-bench for huge-tree catalog measurements (not part of the CLI). Changed dctx pack prints its pack bytes=… files=… retention=… version=V1 status line on stderr. stdout is exactly the page and ends in a newline; pack --json stdout is exactly one JSON document. Scripts that read the status line from stdout must read stderr instead. Indexes live in an engine major.minor subdirectory of the cache parent ( DCTX_CACHE_DIR or the platform dctx/v2 root). 1.3 builds its own index on first use; patch releases share it, and older unscoped cache data is ignored, not deleted. Faster warm path: one fused inventory walk with directory-relative stats, rule files validated by stamps and cheaper decoding (measured checkout 288 -> 94 ms, 4k-file tree 88 -> 32 ms). Timestamp-only changes reuse the index generation. Each place keeps its own warm index; targeted queries no longer admit the whole place first; capacity errors name the exact limit and the flag that changes it. Pack output streams with bounded memory and spools large pages. Pack history uses compact manifest caches. Language extraction audit with new goldens; the default parser id is now dctx-structural/3 . dctx pack --for keeps bare short names such as main and run , and keeps the case of capitalized words. Exact-case names and non-test code rank first, so --for Session finds the Session types before test functions. dctx cache , dctx template , dctx context and a bare dctx follow the exit-code contract in docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md : 2 for usage errors, 3 for I/O errors (naming the path), each with a hint: line. RPC cache_status returns the same codes. dctx context with no TARGET exits 2. A bare dctx whose stdin or stdout is not a terminal prints short usage and exits 2 instead of starting the interactive menu. dctx pack --help prints only the pack usage and flags. dctx plugin … and dctx git text output is plain text. Refusals go to stderr as [no] Error: with a hint: line; a missing consent names dctx plugin enable <id> --approve . JSON output and exit codes are unchanged. dctx cache auto text shows a UTC time next to last_auto_clean_ms and next_due_ms ; JSON is unchanged. Docs and package READMEs no longer present npx dctx , npm install , cargo install dctx-cli , pip install dctx or go get as working install paths. The Python missing-engine message no longer suggests a PyPI install. Bundled SQLite is 3.54.1 (rusqlite 0.41). Removed dctx plugin run and dctx git JSON replies no longer repeat the facade_spawns and facade_git_children keys. The facade counters remain once in --json output and are gone from text output. The cwd-relative plugin root fallback used when HOME was unset (see Security). Fixed Pack headers show ID="UNIQUE_ID" with clean quotes in the file-access instructions, including stamped and tree-only output. This changes pack output bytes. Pack rendering preserves literal template syntax in file bodies and paths, including backslashes, for default, stamped and compiled templates. Variable substitution applies only to template structure; pack --for also preserves source CRLF bytes. The last </FILE_CONTENT_END …> marker of a pack page is no longer glued to the status line. dctx pack --for with no usable terms says so and suggests backticks, instead of reporting that no name matched the index. Its flag refusal now lists --json . dctx map call edges stay within the caller's language family: a Rust .all(..) no longer resolves to a Makefile target. A guessed method call such as iter.map(..) links to a project method only when the caller can see that method's type. Hubs, neighbors, path and pack --for lose these false edges. dctx plugin search and the other text-mode plugin commands no longer mix JSON fields or internal counters ( facade_git= spawns= git_children= ) into the output; dctx git status without consent no longer prints git: ConsentRequired . dctx pack --clipboard with no clipboard tool names the tools it tried and suggests --output FILE . A symlinked or non-regular .gitignore or .dctxignore inside the project is skipped with a warning instead of failing the command; rule-file errors no longer print the absolute project path. Cache policy saves no longer get stuck on a policy.v1.tmp left by a crash. dctx plugin and dctx git work when the plugin root sits below a symlinked directory (macOS /var and /tmp , a linked home) instead of failing with Interrupted ; a symlinked plugin root itself and symlinks inside it stay refused. Windows: dctx plugin enable , disable , install , remove and update say that the plugin store is read-only on Windows ( ReadOnlyStore ) instead of failing with Interrupted , and consent hints there no longer offer only a command that cannot work. dctx doctor shows each binary's build commit ( commit: in text, "commit" in JSON) and names an invalid argument. dctx --help lists map export ; the dctx map --help examples map a file that has symbols. The Python wrapper raises BinaryNotFoundError , not RuntimeError , when no home directory is available (Windows without USERPROFILE / LOCALAPPDATA ). Windows: durable file replacement, inode identity and racy-window directory stamps in map refresh. macOS: symlinked ancestors of the project, config and cache roots (such as /var and /tmp ) are resolved at the boundary while in-tree symlinks stay refused; file names that APFS refuses are handled. Other cross-platform test and code fixes. README CLI reference, map-mode guide, modalities, start, testing and exit-code docs match the current binary and CI: all commands, 50 languages, neighbors depth 1..4, exact --lines , the global ignore file path, and that .git/info/exclude and core.excludesFile are not read. tools/sync-version.sh also syncs the Python, Go and npm package versions and the release links in the docs and package READMEs. Security Bundled SQLite upgraded to 3.54.1 (rusqlite 0.41, libsqlite3-sys 0.39.1) for RUSTSEC-2026-0459. Hardening across the engine and CLI, documented in docs/SECURITY-MODEL.md . Pack and diff output entity-encode & , < , > , " and control or line-separator characters in file paths, so a file name cannot forge file boundary markers. Ordinary paths are unchanged and output stays byte-stable. dctx doctor no longer executes dctx binaries found in ./node_modules/.bin , $VIRTUAL_ENV or relative PATH entries, which an untrusted checkout can plant; they are listed with path and SHA-256. --probe-project opts in. MCP tool arguments are passed after -- and taken literally, so a flag-shaped id or query (for example --place ) cannot change the place outside the server root. MCP never forwards --place or --output . pack --output , map export --output and template build --output never follow a symlink or write into a non-regular target; pack and template write a fresh sibling file and rename it into place. Clipboard tools are looked up only in absolute PATH entries, so . or empty entries cannot run a repository's own xclip or wl-copy . The source reader checks an entry's type before opening it and never opens device nodes, FIFOs or sockets (Unix opens use O_NOCTTY ). StdFs metadata, listings and link reads no longer follow symlinked path components; Windows ancestor guards block directory replacement. The store adapter refuses symlinked, foreign-owned or group/other-writable store roots and creates store directories with mode 0700. The plugin root no longer falls back to a directory relative to the working directory when HOME is unset; plugin commands refuse unless HOME or DCTX_PLUGIN_ROOT is an absolute path. The Python wrapper loads its dctx_binary_<platform> engine package only from the install directory that holds dctx , never from the working directory or other sys.path entries. The Python, Node and Go package READMEs warn that operation arguments carry full CLI authority. The no-follow open flag used by map export --output , the map store and the desktop snapshot rules now comes from the platform instead of a hard-coded x86 value, so it also holds on Linux ARM64. The npm wrapper tarball built in CI no longer lists the unpublished @dctx/cli-* platform packages, so installing it never resolves those names from the public registry; error messages point to the release archive and DCTX_BIN . The website playground rate limit can no longer be bypassed with a forged X-Forwarded-For header. The website deploy builds without secrets and deploys only from main through a protected environment; the desktop release workflow is disabled until the desktop app ships, with pinned toolchains, a frozen lockfile and provenance attestations. 1.2.0 2026-11-07 Added Prebuilt release archives for Linux x64/ARM64 (static musl), macOS x64/ARM64 and Windows x64, with SHA256SUMS. Packaging support for npm ( npx dctx , platform packages under @dctx/cli-* ) and crates.io ( cargo install dctx-cli ); registry publication is coming soon. Install the prebuilt GitHub release archives now. Cross-platform CI: every push and pull request runs the full test suite on Linux, macOS (ARM64 and x64) and Windows, on stable Rust and the minimum supported version. See docs/TESTING.md . The website redeploys automatically from main . GitHub Sponsors: individuals can support dctx at <https://github.com/sponsors/Eris-Margeta>. Changed Minimum supported Rust version is now declared: 1.91. The source tree is formatted with cargo fmt ; no behaviour change. Removed The two internal pre-1.0 project rule files. Project ignore inputs are .gitignore and .dctxignore ; built-in and explicit/global omission rules remain. The implicit dctx PATH snapshot command and its top-level flags, including -d / --diff , -t / --tree and -r / --reset . Use dctx pack PATH . The TUI now uses explicit pack commands without the old registry, state or project exports. dctx cache gc --legacy and its export-selection flags. Cache collection uses the managed ledger. Legacy-named selection test paths; current pure selection and privacy coverage remains. Fixed Windows CLI test environments now map APPDATA to the fixture config directory and provide LOCALAPPDATA for cache/data; missing or empty Windows directory variables return clear errors. Rust parser subprocess startup failures now stop indexing with a clear error instead of silently degrading source spans. pack --for keeps each section in source order when its budget runs out and recognizes file targets such as src/lib.rs . serve (including serve --mcp ) uses the stdio MCP server in the current directory, including fixture folders; read routes to map read . Budget-cut reads move trailing closing delimiters and separators into the continuation, preserving every source line. The release recipe checks the current root CHANGELOG.md path. Compare in the repository 1.1.0 2026-11-06 Release 1.1.0 ( v1.1.0 ; release candidate v1.1.0-rc1 2026-11-04). It folds in the 1.0.1 line, which was never released on its own. Since rc1 (docs, CI, tooling and SPDX licence headers only; no change to dctx output) Docs : byte stability re-measured on 2026-11-06 — 33/33 text and 33/33 JSON map answers identical after unrelated edits and over five runs (see docs/research/stability-20261105/REPORT.md); SPEC and README status texts updated, historical 0/63 kept. Formal : the plugin TLC gate accepts the newer TLC wording 'Temporal property X was violated.' / 'Invariant X was violated.' (all 8 baselines, 59 mutants, 37 witnesses pass); host-specific tla2tools.jar paths removed; TLC trace files ignored. Self-hosted CI ( .github/workflows/ci.yml ): the job run step by step on a self-hosted Linux runner (16 cores) from a clean git archive of the commit; results and badge recorded in docs/ci/RESULTS.md — 2279 run, 2279 passed, 0 skipped. Third-party npm licence inventory : scripts/npm_licenses.py indexes every repository package-lock.json into THIRD_PARTY_NPM.md ; npm_licenses.py --check runs in CI and fails on a disallowed licence or a stale report. Added Perl ( .pl , .pm , .t , .psgi ): package A::B; and package A { .. } as type symbols holding every later sub (named A::B::name ) as fn symbols ( guess confidence, full tier). POD is masked like a comment; call edges come from name(..) , bareword calls with an argument and &name , never after -> , sub or a sigil. Fortran ( .f90 , .f95 , .f03 , .f08 , .f , .for ): module , derived type and named interface as type symbols; program , function and subroutine as fn symbols named module::name ( guess confidence, full tier). Keywords are case-insensitive, ! comments only, fixed-form column rules are not modelled; call edges skip intrinsic and control keywords that precede ( . Verilog/SystemVerilog ( .v , .vh , .sv , .svh ): module , macromodule , interface , package and class declarations as type outline symbols and function / task declarations as fn symbols ( guess confidence, full tier), with module-scope call edges and <module> <instance> ( instantiation links resolved through the call index. Prefix-stable pack output : tree lines carry the ID only, with no MOD: and no SIZE: , so a bare touch leaves the page byte-identical and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix for prompt caches. --tree-stamps=on|off (default off ) selects the built-in tree template; on reproduces the 1.0.0 bytes. The desktop tree-only export keeps its digest line last, behind a stable lead line. Stat stamps in the manifest : a stamp pass runs before the digest, with a racy-timestamp guard; a touch-only change is decided by content. A gate replays 200 random edits against a cold rebuild. Record and entry caps : checked during the scan and set by DCTX_MAX_RECORDS and DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES ; the cache is reclaimed on publish, evicts before refusing, and readers share one lock. Open-source maintenance model : MAINTENANCE.md , TRADEMARK.md , a DCO in CONTRIBUTING.md and FUNDING.yml ; the desktop app is open source too. Changed Id lookup uses a sorted hash index instead of a linear node scan. Large source files were split into submodules by pure moves (400-line rule): pack.rs , path.rs , reuse.rs , bound.rs , plugin.rs , yaml.rs and others. No behaviour change. The version is 1.1.0 for every crates/* and plugins/* package; the desktop app stays on 0.11.0. Fixed A closed stdout pipe ( dctx pack | head ) exits 0 without a panic. Compare in the repository 1.0.0 2026-10-31 The first v1 release, folded from the 0.26 development line. Every crates/* and plugins/* package, VERSION , project-meta.yaml and the README badge are at 1.0.0 ( tools/sync-version.sh --check keeps them and their Cargo.lock entries together). The desktop app keeps its own version line (0.11.0) and its own release workflow. Shipped surface Map verbs : dctx map map | find | neighbors | explain | read | skeleton | grep | hubs | path | export , with hard token budgets, stable ids, cursor paging and precision labels; call and import edges are lexical. dctx mcp : a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools. dctx pack : the whole project as one structured block to stdout, the clipboard or --output . dctx pack --for "<text>" --budget N : task context for an agent card: map find on the names the text mentions, then neighbors and read of the best hits, whole lines only, within N estimated tokens (ceil(2 × UTF-8 bytes / 7), default 3000). tools/cardgen/context.sh prepends it to a card; docs/guides/AGENTS-SNIPPET.md is the AGENTS.md section that tells agents to run it first; tools/cardgen/dogfood.py records before/after prompt tokens for the ten v1 cards. dctx languages : one registry with three tiers (full, outline, docs) that also renders the README table. Privacy deny : sensitive files (env files, keys, credentials, ...), .git at any depth and symlinks are never read or printed by pack , any map verb or mcp ; there is no override flag. Detection is by file name only. Determinism : two fresh indexes give byte-identical answers, and an unrelated edit changes only hubs ; scripts/release-check.sh gates both, and counts network syscalls under strace -f (must be zero). dctx --version prints dctx 1.0.0 (<git sha>) ; the sha is embedded at build time, unknown without git. README benchmark section rendered from the committed run 7 JSON by scripts/render_readme.py ; just readme-check fails when the README differs. Out of scope for v1 Any network or cloud feature. macOS and Windows support claims (untested); Linux x86_64 is the only tested platform. Watch or incremental mode beyond re-indexing. Fortran and Verilog (both shipped in 1.1.0). Shell call edges. Embeddings and semantic search. LSP-grade type resolution. A stable plugin ABI and desktop API (unstable, not a v1 contract). Cross-repository queries. Publishing to crates.io or GitHub (a maintainer decision). Added Call and import edges in the map index: dctx map neighbors --edge calls|imports now answers who calls what, resolved by lexical scope, imports and module paths, with name / guess confidence; ambiguous references are dropped. New map verbs : skeleton <file> (declaration signatures, no bodies), grep <literal> (hits grouped by enclosing symbol), hubs (most-called symbols and per-directory counts), path <FROM> <TO> (shortest edge path) and export --format json|mermaid (the whole graph). neighbors --depth goes up to 4 (breadth-first, each node once). dctx mcp : a stdio MCP server exposing the map verbs as tools. dctx languages ( --json , --markdown ): every supported language with its tag, file names, tier (full: symbols and lexical call edges; outline: symbols only; docs: sections) and confidence, from one facade registry ( dctx::LANGUAGES ) that also feeds --version --verbose and the README table, which a test diffs. A CLI exit-code contract ( docs/CLI-EXIT-CODES.md ) for map , pack , mcp , languages and unknown commands: 0 ok, 1 no result (an id not in the index, a binary file target, nothing to pack), 2 usage, 3 index error. Every failure prints a hint: line. Previously every failure exited 1. A non-UTF-8 argument is now a usage error instead of a panic, an unknown flag is named as unknown, and dctx map <verb> --help prints a page with an Example: line for each map verb. Outline symbols ( guess confidence) for 25 more formats : Scala, Dart, Zig, Solidity, Gleam, Groovy; Elixir, Lua, OCaml, R, Julia, Haskell; Terraform/HCL, SQL, shell, Makefile, Dockerfile, protobuf, Pascal, GraphQL; and headed sections for .txt , .rst , .adoc , .org and .tex documents. A three-way benchmark against graphify and Trail-Code ( docs/BENCHMARK-20261030.md ) and the gap matrix behind it ( docs/GAP-MATRIX-20261030.md ). dctx Desktop is free, forever for individuals, teams and companies ( announcement ). The dctx Context Management Specification ( docs/SPEC.md ): prompt-processing efficiency as the core belief, the ten RAG defect classes and how dctx rules them out, the seven-layer organization policy, prefix-stable tiers and delta answers, the persistent index, the plugin boundary and the roadmap. An isolated, reproducible benchmark against Trail-Code ( docs/research/trail-code-2026-10/ ): methodology, raw data, scripts and numbered findings. Map mode ( dctx map ): map , find , neighbors , explain and read with hard token budgets (up to 2,000 per answer), cursor paging, stable ids, explicit moved / gone / ambiguous outcomes and precision labels on every answer. First-party structural extractors for JavaScript, TypeScript/TSX, Python, Go, Java, C/C++, C#, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, Swift, Markdown and JSON/TOML/YAML; Rust through syn . A verified map generation reused across CLI invocations. Plugin host : capability grants, consent, receipts, liveness by progress, signed distribution verified with Ed25519, and Linux confinement; the bundled Git plugin ( .gitignore protection and consented staging). Cache lifecycle : time-based expiry, a system size cap and a bounded automatic cleaner ( dctx cache status | gc | purge | config | auto ). dctx pack : an explicit pack to stdout, the clipboard or --output , without leaving files in the project. The template system's v2 compiler (a sealed plan IR) and organization ceilings. crates/dctx : one library facade for the CLI, the desktop app and future bindings. A new website with changelog and news, and the dctx film ( presentation/video/ ). Changed Byte-stable map answers : the text header is # <place> <verb> and JSON no longer carries snapshot , generation or freshness.age_s , so answers stay identical across unrelated edits (prompt-cache friendly). --meta restores the old fields. dctx pack never prints env-shaped files ( .env , .env.* , *.env , .envrc ); they stay in the tree by name with their content omitted. Strict sensitive-file deny for every command : besides env files, *.pem , *.key , *.p12 , *.pfx , *.jks , *.keystore , SSH private keys ( id_rsa , id_ed25519 , ...), credentials , credentials.json , secrets.yaml (and other data extensions), .npmrc , .netrc , .pypirc , .pgpass , .htpasswd and .git-credentials are never read or printed by pack , any dctx map verb (by id or raw path, with or without --in ) or dctx mcp . There is no override flag (see ADR-014). .git is closed for good : a .git segment at any depth is never listed or read by the map verbs and never read by pack , even when .gitignore or .dctxignore says !.git/ . No symlink escapes : FsSource opens files with O_NOFOLLOW , requires a regular file handle, and refuses symlinked directories, so a symlink swapped in after the stat cannot leak bytes from outside the root. DCTX_INDEX_IGNORED=1 (ignore files are not applied) is now documented in ADR-014; the sensitive-file deny, the .git guard and the symlink rules still apply when it is set. Total-source ceiling raised from 64 MiB to 1 GiB ; DCTX_MAX_SOURCE_BYTES overrides it. The core never reads .git/ , never spawns git and never uses VCS object ids; content identity is dctx's own SHA-256 ( crates/dctx-hash ). Repository ignore rules are applied before any read on the map path, and --lines A-B returns exact line ranges. Everything in the repository is licensed under Apache-2.0. Fixed Node spans resolve from one newline index per file instead of rescanning the source for every symbol (cold find on a 3,000-file repository: 141 s -> about 6 s). Queries share one generation instead of cloning it (peak memory down by about 30 % on the same repository). One hostile file no longer fails every map verb for the whole repository: a Rust file that is not UTF-8 is indexed as a module with no symbols (like every other language), and a file name the confined path cannot carry (a backslash) is skipped and marks the snapshot partial , as pack already did. Known issues Measured in the benchmarks and scheduled in the specification's roadmap: No incremental indexing: the first query after an edit re-indexes, and each edit adds a full generation to the cache. Outline-tier formats carry symbols and contains edges only; heuristic families are labelled guess . dctx languages lists the tier and confidence of every format. The 70-question task protocol (run 7: 140/140) was designed by the dctx team; an independently selected protocol (v1 card 6) is pending. Compare in the repository 0.25.0 2026-05-29 The last release of the first Rust generation, with zero third-party dependencies in the core and the CLI. Added Snapshot, diff and tree modes; clipboard output; an interactive TUI. Filters by extension, size, content and visibility; binary detection. Ahead-of-time compiled output templates. The privacy guarantee: ignored files are never read, not even in debug mode; omit rules list a file without reading its content. The desktop app (Tauri) on the shared core. Compare in the repository 0.11.0 2026-01-26 Added A redesigned desktop interface with light and dark modes. A sequential, fail-fast CI pipeline. Compare in the repository 0.10.0 2026-01-25 Added Advanced CLI filters and their documentation. Compare in the repository 0.1.0 2026-01-08 Added The Rust rewrite of dircontxt begins. Compare in the repository dircontxt 1.0.0 2025-11-15 The original tool, written in pure C ( legacy-c/ ). Added One LLM-ready .llmcontext.txt snapshot with a manifest and unique ids for every file and directory, plus a binary state file. Automatic versioning with diffs that carry only the changed files. A three-tier ignore system (built-in defaults, a global ignore file and a per-project .dircontxtignore ) and a global configuration file.

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/dctx-1-1/
title: dctx 1.1: three more languages, a prefix-stable pack, and a measured lead.
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/dctx-1-1/
---

Release
dctx 1.1: three more languages, a prefix-stable pack, and a measured lead. Perl, Fortran and Verilog join map mode; dctx pack drops timestamps so prompt caches hit; the three-way benchmark and the byte-stability measurement are public.
4 November 2026 The dctx project
dctx 1.3.1 was released on 4 November 2026. It folds in the 1.0.1 line and follows the first v1 release of 31 October.
What is new
Perl, Fortran and Verilog/SystemVerilog join the full tier, with symbols and lexical call edges labelled guess . dctx now covers 50 language families: 36 full, 8 outline and 6 documentation formats.
A prefix-stable dctx pack . Tree lines carry the file id only, with no modification time and no size, so a bare touch leaves the page byte-identical and an edit keeps everything before the edited file as a shared prefix. --tree-stamps=on brings back the 1.0.0 lines.
Faster id lookup , record and entry caps checked during the scan, and a closed stdout pipe that exits cleanly.
Historical output-only measurements
These other-tool results are retained as release history. Tokens here estimate tool stdout, not whole-session cost. The current baseline is grep plus file reads ; choose a mode and count startup context and all model turns.
On our own 70-question protocol, run on 31 October against Trail-Code 0.28.0 and graphify 0.9.97 in code-only mode, dctx scored 140 of 140 points with 29,340 estimated tokens; Trail-Code scored 122 with 88,923 and graphify 96 with 197,203. Cold indexing of the six corpora took dctx 0.13–1.20 s.
That protocol was designed by the dctx team and can favour dctx. An independently selected protocol is pending, and we will publish its result whatever it shows.
On 6 November, 33 of 33 text answers and 33 of 33 JSON answers stayed byte-identical after unrelated edits across three pinned corpora. Three weeks earlier, answer headers that changed after unrelated edits were one of the findings that our first benchmark held against us.
Benchmark write-up · Stability report · Full changelog
All news

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/desktop-free-forever/
title: dctx Desktop is now free. Forever.
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/desktop-free-forever/
---

Announcement
dctx Desktop is now free. Forever. For individuals, teams and companies. No trial, no seat count, no expiry.
21 October 2026 The dctx project
Starting today, the dctx desktop app is free for everyone who uses it: a single developer, a ten-person studio or an engineering organisation of thousands. It stays that way.
Why we are doing this
dctx exists because of one belief: prompt-processing efficiency. Every token in front of a model is paid for three times, in prefill, in cache misses and in attention. dctx supplies bounded, byte-stable context; it does not save tokens by default. Savings belong to a harness or agent system that reuses byte-identical, prefix-stable context across long sessions over a large body of work, with control over every byte. No measured savings figure exists for such a system yet.
The desktop app is how people who do not live in a terminal reach that engine: designers, analysts, product managers and engineers who simply prefer a window. Charging for it put a toll at the front door of the very habit we want to spread. So we are removing the toll.
Efficient context should be the default for everyone who works with a model, not a premium feature.
What you get
The same engine as the command line and the library: one core, the same privacy guarantee, the same output.
Drag-and-drop or native folder selection, and snapshots generated without blocking the interface.
Your global dctx settings and ignore rules, applied exactly as on the command line.
Everything runs on your machine. No account, no telemetry, no network.
The source is in the open repository under Apache-2.0, next to the CLI and the core. The desktop app is a preview on its own version line (0.11), source only: there is no download yet, so build it from the repository.
What does not change
dctx remains open source. The repository is ongoing work, and we publish what we measure, including where we still have work to do, as in our first public benchmark .
Organisations that depend on dctx can sign a maintenance agreement for security response times, long-term support and priority work. Paying never changes the license, and it funds the work that keeps the desktop app free.
Already bought a license? Thank you. You helped build what everyone now gets for free.
All news

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/specification-and-benchmark/
title: Our specification, and a benchmark that does not flatter us.
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/news/specification-and-benchmark/
---

Engineering
Our specification, and a benchmark that does not flatter us. The dctx Context Management Specification, and an isolated comparison with Trail-Code: wins, losses and what comes next.
21 October 2026 The dctx project
Historical post. These results describe dctx as of October 2026, before call edges and byte-stable answers. For current measurements, read dctx 1.1 .
An engineering organisation should be able to check every claim a tool makes. So we wrote down exactly what dctx is meant to be, and then measured where it stands today.
The specification
The dctx Context Management Specification turns our core belief, prompt-processing efficiency, into five testable constraints: every answer is bounded, deterministic, prefix-stable, non-redundant and honest about its precision and freshness. It names ten ways chunk retrieval fails and the mechanism that rules out each one, defines a seven-layer organisation policy in which every layer can only narrow the one above it, and lays out the roadmap with an acceptance gate for every step. Each item is marked as available, under contract or a target.
The benchmark
This is a secondary historical comparison of tool outputs, not whole-session agent cost. The current baseline is grep plus file reads .
We ran dctx and Trail-Code side by side on a dedicated machine: seven pinned code bases in Rust, Go, Python and TypeScript, no network during the runs, every command pinned to the same CPUs, and an adversarial corpus with planted secrets. The full report, raw data and scripts are public so anyone can rerun it.
Where dctx led
Cold indexing on every code base: 0.09–6.05 s against 2.4–95 s, with 1.6–27× less memory.
Footprint: one 9.2 MB binary against 405.6 MB of Node.js packages.
Bounds: map answers never exceeded their token budget.
Network: dctx opened no sockets and wrote nothing into the repositories.
Where Trail-Code led
Call graphs: dctx's map command did not yet expose call or import edges.
Answers to agent questions: 122 of 140 points against 69 of 140, with fewer tokens.
Stability under edits: Trail-Code kept most answers byte-identical after an unrelated change; dctx did not, which costs prompt-cache hits.
Incremental refresh after an edit.
What happens next
The findings are now the first items on our roadmap: call and import edges with honest confidence labels, a persistent incremental index, answer headers that stay stable across unrelated edits, a bounded repository overview, a search verb, and safer defaults for secrets when packing a whole project. Each one ships only when it passes the gate the specification sets for it, and we will publish the next measurement the same way.
Read the specification · Read the benchmark report
All news

What an agreement covers #
Security fixes. Response targets are counted from the moment a report is confirmed:
Long-term support. The 1.x line receives backported fixes for 18 months after 2.0 is released.
Priority on bug reports. Reports from covered organisations are triaged first.
A say in the roadmap. Covered organisations can propose priorities in a regular review. The maintainer keeps the final decision.
Advance notice of breaking changes. You hear about a breaking change before it ships, with a migration note.
Invoice and written commitment. You receive invoices and a signed maintenance commitment for procurement and vendor review.
Security reports still go through SECURITY.md , whatever your tier.
Tiers #
Supporter sponsorship runs through GitHub Sponsors . Team and Partner agreements are arranged directly.
Pricing and contact #
Guarantees #
The core ( pack ) and every modality stay open.

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/how-it-works/
title: How dctx works
source: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/how-it-works/
---

Docs How dctx works
Five short animations. Each has a caption with its one point and a text version underneath it when motion is off.
Use the Motion toggle in the header to switch between them. Planned features are marked planned.
Two scopes, one binary Cost is calls times context Edit a file, keep the cache The giant folder The safe path
Two scopes, one binary The same engine can live in two places on one machine. Knowing which one you are calling avoids most version confusion. Pause animation: two scopes, one binary Replay animation: two scopes, one binary Same engine, different owner. The system dctx is yours; a project's dctx is pinned by that project. dctx doctor lists every dctx in reach; release archives are cosign-signed. What the animation shows, step by step: One machine. The system dctx on PATH (version 1.3.1) belongs to you and your agents; you decide when to upgrade it. A project vendors its own dctx inside node_modules or a virtualenv, pinned by its lockfile and upgraded only when the project bumps it. The Node wrapper is on npm as @tejl/dctx from 1.3.1; the pip package is built in CI, with registry publication pending. Both are the same engine at different versions. Interactive agents and MCP call the system binary; application code and CI call the project binary. A library never falls back to PATH silently. dctx doctor lists every dctx visible from the current folder with its version, build commit, scope and SHA-256. Verify prebuilt archives against SHA256SUMS and their cosign signatures. Cost is calls times context Whole-session cost depends on how many times the model reads the conversation, not only on how big one answer is. Pause animation: cost is calls times context Replay animation: cost is calls times context Calls cost more than output size. An illustration, not a measured result: every call re-reads the whole conversation so far. What the illustration shows (made-up units, not a benchmark): Each model call reads the whole conversation: the task and prompt, plus every earlier tool result. Agent A uses grep and file reads: eight calls with small results. The conversation grows a little with each call, and each call reads all of it again. Agent B uses dctx: two calls that return larger, bounded pages, then it is done. Adding up what every call re-reads (the shaded areas): 164 units for agent A, 29 for agent B. So the number of calls matters more than the size of one result. The reverse also holds: dctx used without a plan can add calls instead of removing them, so count the calls of your own sessions. Choosing how to use dctx explains how to count them. Edit a file, keep the cache Prompt caches reuse bytes up to the first change. A stable order without timestamps keeps that prefix long. Pause animation: edit a file, keep the cache Replay animation: edit a file, keep the cache Edit a file, keep the cache. Illustrative sizes. The pack keeps a stable order and carries no timestamps by default, so a prompt cache can reuse every byte before the edit. What the animation shows: Turn 1: the pack is sent as one strip of bytes, file after file in a fixed order; the model provider caches it. You edit one file near the end of that order. Turn 2: the same tree gives the same bytes up to that file, so only the edited file and what follows are new. The cache reuses the unchanged prefix, here about three quarters of the bytes. If the pack began with a timestamp, the first byte would change and nothing would be reused. dctx answers carry no timestamps, digests or ages by default; --meta adds them back. Ordering rarely changed files first (prefix tiers) is planned. The giant folder For a very large folder, the plan is to catalog names once and index only the parts a task needs. Pause animation: the giant folder Replay animation: the giant folder Index what the task touches, never copy the tree. The catalog and shards are the planned architecture. Today, point dctx at a sub-folder named in the task, not at the whole tree. What the animation shows (the planned architecture): A 200 GB folder: photos, datasets, archives and a folder of repositories. A catalog (planned) sweeps it once and records names and sizes only; no file contents are read. A task arrives: fix invoice rounding. Two shards match the task: repos/billing and repos/shared-ui . Only those two get symbol indexes; the rest of the tree is never indexed or copied. A bounded page, inside the budget and in a stable order, comes out of the two shards. What works today: start dctx on the sub-folder the task names (for example dctx mcp ~/data/repos/billing ), with ignore rules for the rest. The safe path The shortest way to find out whether dctx helps your work, without changing several things at once. Pause animation: the safe path Replay animation: the safe path Measure before you change anything. The safe path for a new user, with commands that exist in dctx 1.3.1. Receipts are planned. If you are new, follow the safe path: one project, the system binary, the lean MCP profile. Measure before you change anything. Step by step: A new user with one agent and one repository. Install the system binary: download the archive for your platform from GitHub Releases, check it with sha256sum -c SHA256SUMS --ignore-missing , then run dctx --version . Pick one project, not your home folder or a huge tree. The system binary serves it; nothing is installed per project. Connect the lean MCP profile: dctx mcp --profile lean /abs/path/to/app exposes two tools, find and read, with compact descriptions, so fewer tool definitions ride along in every turn. Make the first call, for example dctx pack . --for 'greet store' --budget 800 , and read its last line: # end body_tokens=223 budget=800 dropped=0 on the sample project. Measure: per task, count the calls, the start-up tokens and the total input, and compare with grep and file reads on the same task. Receipts that count this for you are planned. Only then change one thing at a time.
Next: Choosing how to use dctx · Examples · Benchmarks

## CLI reference and examples (captured from the binary)

---
url: https://www.dctx.internet.technology/cli/
title: CLI reference (captured help)
source: https://github.com/Eris-Margeta/dctx/blob/main/tools/website/data/demo.json
---

```text
$ dctx --help
Usage: dctx <COMMAND> [OPTIONS]
       dctx pack [PATH] [--output PATH] [--clipboard] [--json]
       dctx pack [PATH] --for <TEXT> [--budget TOKENS]
       dctx map <map|find|neighbors|explain|read|skeleton|grep|hubs|path|export> [--json]
       dctx context TARGET [--place PATH] [--budget N] [--json] [--session ID --dedupe]
       dctx rpc
       dctx mcp [PATH]
       dctx serve [--mcp] [PATH]
       dctx trace <A> <B> [--max-depth N] [--max-paths N] [--max-bytes N] [--json]
       dctx impact <SYMBOL> [--max-depth N] [--max-sites N] [--max-bytes N] [--json]
       dctx read <TARGET> [OPTIONS]
       dctx languages [--json|--markdown]
       dctx doctor [--json]
       dctx agent-setup [--format claude|agents|plain]
       dctx cache status [--json] [--root PATH]
       dctx cache gc [--dry-run] [--root PATH] [--max-bytes N]
       dctx cache purge --root PATH [--dry-run] [--yes]
       dctx cache purge --all [--dry-run] [--yes]
       dctx cache config [auto on|off] [--max-bytes N] [--ttl-days N]
       dctx cache auto [--json]
       dctx template build <PATH> [--output PATH]
       dctx template list [--dir PATH]
       dctx plugin search|install|list|info|enable|disable|remove|update|verify
       dctx git <status|protect>

`dctx languages` lists every supported language with its tier: full (symbols and call edges), outline (symbols only) or docs (sections).
`dctx rpc` serves the versioned engine protocol for language packages (send hello first; docs/protocol/README.md).
`dctx mcp` serves the map verbs as MCP tools over stdio (JSON-RPC 2.0, one message per line) for Claude Code, Cursor and Codex.
`dctx serve` and `dctx serve --mcp` use that same server; `dctx read` uses `dctx map read`.
Explicit `dctx pack` writes stdout, the clipboard, or `--output`. It does not create a project text file.
`dctx pack --for <TEXT>` prints task context for an agent card instead: map find, neighbors and read of the names in TEXT, cut to `--budget` estimated tokens (default 3000).
`dctx plugin list` and `dctx --help` do not create a project `.dctx/` directory or start a plugin.
`dctx git` routes to the bundled dctx/git plugin. It is not a Git passthrough.
Cache purge requires `--root PATH` or `--all`, and `--yes` unless `--dry-run` is set.
`dctx cache config` shows the persisted policy. `auto on|off` enables auto-clean, `--max-bytes` tightens the system cap, and `--ttl-days` sets idle overlay and preview lifetime.
`dctx cache auto` prints the last auto-clean time, the bytes it reclaimed and the next due time.
`dctx doctor` lists visible binaries, ownership scopes, SHA-256 checksums and cache sizes without changing the cache or using the network.
`dctx agent-setup` prints concise rules to paste into CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md (default: agents).
pack, map, template, plugin and the TUI run one bounded auto-clean when it is due. They print nothing unless bytes were reclaimed.
`--no-auto-clean` and `DCTX_AUTO_CLEAN=0` disable that slice. `DCTX_CACHE_DIR` selects the cache parent; indexes live in its engine-major.minor subdirectory.

General Options:
  -h, --help            Show help
  -v, --version         Show version
  --verbose            With --version, also show executable path, scope and limits

Run `dctx pack --help` for pack options and filters.

Template Commands:
  template build <PATH>  Compile a template through the facade
  template list          List explicit compiled plans; no home-directory scan

Examples:
  dctx pack .                 Pack to stdout and write no project text file
  dctx pack . --output out.txt
  dctx languages --json
  dctx cache status --json
  dctx cache gc --dry-run
  dctx cache purge --root /path --dry-run
  dctx cache config auto off --max-bytes 1000000 --ttl-days 7
  dctx cache auto
  dctx template build policy.dctx_template

Feature and precision limits:
facade_version: 1.3.1
profile: enhanced
wire_version: 2
segment_version: 1
storage: buffered-segments
features: pack,map,templates,fs,segments,cache,syntax-rust
parsers: dctx-structural/3,dctx-lex-js:1,dctx-lex-md:1,dctx-lex-rust/syn-3.0.9
languages: rust,javascript,typescript,python,go,java,c,csharp,kotlin,ruby,php,swift,web,scala,dart,zig,solidity,gleam,fortran,perl,groovy,powershell,elixir,lua,ocaml,r,julia,haskell,erlang,verilog,hcl,sql,clojure,lisp,scheme,elisp,config,shell,make,docker,proto,pascal,graphql,nix,markdown,text,rst,asciidoc,org,tex
unsafe_boundary: syn-dependency
native_code: false
git: false
subprocess: none
precision: the structural extractor reports declarations, imports, headings and conservative calls.
It does not promise exact semantic calls, name or type resolution, or macro expansion.
A syntax-rust build adds syn for supported Rust syntax only, still without type checking.
token estimate: ceil(2 * UTF-8 bytes / 7) is an estimate, not a tokenizer guarantee.
cache cap: 2 GiB hard, 1.5 GiB soft watermark, 1.2 GiB eviction target.
cache ttl: idle overlays and previews 7 days, unpinned roots 30 days, staging 1 day.
auto-clean interval: 1 day.

         The whole graph as one deterministic document (default json: nodes and edges; mermaid: a flowchart of calls and imports). No TARGET, no token cap; --output writes a file.
  TARGET                  Required. map accepts a stable id or a place-relative file.
                          skeleton takes a file (or m:<path>) and prints its declaration signatures, no bodies,
                          in source order: id, kind, L<start>-<end>, signature.
                          A file path is read as m:<path>. Omitting TARGET does not scan.
  --json                  Facade JSON v2, including the precision label
  --also DIR              Add a read-only root (repeatable); paths and ids carry directory labels
  --place PATH            Place or worktree root (default: current directory)

  --profile               Stderr stage timings and the five slowest files. DCTX_PROFILE=1 is the same switch.

  DCTX_MAX_RECORDS        Env: files, symbols and edges one index may hold, 1..100000000 (default 1000000). A bigger place is refused while it is scanned.
  DCTX_MAX_ENTRIES        Env: files and directories one scan may visit, 1..100000000 (default 100000).
  DCTX_FRESHNESS          Env: strict_live hashes every file on a warm start; the default (stamp) trusts a file whose size, mtime and inode are unchanged and older than 2 s.
  --budget TOKENS         Output tokens, 1..2000 (explain max: 1000).
                          Read with no --budget uses the 2,000-token hard cap.
  --depth N               Map: 1..3; neighbors: 1..4. Explain and read take no depth.
  --limit N               Map, find and neighbors page size. Explain and read accept only 1.
  --offset N              Refused. Pass the previous page's next value to --cursor.
  --cursor TOKEN          Opaque continuation. A stale token is rejected.
  --kind fn,type,doc      Find kinds
```

```text
# kiosk

A tiny order kiosk. It is the example project that every command on the dctx website runs on.

## Run

    cargo run -- ada

prints `Hello, Ada!` and saves order 1 to `orders/1.tsv`.

## Orders

Each order is one tab-separated line: id, item, quantity and a checksum of the item name.
`python3 tools/report.py orders/` sums the quantities.

## Configuration

`config.toml` holds the currency and the screen title. Secrets live in `.env`, which is never committed.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F004">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F005" PATH="config.toml" LINES="7">
[screen]
title = "kiosk example"
currency = "EUR"

[orders]
folder = "orders"

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F005">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F007" PATH="src/main.rs" LINES="11">
//! kiosk: greet a customer, take one order, save it.
mod store;
mod util;

fn main() {
    let name = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "guest".to_string());
    println!("{}", util::greet(&name));
    let order = store::Order { id: 1, item: "coffee".to_string(), qty: 2 };
    store::save(&order).expect("save order");
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F007">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F008" PATH="src/store.rs" LINES="25">
use std::io;

/// One order as the kiosk records it.
pub struct Order {
    pub id: u32,
    pub item: String,
    pub qty: u32,
}

/// Write the order to orders/<id>.tsv.
pub fn save(order: &Order) -> io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all("orders")?;
    std::fs::write(format!("orders/{}.tsv", order.id), encode(order))
}

/// One tab-separated line with a checksum of the item name.
fn encode(order: &Order) -> String {
    format!("{}\t{}\t{}\t{:08x}\n", order.id, order.item, order.qty, checksum(&order.item))
}

/// FNV-1a over the bytes of the text.
fn checksum(text: &str) -> u32 {
    text.bytes().fold(0x811c9dc5, |hash, byte| (hash ^ u32::from(byte)).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193))
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F008">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F009" PATH="src/util.rs" LINES="14">
/// The greeting shown on the kiosk screen.
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}

/// Upper-case the first letter of a name, leave the rest as typed.
pub fn title_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = name.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().chain(chars).collect(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F009">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F011" PATH="tools/report.py" LINES="19">
"""Sum the quantities of every saved order: python3 tools/report.py orders/"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def read_orders(folder):
    for path in sorted(Path(folder).glob("*.tsv")):
        order_id, item, qty, _checksum = path.read_text().rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        yield order_id, item, int(qty)


def main(folder="orders"):
    total = sum(qty for _, _, qty in read_orders(folder))
    print(f"{total} items")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(*sys.argv[1:])

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F011">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F013" PATH="web/app.ts" LINES="20">
import { formatName, formatPrice } from "./format";

interface Line {
  item: string;
  cents: number;
  qty: number;
}

/** The greeting banner of the kiosk web screen. */
export function renderGreeting(name: string): string {
  return `Hello, ${formatName(name)}!`;
}

/** One receipt line per order line, then the total. */
export function renderReceipt(lines: Line[]): string[] {
  const rows = lines.map((l) => `${l.qty} x ${l.item}  ${formatPrice(l.cents * l.qty)}`);
  const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.cents * l.qty, 0);
  return [...rows, `total  ${formatPrice(total)}`];
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F013">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F014" PATH="web/format.ts" LINES="10">
/** Price in cents to a display string, e.g. 250 -> "2.50 EUR". */
export function formatPrice(cents: number, currency = "EUR"): string {
  return `${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)} ${currency}`;
}

/** The customer's name as the screen shows it. */
export function formatName(name: string): string {
  return name.trim() === "" ? "guest" : name.trim();
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F014">
```

```text
//! kiosk: greet a customer, take one order, save it.
mod store;
mod util;

fn main() {
    let name = std::env::args().nth(1).unwrap_or_else(|| "guest".to_string());
    println!("{}", util::greet(&name));
    let order = store::Order { id: 1, item: "coffee".to_string(), qty: 2 };
```

```text
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F002">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F003" PATH="src/store.rs" LINES="25">
use std::io;

/// One order as the kiosk records it.
pub struct Order {
    pub id: u32,
    pub item: String,
    pub qty: u32,
}

/// Write the order to orders/<id>.tsv.
pub fn save(order: &Order) -> io::Result<()> {
    std::fs::create_dir_all("orders")?;
    std::fs::write(format!("orders/{}.tsv", order.id), encode(order))
}

/// One tab-separated line with a checksum of the item name.
fn encode(order: &Order) -> String {
    format!("{}\t{}\t{}\t{:08x}\n", order.id, order.item, order.qty, checksum(&order.item))
}

/// FNV-1a over the bytes of the text.
fn checksum(text: &str) -> u32 {
    text.bytes().fold(0x811c9dc5, |hash, byte| (hash ^ u32::from(byte)).wrapping_mul(0x0100_0193))
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F003">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F004" PATH="src/util.rs" LINES="14">
/// The greeting shown on the kiosk screen.
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {
    format!("Hello, {}!", title_case(name))
}

/// Upper-case the first letter of a name, leave the rest as typed.
pub fn title_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = name.chars();
    match chars.next() {
        Some(first) => first.to_uppercase().chain(chars).collect(),
        None => String::new(),
    }
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F004">
```

```text
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F004" PATH="README.md" LINES="19">
# kiosk

A tiny order kiosk. It is the example project that every command on the dctx website runs on.

## Run

    cargo run -- ada

prints `Hello, Ada!` and saves order 1 to `orders/1.tsv`.

## Orders

Each order is one tab-separated line: id, item, quantity and a checksum of the item name.
`python3 tools/report.py orders/` sums the quantities.

## Configuration

`config.toml` holds the currency and the screen title. Secrets live in `.env`, which is never committed.

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F004">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F005" PATH="config.toml" LINES="7">
[screen]
title = "kiosk example"
currency = "EUR"

[orders]
folder = "orders"

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F005">

/// One order as the kiosk records it.
pub struct Order {
    pub id: u32,
    pub item: String,

}

/// Write the order to orders/<id>.tsv.

/// FNV-1a over the bytes of the text.

/// The greeting shown on the kiosk screen.
pub fn greet(name: &str) -> String {

}

/// Upper-case the first letter of a name, leave the rest as typed.
pub fn title_case(name: &str) -> String {
    let mut chars = name.chars();
    match chars.next() {

    }

<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F014" PATH="tools/report.py" LINES="19">
"""Sum the quantities of every saved order: python3 tools/report.py orders/"""
import sys
from pathlib import Path


def read_orders(folder):
    for path in sorted(Path(folder).glob("*.tsv")):
        order_id, item, qty, _checksum = path.read_text().rstrip("\n").split("\t")
        yield order_id, item, int(qty)


def main(folder="orders"):
    total = sum(qty for _, _, qty in read_orders(folder))
    print(f"{total} items")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main(*sys.argv[1:])

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F014">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F016" PATH="web/app.ts" LINES="20">
import { formatName, formatPrice } from "./format";

interface Line {
  item: string;
  cents: number;
  qty: number;
}

/** The greeting banner of the kiosk web screen. */
export function renderGreeting(name: string): string {
  return `Hello, ${formatName(name)}!`;
}

/** One receipt line per order line, then the total. */
export function renderReceipt(lines: Line[]): string[] {
  const rows = lines.map((l) => `${l.qty} x ${l.item}  ${formatPrice(l.cents * l.qty)}`);
  const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.cents * l.qty, 0);
  return [...rows, `total  ${formatPrice(total)}`];
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F016">
<FILE_CONTENT_START ID="F017" PATH="web/format.ts" LINES="10">
/** Price in cents to a display string, e.g. 250 -> "2.50 EUR". */
export function formatPrice(cents: number, currency = "EUR"): string {
  return `${(cents / 100).toFixed(2)} ${currency}`;
}

/** The customer's name as the screen shows it. */
export function formatName(name: string): string {
  return name.trim() === "" ? "guest" : name.trim();
}

</FILE_CONTENT_END ID="F017">
```
